articles.title: HME Launches Nitro Vision AI for Drive-Thru Operations
articles.titleKo: HME Launches Nitro Vision AI for Drive-Thru Operations
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . HME Hospitality & Specialty Communications (HSC), the leader in drive-thru communications and timing technology, announced the launch of Nitro Vision AI, a camera-based intelligence layer for the drive-thru. Nitro Vision AI helps restaurants move beyond timing alone to see what is happening across the lane, understand what matters, and get that understanding to the people who can act on it. The drive-thru has become a more dynamic operation. Mobile ordering, delivery, and multiple fulfillment paths create demand that shifts quickly across channels, which is why it’s more important than ever for operators to understand what’s happening across their operation. Total visibility is what gives them the context to improve every stage of the customer journey, and that is what Nitro Vision AI adds. Nitro Vision AI builds upon the ZOOM Nitro® Timer, using camera-first vision to recognize each vehicle by Nitro Vision AI also draws on the in-shift tools operators already use in ZOOM Nitro, including the bottleneck tracker, pre-menu threshold alerts, drive-off alerts, and POS integration that surfaces transaction details so crews can spot large orders and keep the line moving, and adds context from across the lane. Together with HME’s NEXEO | HDX™ platform, Nitro Vision AI creates a path for that information to reach crew members through the headsets they already wear, so crews can act while the car is still in the lane. Nitro Vision AI is privacy-conscious by design. It reads vehicle features without license plate recognition or biometric tracking, and it retains no personally identifiable information. By keeping the data accurate and the focus on the lane rather than the people in it, Nitro Vision AI is built to earn the trust of the teams who rely on it. “HME has spent decades helping operators measure the drive-thru. Nitro Vision AI moves us from measurement to intelligence. It brings lane measurement, communication, and now vision together in a way no one else in this space offers,” said Jason Bertellotti, President, HME Hospitality & Specialty Communications. Designed to grow with each restaurant, Nitro Vision AI is built to evolve as vision AI technology advances. To learn more or request a demonstration, visit qsr.hme.com/zoom/visionai. The post HME Launches Nitro Vision AI for Drive-Thru Operations appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: One Year In, Michael McDermott is Writing Chi-Chi’s Next Chapter
articles.titleKo: One Year In, Michael McDermott is Writing Chi-Chi’s Next Chapter
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Chi-Chi's was founded by Michael McDermott's father Marno McDermott. For Michael McDermott, the resurgence of Chi-Chi’s is personal. As the son of co-founder Marno McDermott, he grew up running around in the restaurants before going on to build concepts like Kona Grill. Quick history lesson: His father co-founded Chi-Chi’s alongside former Green Bay Packers player Max McGee in 1975. They took the brand public just four years later, and Chi-Chi’s grew to more than 200 locations across the country at its peak in the mid-1980s and 1990s. But the brand collapsed into bankruptcy in the early 2000s, and all locations closed by 2004 . Then, last year on October 6, Chi-Chi’s made its triumphant return with the opening of its first new location in Minneapolis suburb St. Louis Park, Minnesota. But reviving a legacy brand with this much history comes with a delicate balancing act. Longtime fans show up eager for the nostalgia of chips and salsa, Mexican pizza, and chimichangas, but sustainable growth requires winning over a new generation that never actually set foot in an OG location. Over the past year, McDermott’s commitment to listening to guests has shaped choices like introducing modernized menu items like birria and short rib tacos to rolling out a value-engineered lunch menu with smaller portions and accessible price points. Heading into its one-year mark, Chi-Chi’s expanded its offerings with a $10 to $15 lunch lineup and the return of fan favorites like the Twice Grilled BBQ Burrito, Seafood Nachos, and Margarita Chicken Tacos. The rollout showcases McDermott’s strategy of pairing scratch-made nostalgia with modern, accessible everyday value. To mark today’s milestone, they’re even rolling back prices for one day to 1976 levels, serving up $3.25 chimichangas and $1.25 house margaritas. And more growth is on the way. McDermott notes he’s in talks with developers along the East Coast and throughout the Midwest, though he’ll likely open a few more strategic corporate stores to prove out this next model of Chi-Chi’s before officially announcing any franchise deals. I sat down with McDermott to hear how he’s leading the company’s revival with a focus on honoring the legacy his father built while introducing the beloved brand to a new generation of guests. Why was now the right time for Chi-Chi’s to make its comeback? I believe in divine timing. I’ve been creating restaurant concepts for more than 25 years and bringing Chi-Chi’s back was never on my radar. A couple of years ago, I was considering transforming one of the concepts we owned because I felt it had run its course. I had a few ideas, but nothing seemed quite right. Then one morning during meditation, the thought came to me: bring Chi-Chi’s back. I ran the idea by a few people, and they thought it was a great one. The rest is history. What made the idea especially meaningful is that my connection to Chi-Chi’s is deeply personal. I was around the company when I was nine or ten years old, before my family moved to Arizona. While I don’t remember every detail, I certainly remember the chips and salsa. More importantly, I understand the responsibility that comes with continuing what my father started. Bringing Chi-Chi’s back felt like the right opportunity to honor my family while introducing the brand to a new generation. How are you balancing nostalgia with attracting new customers? Our intention was to bring Chi-Chi’s forward, not simply bring it back. We wanted longtime fans to recognize and reconnect with the brand they remember, while also creating a restaurant that feels relevant today. The restaurant incorporates familiar design elements such as hanging plants and Mexican tile, but the overall atmosphere reflects modern design and guest expectations. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . T’s Brunch Bar, owned by restaurateur and serial entrepreneur, Teneshia Murray, is set to open their fifth location in Powder Springs (located in West Cobb County, 30 miles from Downtown Atlanta) in November 2026. This location, which continues to be Murray’s love letter to Atlanta’s classic brunch dishes, will open at 5780 Ch James Pkwy, Ste 110, Powder Springs, GA 30127 (formerly occupied by 1738 Restaurant Bar & Lounge (an African & American Fusion Restaurant). Known for a “day party” atmosphere accompanied by live weekend DJ sets, the restaurant has built a strong social media following around photogenic, large-format menu items, such as Crab Fingers, Fried Green Tomatoes, Biscuits & Oxtail Gravy, Seafood Deviled Eggs, Salmon Croquettes, Oxtail Omelets, Chicken & Waffles, Cinnamon Roll Pancakes, and more. With location five, Murray continues to expand her restaurant footprint, which includes locations in Midtown , Cumberland Mall , Douglasville , and College Park . T’s Brunch Bar-Powder Springs will join Jim ‘N Nicks BBQ, Chili’s Bar & Grill, and LongHorn Steakhouse , which are all within ten-mile radius – along the nearby Jimmy Lee Smith Parkway . “With this new space bordering West Cobb County (Powder Springs) and Paulding County (Hiram), we look forward to serving residents in both municipalities who want a shorter drive for our tasty food and festive experience,” says owner, Teneshia Murray-Butler. For T’s Brunch Bar, Murray spent years visiting brunch restaurants around Atlanta, doing research and taking mental notes of her favorite dishes to develop the menu. Brandon Wilhelm brings more than 20 years of franchise development experience to the role. Hangry Joe’s, the fast-growing hot chicken franchise with more than 90 locations, today announced the appointment of Brandon Wilhelm as Chief Executive Officer, effective immediately. He will lead the company’s next phase of growth, with a focus on strengthening franchisee support, expanding the brand’s footprint as they are poised to open 20 new locations, and investing in the marketing and operational infrastructure behind Hangry Joe’s continued expansion. Brandon Wilhelm brings more than 20 years of franchise development experience to the role. He spent nearly two decades developing Subway franchise territory across the Midwest as a Development Agent, eventually overseeing operations strategy for more than 500 quick-service restaurant locations and mentoring more than 140 franchisees, before joining the Hangry Joe’s system as a multi-unit franchisee and President of Hangry Development Texas. He currently serves on Hangry Joe’s Franchising’s Board of Directors and most recently served as the company’s Acting Chief Marketing Officer. Wilhelm holds a BBA from Baylor University and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. “My number one focus as CEO is franchisee profitability — reducing COGS, driving sales, and improving our franchise partners’ bottom lines. If we give our franchisees the support, marketing, and systems they need to thrive, this brand will grow organically and quickly. I was actually considering stepping away from the restaurant business altogether, until I tried Hangry Joe’s and fell in love with the food. We have the best chicken in the industry, and I believe the whole country needs to try it.” said Brandon Wilhelm, CEO of Hangry Joe’s. Under Brandon Wilhelm’s leadership, Hangry Joe’s will focus on four priorities. First and foremost, strengthening the profitability of its current franchised locations, ensuring existing franchisees have the support and unit economics to thrive. Second, bolstering the brand’s marketing and advertising investment to drive traffic and brand awareness system wide. Third, improving operational efficiency across the business to support franchisees more effectively. And finally, pursuing smart, disciplined restaurant development by pairing the right franchise owner with the right location, every time. “Brandon has been a trusted partner to this brand for years, and we couldn’t be more confident handing him the keys to our next chapter. His operational experience and genuine commitment to our franchisees make him exactly the right leader to take Hangry Joe’s forward.” said Mike Kim, Co-Founder, Hangry Joe’s Franchising. The Canadian-born sports bar sees room for U.S. growth with an elevated food program, flexible real estate strategy, and focus on hospitality. Shark Club’s second U.S. restaurant could prove to be much more than another dot on the map. The Canadian-born sports bar opened in Northlake, Texas, in August, seven years after making its U.S. debut in nearby Plano. The brand is operated by Northland Properties Corporation, which also owns the NHL’s Dallas Stars. The newest restaurant sits inside the Children’s Health StarCenter Multisport complex, a Dallas Stars-affiliated facility serving youth sports and community programming. According to Northland Restaurant Group president and CEO Alan Howie, the location illustrates how Shark Club can find its place in a crowded sports bar field and how its parent company can put the right restaurant into the right piece of real estate. The Northlake opening also gives Shark Club another foundation for U.S. expansion. “We’ve now got two, so we’ve doubled. Maybe we’ll double again,” Howie says. In addition to the two Texas-based locations, Shark Club has four units in Canada and two in the U.K. Northland isn’t committing to a specific unit target for Shark Club. The family-held company has flexibility to pursue real estate as opportunities emerge instead of promising a predetermined number of openings each year. Growth is still a priority. Northland owns a collection of restaurant concepts that covers a wide spectrum of dining occasions. Its portfolio includes Moxies, steakhouse concept Chop, Shark Club, and other brands. The company also owns Denny’s in Canada. That variety gives Northland options when developers or landlords bring potential sites to the company. Instead of finding real estate for a single restaurant concept, Northland can study a property and determine which member of its portfolio has the best fit. Northlake offered an unusually natural match for Shark Club. The Dallas Stars and Northland share an ownership group, and the multisport complex attracts families, athletes, coaches, and fans for hockey, basketball, volleyball, pickleball, and other activities. Howie says Northland considered its portfolio before settling on Shark Club for the complex. “Maybe Denny’s wasn’t the right one for that one, maybe Moxie’s wasn’t the right one for that one, but Shark Club definitely is because this would be people going to play sports and watch their kids play sports and hockey and basketball, all those sorts of things, and the Shark Club environment is the right one for that,” he says. Shark Club occupies roughly 5,000 square feet in Northlake and features 37 televisions, along with a patio overlooking pickleball courts. Its menu includes shareable appetizers, burgers, handhelds, entrees, beverages, late-night specials, and happy hour offerings. Food is a major piece of Northland’s effort to distinguish Shark Club from the field. Howie describes the concept as a sports bar backed by a premium-casual food program and elevated service. The basic requirements for competing in the category are straightforward. Guests expect plenty of televisions, quality sound, and cold beer. Howie believes the restaurant experience provides the separation. Each Shark Club has its own chef in addition to a general manager, a structure Northland also uses at Moxies and Chop. “The things that differentiate us, I think, is the environment and the food,” Howie says. That positioning connects with Shark Club’s “For All Fankind” message. Sports may be the catalyst for many visits, but Northland wants the concept to appeal to people who aren’t arriving solely to watch a game. Manhattan’s Piccola Cucina Estiatorio and Piccola Cucina Osteria have been named among the United States’ premier dining destinations in the Tripadvisor Travelers’ Choice Awards Best of the Best, ranking #7 and #11 nationally. This exclusive honor places both establishments within the top 1% of more than 8 million global listings. Helmed by Chef Philip Guardione, the Piccola Cucina Group is a family of restaurants considered to be among the first to bring authentic Sicilian cuisine to Manhattan at a time when southern Italian fare was still emerging in the city’s culinary landscape. Today, the group welcomes diners from across the world, becoming both neighborhood staples as well as destinations for authentic, regionally-specific “ vero cibo siciliano ” for locals and visitors alike. Ranked #7 in the U.S., Piccola Cucina Estiatorio is nestled in the heart of Soho at 75 Thompson Street and beloved for its selection of fresh seafood and coastal Mediterranean dishes. Designed as a traditional Sicilian-style mercato inspired by Chef Guardione’s upbringing in Etna, diners can select their fish directly from the display, alongside classics like octopus caprese. Nearby at 196 Spring Street in Soho, Piccola Cucina Osteria, #11 in the U.S., is a celebration of Chef Guardione’s native Catania. Welcoming diners in a cozy, inviting space, its menu highlights housemade pasta, rustic preparations such as pane cunzato topped with primo sale cheese and anchovy; crowd-pleasing arancini catanese, and tableside tiramisu or cannoli for dessert. Piccola Cucina Group restaurants are renowned for their extensive wine program featuring an encyclopedic, 4,000-bottle wine cellar. The list spans more than 600 labels, with nearly 40% sourced from Sicily and a deep emphasis on Mount Etna, one of the most dynamic and celebrated wine regions in the world today. Every year, TripAdvisor awards travelers’ favorite destinations, hotels, restaurants, and things to do around the world, based on reviews and ratings collected over 12 months. The Travelers’ Choice Awards Best of the Best winners are decided by real travelers from all over, sharing real opinions and stories. The 2026 winners are a celebration of all the places travelers discovered. Piccola Cucina currently has seven locations spanning New York City, Montana, and Ibiza. How Ya Doughn’ Pizza, South Florida’s fast-growing local pizza brand, today announced a multi-year partnership with the Florida Panthers, naming How Ya Doughn’ the team’s Official Pizza Partner. The agreement brings How Ya Doughn’s signature pies to Amerant Bank Arena and connects the brand with one of the NHL’s most passionate and fastest-growing fan bases. As part of the partnership, How Ya Doughn’ will have an in-arena concession presence at Panthers home games, branded integrations across the arena and Panthers digital channels, and joint marketing activations throughout the season. “As someone who grew up playing hockey it has been part of my life for nearly twenty-five years. I’m proud to partner with an organization that cares for the players and fans as much as we care for the pizza,” said Garett Goodman, Founder of How Ya Doughn’ Pizza. “This partnership lets us bring How Ya Dough’n to even more of our neighbors, right where they’re already celebrating.” “We’re proud to partner with local businesses that share our roots and passion for this community, and How Ya Dough’n is a perfect example of that,” said Panthers Vice President of Corporate Partnerships, Joshua Korlin. “We look forward to having their pizza available at select locations throughout Amerant Bank Arena this season.” The partnership kicks off this week with the 2026 season and will include: • In-arena availability of How Ya Doughn’ Pizza at plaza level section 118, upper level section 318, on the Suite Level and in The Panther Bar as well as at concession locations throughout Amerant Bank Arena • Branded signage and digital integrations across the arena and Panthers media channels • Co-branded promotions, activations and giveaways during select home games throughout the season. About How Ya Doughn’ Pizza Founded in Boca Raton in 2020 by Garett and Gabby Goodman, How Ya Dough’n is a viral sourdough-fueled, husband-and-wife-led pizza brand redefining the slice game. With Michelin-style precision, a signature extended fermentation process, and support from the Ferolito family, the brand has risen from backyard pizza drops to four South Florida storefronts, with Las Vegas marking its fifth location. A healthy alternative to traditional pizza, How Ya Dough’n is 100% seed oil-free, organic, and good for your gut health. For more information, visit howyadoughn.com. articles.title: Zaxbys Partners with Areas USA to Expand into Travel Plazas
articles.titleKo: Zaxbys Partners with Areas USA to Expand into Travel Plazas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Zaxbys, the rapidly growing Georgia-based QSR franchise known for its Chicken Fingerz, wings and 12 signature sauces, is entering the travel hospitality sector through a multi-unit agreement with Areas USA, the nation’s largest privately held travel hospitality company. The deal will develop five restaurants at Florida Turnpike service plazas, and the team recently opened the first unit on Sept. 29 at the Turkey Lake Service Plaza in Orlando. The restaurant situated at 263 Florida’s Turnpike will introduce millions of travelers each year to one of the nation’s fastest-growing chicken brands along a high-traffic Florida travel corridor. The deal marks a significant step in Zaxbys’ long-term growth strategy and is the brand’s largest non-traditional development agreement to date. As consumers increasingly seek recognizable restaurant brands wherever they travel, Zaxbys is expanding beyond traditional freestanding restaurants into heavily frequented destinations that offer greater convenience and introduce the brand to new audiences. Pairing Areas’ extensive travel hospitality expertise with Zaxbys’ growing brand presence and consumer appeal, the partnership creates a strong foundation for continued expansion in travel venues and other non-traditional environments. Areas will support Zaxbys’ broader strategy to pursue flexible formats and strategic real estate opportunities that encourage long-term growth. “Today’s guests expect convenience without compromising on quality, and this partnership allows us to meet them where they are,” said Russ Holland, Chief Development Officer at Zaxbys. “Working with Areas USA enables us to introduce the Zaxbys experience to millions of travelers each year while continuing to build on our non-traditional development strategy. We’re excited to expand into one of Florida’s most heavily traveled corridors alongside a partner that shares our commitment to delivering exceptional guest experiences.” The Areas agreement, part of Areas’ longstanding partnership with Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise to enhance the state’s service plazas, establishes a scalable model for future growth while reinforcing Zaxbys’ potential across broader non-traditional environments. Zaxbys is actively exploring opportunities within airports, colleges and universities, military installations and other high-traffic destinations. By combining flexible restaurant formats with strong operational support, Zaxbys is well positioned to work with leading non-traditional operators to expand its presence in new venues while strengthening brand awareness nationwide. “With its bold flavors and Southern hospitality, Zaxbys is a great fit for these plazas. We’re proud to be part of Florida, home to our U.S. headquarters, and to partner with Zaxbys and Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise on this expansion. We’ve invested in these plazas, and we’re excited to continue investing in their future. For us, hospitality is about making every stop a better experience, with welcoming spaces, great service and more choices for travelers,” said Richard Schneider, Chief Development Officer of Areas USA. Founded in 1990, Zaxbys has grown to more than 1,000 restaurants by delivering differentiated chicken offerings, bold flavors and Southern hospitality. Today, the brand continues to build momentum through strategic franchise expansion, menu innovation and flexible development models designed to meet guests wherever they live, work and travel. The brand’s commitment to quality and innovation has earned it numerous industry accolades, including recognition in QSR Magazine’s 2024 Top 50 Fast-Food Chains, Entrepreneur, Forbes, and Newsweek. With a strong leadership team and a focus on long-term, sustainable growth, Zaxbys continues to stay true to its mission of delivering mouthwatering food and memorable experiences to its loyal fanbase. articles.title: Indigo Road Hospitality Group to Bring O-Ku and Rooftop Italian Concept to The Doyle in Charlottesville, Virginia
articles.titleKo: Indigo Road Hospitality Group to Bring O-Ku and Rooftop Italian Concept to The Doyle in Charlottesville, Virginia
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Indigo Road Hospitality Group (IRHG) is delighted to announce it will bring its award-winning Japanese concept, O-Ku, to Charlottesville this winter. In addition to O-Ku, Ross Hotel Partners and Buckhead America, the new owners of The Doyle on West Main Street, selected IRHG to reimagine and operate the existing food and beverage offerings throughout The Doyle, including the bourbon bar, rooftop bar, and all-day coffee shop and café. “We are excited about the opportunity to join this rich and vibrant food scene through our partnership with Ross Hotel Partners and Buckhead America,” says Steve Palmer, Founder and Chief Vision Officer of IRHG. “We have always believed that hospitality is rooted in the people we serve and the community it creates. We look forward to contributing to Charlottesville in a small way through meals served at O-Ku along with our other food and beverage offerings at The Doyle.” O-Ku celebrates authentic Japanese cuisine with a regional approach through a chef-driven menu that focuses on unique ingredients and sophisticated presentations. From temaki, nigiri, and sashimi to hot plates and signature rolls, O-Ku will showcase the freshest fish from the world’s finest markets alongside sustainably sourced ingredients from local purveyors. An executive chef for the restaurant will be announced at a later date. “I’ve fallen in love with Charlottesville over the past three years while my daughter has been a student at UVA. This hotel has an incredible location and tremendous potential, and we aim to become part of the Hilton Tapestry collection by springtime,” says Butch Ross, Founder of Ross Hotel Partners. “We’ve brought in two best-in-class management teams—Dreamscape Hospitality for hotel and Indigo Road for food and beverage—to give this hotel a real soul and create concepts that feel worthy of Charlottesville. The Indigo Road knows high-end hospitality, and I’m excited for them to introduce their signature cuisine and warm, friendly service to Charlottesville locals, students, and visitors. IRHG is developing an Italian-inspired concept on the rooftop centered around the existing wood-fired pizza oven, which is anticipated to open in Spring 2027. IRHG also plans to enhance the all-day coffee bar and café with a fresh pastry program from Culinary Director of Pastry Anne White while expanding the offerings available at the bourbon bar. The hotel is newly managed by Dreamscape Hospitality. The design team for the property—including the hotel and its food and beverage concepts—is led by Jeannette Andamasaris of Studio FIGURE. articles.title: everbowl Marks 10 Years with Anniversary Bowl and $8 Deal
articles.titleKo: everbowl Marks 10 Years with Anniversary Bowl and $8 Deal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . everbowl, the elevated fast-casual superfood brand, reaches its 10th anniversary on Friday, October 16. The celebration thanks the customers and communities behind a decade of growth that took everbowl from its first San Diego location to more than 100 locations in 33 states and more than 5 million bowls sold. Founder Jeff Fenster came to the food industry from sales and startups. After becoming ADP’s top sales rep in the country, he launched a payroll company from his mother’s kitchen at 25 and later ran a digital marketing agency, now an everbowl investor. By 2020, everbowl operated 28 corporate stores, and a QVC partnership sold 70,000 boxes of DIY açai bowl kits in seven minutes, sold out 17 airings, and earned Product of the Year in 2021. That demand led everbowl to begin franchising. That growth was built by people who have been there from the start. For example, Hailey Coffman began as a store employee at an everbowl in San Diego, and now serves as Manager of Training & Special Operations at everbowl’s San Diego headquarters, helping train franchisees across the country. To mark the milestone, everbowl is introducing the limited-edition 10 Year Anniversary Bowl, available through October 11–25 at participating locations. The bowl features everbowl’s iconic açaí superfood base paired with its seasonal ube, topped with gluten-free granola, strawberries, bananas and blueberries, and finished with a drizzle of creamy peanut butter. On the anniversary itself, Friday, October 16, everbowl loyalty members can get a regular-size Anniversary Bowl for $8 all day, throwing it back to 2016 pricing when everbowl first opened its doors. With more than 100 additional locations in development, everbowl enters its second decade focused on making better-for-you food a daily habit for more communities. Customers can join the loyalty program and find a participating location at www.everbowl.com. The post everbowl Marks 10 Years with Anniversary Bowl and $8 Deal appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Playa Bowls Announces Partnership with Breast Cancer Research Foundation
articles.titleKo: Playa Bowls Announces Partnership with Breast Cancer Research Foundation
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Playa Bowls is rallying its shops and guests across the country around the superfruit behind its most recognizable bright pink menu items for a bigger purpose this Breast Cancer Awareness Month. From September 29 through November 2, Playa Bowls is partnering with the Breast Cancer Research Foundation (BCRF), donating a portion of its sales in support of the organization. Playa’s Pink Pitaya campaign supports BCRF’s work advancing breast cancer prevention, detection and treatment while also bringing attention to the role that better-for-you menu items play in supporting guests’ overall wellness. Beyond giving the campaign its vibrant pink hue, pitaya is a nutrient-rich superfruit that is high in essential vitamins and minerals, packed with antioxidants and highlighted as an anti-inflammatory booster. The campaign features three Playa favorites made with the brand’s signature Playa Pitaya base: the Electric Mermaid Bowl, Dragonberry Bowl and Pink Pitaya smoothie. Electric Mermaid Bowl: Naturally hydrating Playa Pitaya topped with blueberry flax granola, pineapple, fiber-rich mango and kiwi, coconut flakes and a drizzle of honey for a colorful, tropical combination that supports digestion. Dragonberry Bowl: Antioxidant- and Vitamin C-rich Playa Pitaya topped with blueberry flax granola, fresh strawberries, blueberries and a drizzle of honey, with prebiotics and fiber from pitaya to support a healthy gut. Pink Pitaya Smoothie: A smooth, vivid blend of Playa Pitaya and organic coconut milk that pairs antioxidant-rich, hydrating pitaya with electrolytes and healthy fats from coconut. Guests can support BCRF throughout the campaign by making a donation in shops, when ordering online, or through Playa Bowls’ dedicated BCRF fundraising page. The giveback efforts will then culminate on Pink Pitaya Giving Day on October 25, as Playa Bowls donates $2 from every pitaya bowl sold nationwide to the organization, giving guests another way to turn their favorite bowl into fuel for lifesaving breast cancer research. “Our vibrant pink Playa Pitaya is a natural connection during Breast Cancer Awareness Month and our mission to offer our guests a convenient way to incorporate more nutrient-rich, better-for-you food into their daily routines,” said Tim Hackbardt, chief marketing officer at Playa Bowls. “It is our goal to bring our Playa community together around them throughout October to help raise funds for BCRF and the lifesaving research it supports.” Founded by Evelyn H. Lauder in 1993, BCRF is one of the world’s leading breast cancer research organizations and the largest private funder of breast cancer research worldwide. The organization supports research spanning prevention, detection, treatment, metastatic disease and survivorship. To learn more about Playa Bowls, visit www.playabowls.com and follow along on Instagram , TikTok , and Facebook for the latest updates. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Johnsonville, the No. 1 national sausage brand, and Grillo’s Pickles, the pickle company known for changing the pickle game, are excited to announce a series of product collaborations in 2027, starting with bringing a bold new flavor to c-store roller grills with the launch of the Johnsonville Spicy Dill Pickle Flavored Ultimate Sausage, inspired by Grillo’s Pickles. The new item combines bright pickle flavor with savory caraway, garlic, and a kick of red pepper, tapping into one of the fastest-rising flavor trends on menus today and giving operators a fresh way to build roller grill traffic. The collaboration debuts at NACS Show 2026 in Las Vegas, where Johnsonville is featuring the Spicy Dill Pickle Flavored Ultimate Sausage at Booth C4717 in the Central Hall. Dill pickle has taken over the snack aisle and is even showing up in offerings like beverages and prepared foods as one of the most in-demand flavors in convenience stores today. “Dill continues its surge across Convenience in all categories, and pickle-forward profiles with a little heat are resonating especially well with younger consumers,” said Kim Main, Sr. Director, Channel Marketing at Johnsonville. “Partnering with Grillo’s – a name pickle lovers trust and admire – is a natural choice for Johnsonville to bring exciting innovation consumers are already looking for to the roller grill.” Crafted to deliver the tangy, dill-forward profile Grillo’s is known for in a roller grill format, the new sausage is pre-cooked and roller-grill-ready, giving operators the same reliable prep with a bold new flavor. It pairs easily with the toppings and condiments c-stores already stock, requiring no new equipment or menu overhaul. Grillo’s brings a loyal, outsized fan base to the partnership. “Pickles have always been a classic complement to brats and hot dogs, so we were excited to bring these flavors together in one offering,” said Mark Luker, Chief Commercial Officer at Grillo’s. “We’re proud to partner with Johnsonville and can’t wait for customers to give it a try!” According to Datassential, spicy dill pickle is up 55% on handheld menus, and dill pickle flavor has grown 18% over the past four years, positioning the collaboration to capture a fast-growing, high-frequency customer base. That momentum is especially strong with younger customers, with 60% of Gen Z c-store customers saying they like or love pickle flavors. The Johnsonville and Grillo’s partnership will continue to expand in 2027, with additional fresh, smoked, and snacking sausage offerings planned for nationwide rollout to grocery retailers. Additional details about the 2027 lineup and availability will be shared closer to launch. articles.title: Uber to Acquire ezCater for $2.3 Billion
articles.titleKo: Uber to Acquire ezCater for $2.3 Billion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Uber Eats couriers are expected to gain additional earning opportunities through catering orders. Uber is making a significant move into the catering business. The company announced Tuesday that it reached a $2.3 billion agreement to acquire ezCater, a platform for catering and workplace meals, in an all-cash transaction. The deal is expected to close in the coming months, pending regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions. The acquisition would combine ezCater’s business catering platform with Uber Eats and Uber for Business, giving Uber a larger foothold in a segment that can deliver high-value orders to restaurant partners. ezCater works with more than 140,000 restaurants nationwide and helps businesses manage food orders for meetings, events, and recurring workplace meals. Its technology also includes tools for managing orders and food spending, along with 24/7 customer support. Within the past year, chains like Five Guys, Denny’s, Mendocino Farms, and Mission BBQ have joined the ezCater platform. The company recorded more than $2.5 billion in gross bookings during the trailing 12 months, with growth in the high teens year-over-year. It is profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis and is expected to be margin accretive to Uber. The size of ezCater’s transactions also sets the business apart from traditional restaurant delivery. Its average order value exceeds $400. “We’re thrilled to be joining forces with Uber. Our team is proud of what we’ve built — the leading platform for workplace catering, and a major growth channel for our restaurant partners,” ezCater CEO Nihad Rahman said in a statement. “We’re energized to bring our catering and B2B expertise to Uber’s global ecosystem of customers, merchants, and couriers.” For restaurants, Uber said the combination could provide access to larger orders and new customers. The deal also gives businesses another way to order group meals through Uber’s ecosystem, covering workplace meals, events, and social gatherings. Uber Eats couriers are expected to gain additional earning opportunities through catering orders as well. The transaction connects three pieces of the companies’ businesses. ezCater brings its catering and B2B expertise and restaurant network, Uber Eats contributes its consumer, restaurant, and delivery reach, and Uber for Business provides existing relationships with organizations of varying sizes. For ezCater, joining Uber offers an opportunity to put its catering technology and restaurant network in front of a much larger customer base. “Catering is a big business, and can be a huge revenue stream for restaurants,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said in a statement. “Nihad and his incredible team have built an amazing platform. With Uber’s reach, we can bring that experience to millions more customers and help restaurants win more of these valuable orders.” The post Uber to Acquire ezCater for $2.3 Billion appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: QSR Ad of the Month: Chick-fil-A Brings Waffles, and Nostalgia, to the Masses
articles.titleKo: QSR Ad of the Month: Chick-fil-A Brings Waffles, and Nostalgia, to the Masses
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chick-fil-A put on its pajamas for this month’s spotlighted ad, a seasonal promotion for its new Chicken and Waffles sandwich. The ad’s throwback style conceals a canny bit of strategy for the restaurant chain: a move to expand the waffles window from morning to all-day bringing a southern brunch classic to all areas of the country. Waffles and syrup are for breakfast and the brand knows it. Its cast are dressed in pajamas and sleepwear with images of alarm clocks and breakfast tables throughout the ad, and dances which look very much like a set of morning exercises. But the sandwich being promoted with Chick-fil-A chicken joining the waffles is not just a morning proposition, and the ad makes sure viewers know it’s going to be available all day. It’s a win-win strategy for the brand. Promote a new menu item but also make both breakfast and daytime options more attractive for customers and what better way to do that than breakfast all day? The smart marketing extends to the creative elements of the ad, which embraces a very old school aesthetic of joyful dancing, clear product offers and even a brand new and highly catchy jingle, which could easily become a new distinctive asset for Chick-fil-A. PAST WINNERS: Anderson .Paak Gets His Pizza Hut Degree Little Caesars’ ‘Deal Deer’ Hits the Right Value Notes KFC’s Comeback is Crispy, Competitive, and Cooked to Perfection Why Panda Express Hit the Right Notes with AAPI Heritage Tribute Jersey Mike’s ‘Pocket’ Packs Starpower Zaxbys’ ‘Sauce Boss’ Has Star Quality Starbucks Shows Why ‘Together Is The Best Place To Be’ Subway’s Value-Based Spot Hits Home Panda Express’ ‘Wishes’ Takes Customers on an Emotional Journey Chick-fil-A Captures the Appeal of ‘Newstalgia’ Wendy’s Finds the Sweet Spot with a March Madness Dunk Pun KFC and the Colonel Dance into Audience’s Hearts Chipotle Comes Out Swinging Chili’s and Lizzo Get Wild Without Losing Focus Starbucks’ ‘Pink Energy’ Fizzes with Creativity Wendy’s Pretzel Bacon Pub Cheeseburger Makes the Perfect Reintroduction That’s no small thing: System1’s research, The Creative Dividend , found that campaigns using a jingle average a 3.1 Star Rating (long-term brand growth), compared to 2.8 for those using neither a jingle nor a sonic device, along with stronger brand recognition and a bigger lift in fame and distinctiveness. You might be tempted to call it “newstalgia,” a trend Chick-fil-A tapped into earlier this year, or part of a trend, but this style of advertising is classic for a reason – it works. Ads like this don’t care whether they seem corny—not when they boast strong branding, clear messaging, and most of all entertainment, all things that moved the sales needle. System1’s Test Your Ad report shows that the old tricks still work. Chick-fil-A’s Chicken and Waffles ad scores a very strong 4.5-Star Rating, a measure that predicts long-term business effects and brand growth. That puts in the top 12 percent of all QSR and Coffee Shop ads. Where Chick-fil-A really shines is in another one of System1’s key metrics, Spike Rating, which predicts an ad’s potential for short-term sales boosts. The Exceptional Spike score is in the top 1 percent in the category—this ad has the potential to be sales dynamite. Why does it work so well? And Fast Fluency—quick recognition—is born from the early, strong branding. Brand well and get noticed—old school virtues that go together for Chick-fil-A as well as … chicken and waffles. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . John Peyton, sitting at Dine Brands HQ in Pasadena, California, was some 8,000 miles away from where the first dual-branded IHOP and Applebee’s sprung up in Dubai. Being so far from corporate, he said, meant the franchisee could veer from the playbook and ask for permission later. Eagles Landing International Restaurants did just that as it designed and opened half a dozen “before we were even paying attention,” Peyton recalled. But, approval aside, he kept hearing positive things. A couple debuted in Mexico and Peyton hopped on a plane. “[I] came back and said to the team, this is a really big idea,” he said. “And we opened the first one a year ago, April.” Speaking at the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference, Peyton walked through the much-talked-about model that’s provided Dine Brands a growth lane it hasn’t appreciated in a while. That overseas inspiration- turned-stateside launch outside San Antonio , has 45 open today, with 80 projected by year’s end. All but three are conversions, meaning the original restaurant (Applebee’s or IHOP) added the second. With close to 50 active, Dine Brands has been able to paint a steady economic impact for franchisees. It costs about $1 million to tack on (a bit more going from IHOP to Applebee’s thanks to the addition of a bar). And stores are seeing consistent revenue growth of 1.5 to 2.5X original gains. So, a $2 million IHOP becomes a $3 million combo. The most compelling note for Peyton, he explained, is nobody walked into HQ and suggested putting an IHOP and Applebee’s in the same building, “because no one [would] ever think of that.” Yet when examining tickets, two-thirds are items from both sides of the menu. In the morning, combo restaurants are selling pancakes and ribs. In the evening, they’re moving omelets and skillets. “And so, guests that are experiencing it are actually taking advantage of it,” Peyton said. “We’re giving them something they didn’t know they wanted. And we’ve got a very robust pipeline for next year as well.” He noted most combo stores are now serving Bloody Marys. Peyton was asked about the deliberation process going forward. As leases come up, or franchisee agreements spin, Dine Brands is hosting conversations 12–24 months in advance on what might be next. It covers the typical queries. Should the store move? Has the market changed over the decades? But now, if operators do elect to continue (94 percent of Dine Brands’ agreements are renewed, Peyton said), the notion of a renovation or combo could enter the debate. It’s likely that will happen more often in the years to come. Dine Brands projects 900 opportunities for IHOP-Applebee’s combo stores in the U.S. alone. Of those, 450 are new builds and 450 conversions (an existing brand adding the other). When the company devised the 900 number, Peyton said, as you’d imagine, it built a big model in Pasadena with ample assumptions, market conditions, population growth, and traffic factors. It ran figures with the idea it wouldn’t approve any restaurant in danger of cannibalizing another. If Dine Brands had, for instance, done so with 5–10 percent impact, it would have come up with 1,600 potential outlets instead of 900 (IHOP ended Q2 with 1,813 restaurants and Applebee’s 1,557). In other terms, a lot of franchisees can’t covert. An operator running an Applebee’s 2 miles from an IHOP won’t receive approval to do so. Dine Brands isn’t lacking for internal interest, however. Regarding this note, Peyton said things have not unfolded exactly as expected. The company’s initial hypothesis was it would need to build a batch to prove out the concept and demonstrate numbers for franchisees. Portillo’s fans know the brand’s famous chocolate cake and cake shakes are simply out of this world. Now, as spooky season gets into full swing, Portillo’s is teaming up with the OREO brand to introduce a trio of new treats: the OREO Shake, OREO Cake and OREO Cake Shake. Available nationwide for a limited time starting October 6, this iconic collaboration gives guests even more flavor-packed menu items to complete their favorite Portillo’s meal. “At Portillo’s, innovation starts with understanding what our guests love, and amplifying it,” said Denise Lauer, Chief Marketing Officer of Portillo’s. “That’s why we’ve reimagined our dessert lineup with three distinctive offerings that bring together the rich flavors of our famous cake and shakes with the unmistakable taste of OREO cookies. We’re excited to introduce an iconic pairing that is both playful and perfectly indulgent, just in time for the Halloween season.” Portillo’s has built a loyal following around its desserts, with the brand’s beloved chocolate cake becoming one of the most talked-about items on the menu – the kind of treat guests build entire orders around. This new collaboration featuring OREO cookies gives fans three new ways to experience that spirit of indulgence: OREO Shake : Portillo’s creamy hand-spun vanilla shake, loaded with crushed OREO cookie pieces in every sip. OREO Cake : A delicate, moist white cake mixed with crushed OREO cookie pieces, iced with sweet OREO frosting and topped with OREO cookie pieces. OREO Cake Shake : A creamy hand-spun vanilla shake mixed with OREO Cake and topped with crushed OREO cookie pieces. The OREO Cake Shake draws its roots from one of Portillo’s signature creations: the original Chocolate Cake Shake, born from a simple idea – blend the brand’s famous cake right into a creamy shake. That creative twist quickly became a guest favorite in its own right, and decades later, the same spirit of invention shaped this collaboration, giving fans three brand-new ways to enjoy Portillo’s cake with one of the world’s most beloved cookies. “The OREO brand has always been about turning a delicious cookie into something people build memories around, and this collaboration with Portillo’s does exactly that,” said Matt Foley, Vice President, OREO. “Bringing our cookie into Portillo’s famous cake, in three different ways, gives fans a fresh, playful way to enjoy OREO cookies beyond the pack.” Portillo’s is also offering members of its Portillo’s Perks loyalty program a hauntingly delicious limited-time deal. From October 12-18, Perks members can enjoy a $1 slice of OREO Cake with a purchase of $5 or more.* The OREO Shake, OREO Cake and OREO Cake Shake are available nationwide at Portillo’s locations beginning October 6, 2026, while supplies last. articles.titleKo: As New COO at Snooze, Amy Hom’s Leadership Playbook Starts With Listening

Few operators have seen as many corners of the restaurant industry as Amy Hom. She’s helped run salad bowls at sweetgreen, burgers at Red Robin, and tapas at Barcelona Wine Bar. Now, she’s taking on pancake flights and mimosas. Hom stepped in as chief operating officer of Snooze Eatery on September 28, joining a brand known for its playful, retro-futuristic vibe and creative twists on breakfast classics. “I’m very intentional about the opportunities I choose … At this stage of my career, the question isn’t whether I’ve done the job before,” Hom says. “It’s where I can make a meaningful contribution, continue learning, help build what comes next, and have fun along the way.” In her conversations with CEO Josh Kern and the rest of Snooze’s leadership team, Hom led with curiosity. She wanted to understand the vision for the business, where they believed Snooze could go next, and how she could complement the strengths of the leaders already around the table. Join Hom and other women leaders at FSR and QSR’s annual WiRL Summit! Registration is now open here. “What excited me was the opportunity to help influence and grow the brand while protecting what already makes it special,” Hom adds. “I’m also genuinely looking forward to the journey with Josh and the team … work should be meaningful, challenging, and rewarding, but it should also be enjoyable.” With 72 locations in 10 states, Snooze is eyeing its next growth spurt, and Hom’s appointment reflects an investment in operational leadership. Her task is to lead restaurant operations and work closely with field leaders and teams across the organization. That means elevating hospitality, strengthening operational accountability, and making sure the restaurants have the tools and support to deliver an exceptional guest experience. Hom says consistency doesn’t mean conformity, and she’s certainly not coming in to flatten Snooze’s culture. She doesn’t believe culture and accountability should compete. Instead, she thinks the right operational strategy helps protect culture and creates more freedom for Snoozers. Some things, she says, should be non-negotiable: how the brand takes care of its Snoozers, the quality of its food, and how it treats guests. Leaders also need to be excruciatingly clear about standards. That level of clarity, she says, is part of caring deeply for others. “I don’t need Snooze to feel exactly the same. I want every Snooze to unmistakably feel like Snooze. The last thing I want to do is take the personality, fun, hospitality, and individuality out of our restaurants in the name of operational excellence,” Hom says. “I’ve always said, easy on people, tough on standards … operational discipline should remove unnecessary friction, so our people have more energy to do what they do best—take care of each other and our guests.” Hom has always believed that great operations start with great people, so her first 90 days will include a lot of time in restaurants listening. Her biggest responsibility right now, she says, is to learn the business from the Snoozers who live in it every day. She wants to hear what’s not working, what they need, and what gaps exist between the restaurant support center and the restaurants themselves. But she’s also listening for what’s working. Sometimes, she says, organizations spend so much time looking for problems that they miss chances to celebrate the small wins happening inside their restaurants every day. She’s listening for everything, but especially for patterns. After that, she says, she has a responsibility to close the loop and make sure teams feel heard and understand each decision, whether it’s a yes or a no. “One person saying something is feedback. articles.originalSummary: Christie & Co has reported a 22% increase in pubs and restaurants brought to market between January and August compared to the same period last year. The property adviser’s latest Pubs & Restaurants Market Review revealed that within the eight-month period the business was instructed to sell more than 360 properties, and agreed more than 230 deals, a 12.5% increase on the year before. Christie & Co say the figures reflect strong buyer demand across the pubs and restaurants market, with average completion values increasing by approximately £105,000 for freehold sales and £87,000 for leasehold sales. Freehold transactions accounted for 79% of pub deals, while 12% were leasehold and 9% involved a new lease. Restaurant transactions were split between new leases at 44%, leaseholds at 37% and freeholds at 19%.

articles.title: Scott Hallsworth Brings Back Joe’s Oriental Diner to Balham
articles.titleKo: Scott Hallsworth Brings Back Joe’s Oriental Diner to Balham
articles.originalSummary: Acclaimed chef Scott Hallsworth brings Joe’s Oriental Diner back to London this week, opening at 1 Ramsden Road, Balham , in the former home of his cult restaurant Freak Scene. Joe’s Oriental Diner first popped up on London’s King’s Road in 2015 , taking over the tiny space where Hallsworth’s Kurobuta had begun life a couple of years earlier. The idea was simple: big Southeast Asian flavours, small plates, cold drinks and none of the ceremony . Now Joe’s is back, with the same spirit and a new home in Balham. Taking its cues from the diners, bars, street stalls and late-night eating spots of Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and beyond , the menu is all about punchy, spicy, sweet, sour and smoky food made for sharing and getting stuck into. Dishes include Tuna Sashimi with Pomelo, Hot Miso, Pickled Chillies and Yuzu Soy (£14) ; Rare Thai Beef Salad with Roasted Peanuts and Burford Brown Egg Relish (£14) ; Jungle Curry of Quail with Sticky Rice and Lettuce Cups (£10) ; and Singapore Chilli Crab Wonton Bombs . Drawing on Hallsworth’s 35-plus years in professional kitchens , including seven years at Nobu where he rose to Head Chef at Nobu London, Joe’s brings serious cooking without the fine-dining formality. Designed to be affordable enough for a Tuesday night and good enough for a Saturday night , Joe’s pairs its sharing plates with properly made cocktails, cold beer and a short, sharp wine and sake list. Informal, energetic and approachable, it is first and foremost a neighbourhood diner designed to be used all the time, with plenty of reason to travel to Balham for it too. For Hallsworth, the return of Joe’s marks a return to the spirit of the original King’s Road restaurant – big flavours, great drinks and seriously good food without the fuss – this time firmly rooted in its new Balham neighbourhood. Joe’s Oriental Diner opens this month at 1 Ramsden Road, Balham, London

articles.title: The Original Ivy Introduces the Ivy Edition Vol. 03, A New Chef-Curated Menu Available Exclusively at West Street
articles.titleKo: The Original Ivy Introduces the Ivy Edition Vol. 03, A New Chef-Curated Menu Available Exclusively at West Street
articles.originalSummary: Something new is on the table as The Original Ivy introduces the latest volume of its exclusive chef-curated Edition Menu. The Original Ivy is delighted to introduce The Ivy Edition Vol. 03, the latest chapter in its exclusive menu series, available only at the iconic West Street restaurant. Carefully curated by The Ivy’s chefs, the new edition brings together familiar favourites and refined seasonal dishes, guided by exceptional ingredients, bold flavour and thoughtful execution. Available daily from 11.30am until close, guests can enjoy two courses for £39.95 or three courses for £49.95, with each volume offering a carefully considered collection of dishes that reflects The Original Ivy’s enduring commitment to timeless cooking and impeccable hospitality. The menu opens with elegant starters including a vibrant English Goat’s Cheese Salad with heritage tomatoes, peach and toasted almonds; Potted Shrimp with seasoned brown shrimp butter, dill-pickled cucumber and toasted granary bread; comforting Pea and Ham Soup with smoked ham hock, lovage and pea shoots; or Crispy Cod Cheek served with tartare sauce, cornichons and baby leaves. For the main course, guests can savour beautifully prepared dishes including Pan-Fried Cornish Hake with silky cauliflower purée, confit potatoes, sea herbs and parsley sauce; Salted Beef with horseradish dumplings, swede, carrots and root vegetable broth; Treacle-Cured Pork Cutlet with fried hen’s egg, pineapple and grain mustard sauce; or a comforting Lentil and Aubergine Cottage Pie with roasted pumpkin purée and spiced tomato. An 8oz Grilled Sirloin of Beef with garlic butter, onion rings, roasted cherry tomatoes and baby watercress is also available for a £5.95 supplement, for those wishing to elevate the experience further. To conclude, the menu celebrates timeless British desserts with a nostalgic Banoffee Pie , a refreshing Lemon Posset with raspberry compote and thyme shortbread, classic Eton Mess with English strawberries, or a selection of Cornish Yarg and Barkham Blue cheeses with apple and apricot chutney and wholegrain crackers. Guests can also begin with one of The Original Ivy’s signature nibbles, from Truffle Arancini and Zucchini Fritti to the luxurious pairing of Imperial Caviar and Crisps , setting the tone for an elegant dining experience from the very first bite. Sean Burbidge, Executive Chef at The Ivy Collection, said: “With every Edition Menu we look to create something that feels both familiar and fresh. Volume 03 brings together dishes our guests know and love alongside new seasonal additions, each chosen for the quality of the ingredients and prepared with care. It’s a menu that reflects everything The Original Ivy has always stood for: timeless cooking, bold flavour and exceptional produce.”

articles.title: The Big Challenge of Building Smaller Restaurants
articles.titleKo: The Big Challenge of Building Smaller Restaurants
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Compact drive-thrus have long been part of Scooter's Coffee's identity. The race to smaller restaurant footprints has a limit. Checkers & Rally’s learned that lesson with a 570-square-foot prototype unveiled last spring. “We tested it and found that it was just slightly too small,” says Eileen Himber, senior manager of franchise development. The company adjusted the design to about 700 square feet—still 300 square feet smaller than its prior prototype, but with more room to protect operational flow. That distinction is increasingly important as quick-service brands chase lower development costs, more flexible real estate, and faster, convenience-led service. A small building can widen a franchisee’s options, but leaders behind three drive-thru-centric concepts say it cannot simply be a conventional restaurant with square footage stripped away. It must be designed around its menu, employees, channels, and guests. Smalls Sliders utilizes a modular real estate and construction strategy built around 750- to 800-square-foot repurposed shipping containers called “cans.” They are prefabricated off-site and dropped onto compact half-acre plots. “We don’t really think about it in the sense of shrinking a restaurant,” says chief development officer Ryan Crumley. “Rather, we built the can around the kitchen and the team so that they can do one thing exceptionally well.” Scooter’s Coffee’s small stores, likewise, are a longstanding part of its business model rather than a response to the latest development cycle. Its roughly 1,000-square-foot end-cap format accommodates guests in the store, and the company also operates nontraditional units in airports, hospitals, and sports venues. But its traditional drive-thru kiosk, between 650 and 700 square feet, is the core prototype. “The way this space is designed is intentionally around the business we want to operate,” says Aaron Hoffman, Scooter’s vice president of franchise sales. “We’re not trying to squeeze a traditional coffee house into a smaller box.” That model can support expansion in secondary and tertiary markets, where a large café may not pencil out. “You don’t need a massive population base or large-format building to have a successful coffee business,” Hoffman says. “Those customers still want great brands and experiences, but the economics have to fit the community.” Checkers & Rally’s sees the inverse opportunity. A smaller box can help franchisees enter large metropolitan markets, where space is limited and expensive, Himber says. It can work on a smaller parcel or let an operator use a larger site for co-branding. On a conventional site, it can make room for a longer drive-thru stack. The operational work is where the model either delivers on its promise or breaks down. In a compact kitchen, equipment placement, inventory, and employee movement are intertwined. Smalls works from the kitchen outward, examining the movements required for each role. Crumley says the brand’s model enables it to run with fewer employees and adjust staffing more readily during peak and off-peak dayparts. “You’re not paying people to run across the restaurant,” he says. But tighter quarters can magnify seemingly minor design mistakes. Smalls once tested a tall piece of equipment to move food from its cook line to its expo line, only to learn that it obstructed sightlines and reduced nonverbal communication between employees. “The only way we’re ever able to do that is having a great feedback loop from our franchisees,” Crumley says. At Checkers & Rally’s, eliminating a second drive-thru lane in the 570-square-foot prototype hindered flow, Himber says. The lane also serves digital-order and third-party delivery pickup customers, so the brand brought it back. The company also scrutinized redundant equipment. “We found that there were redundancies that we could eliminate,” she says.

articles.title: When A Restaurant Empire Unravels: What Franchisees, Landlords, and Suppliers Should Know
articles.titleKo: When A Restaurant Empire Unravels: What Franchisees, Landlords, and Suppliers Should Know
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Restaurant bankruptcies can move quickly, particularly when a company is pursuing a sale intended to preserve operating value and operations. Recent restaurant bankruptcies have shown just how quickly financial trouble at the corporate level can ripple across an entire franchise system. Red Lobster, Rubio’s Coastal Grill, and other restaurant companies have gone through bankruptcy proceedings in recent years. More recently, FAT Brands, the parent company of 18 restaurant brands and a system of approximately 2,200 locations and 670 franchise partners worldwide, filed for bankruptcy in January. For restaurant operators, franchisees, landlords, and suppliers, the important question is often not simply whether a restaurant company files for bankruptcy. It is what happens next. A bankruptcy filing does not necessarily mean every restaurant closes or every brand disappears. A company may restructure, sell individual concepts or assets, transfer certain agreements to new owners, or reject contracts it no longer intends to perform. As a result, different pieces of the same restaurant system can have very different outcomes. Businesses tied to a distressed restaurant company should evaluate those possibilities early. A buyer may not inherit everything One of the biggest misconceptions surrounding a restaurant bankruptcy is that when a brand or group of restaurants is sold, the buyer simply steps into the shoes of the previous owner. That assumption is often wrong. The Bankruptcy Code allows a buyer to acquire selected assets, including restaurant brands, intellectual property, and certain contracts, free and clear of many prior claims and obligations, provided the court approves the sale and specific legal conditions are met. The scope of what a buyer assumes depends on the purchase agreement and the court’s sale order. That distinction matters throughout a franchise system. A buyer may want the brand and its strongest locations without taking on every existing agreement or financial obligation. The sale agreement and bankruptcy court order ultimately determine what is transferring. Stakeholders should not assume that a new owner will honor every obligation simply because the brand continues operating. Franchisees need to know where their agreements stand For a franchisee, the continued existence of the brand does not mean business will continue as usual. Franchise agreements are generally treated as “executory contracts” under the Bankruptcy Code, which means the company may have the option to keep the agreement, transfer it to a buyer, or reject it through the bankruptcy process. Before keeping or transferring a franchise agreement, the company must address any existing defaults, typically by paying what is owed, and show the court that whoever takes over the agreement can perform going forward. Those decisions can affect some of the most fundamental elements of a franchisee’s business, including its right to operate under the brand, royalty and advertising obligations, access to operating systems and approved suppliers, and territorial or development rights. Brand and trademark rights can become particularly complicated when a franchise agreement is rejected through the bankruptcy process. A franchisee may still have certain rights after rejection, but whether it can continue using the brand, and under what terms, can depend on the agreement and circumstances of the case. Franchisees should not assume that rejection automatically ends every right under their agreement. In some cases, a franchisee whose agreement is rejected may have the right to continue using the brand’s intellectual property, such as trademarks and operating systems, for the remaining term of the agreement, provided the franchisee continues making required royalty payments. Anise, located at The Drey Hotel at The Village, is entering a new chapter with a completely reimagined food and beverage program led by The Village Culinary Director Eduardo Osorio and Executive Chef Rene Deleon. The refreshed Anise is now a contemporary neighborhood gathering place designed to take guests from breakfast and coffee through lunch and weekend brunch, before transitioning into cocktails and evening bites after dark. The evolution marks a new identity for Anise, centered around the idea of becoming the kind of restaurant guests can make their own. Warm and welcoming with an easygoing approach to hospitality, Anise is equally suited for settling in over locally roasted coffee, meeting for a working lunch, lingering over weekend brunch or stopping in for cocktails and a bite at the bar in the evening. At the heart of the new Anise is a culinary philosophy Osorio describes simply: great ingredients, cooked with intention, approachable enough to remember and comforting enough to come back for. “Anise is about food that makes people feel good,” said Eduardo Osorio, Culinary Director at The Village. “Guests should recognize what they’re eating, but there should always be something — a technique, a sauce or an unexpected ingredient — that makes the dish feel distinctly Anise. We want guests to be impressed by how the food tastes, not by how complicated it is.” Culinary Talent To bring that vision to life, Osorio is joined by Executive Chef Rene Deleon, who returns to Anise after previously working at the restaurant in 2022. Deleon brings an accomplished culinary background to his new role, including serving as Executive Chef at Bullion and Corporate Executive Sous Chef for Mina Group. His experience also includes time at Grant Achatz’s Michelin-starred Next Restaurant in Chicago, after beginning his career at Achatz’s acclaimed Alinea as a chef de partie, server and expediter. Together, Osorio and Deleon have created menus rooted in familiar dishes layered with thoughtful ingredients, sauces and techniques. The result is food intended to feel polished without becoming precious — from breads and pastas to vegetables, comforting classics and desserts from Pastry Chef Brenda Perez. articles.title: Vandelay Companies to Bring Hudson House and Jack & Harry’s to San Antonio
articles.titleKo: Vandelay Companies to Bring Hudson House and Jack & Harry’s to San Antonio
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Vandelay Companies – a Texas-based hospitality and investment company – is expanding to San Antonio with two of its signature concepts, Hudson House and Jack & Harry’s, set to open side by side at 5307 Broadway in Alamo Heights in 2027. Hudson House is slated to open late Spring 2027, with Jack & Harry’s to follow Summer 2027. Exact opening dates will be announced closer to launch. The two restaurants will occupy the ground floor of the former Nix Health building at 5307 Broadway in Alamo Heights, a two-story property currently undergoing an adaptive reuse by San Antonio-based Ridgemont Properties. Originally built in 1965, the building is being transformed from its former medical use back to its retail origins, including the reopening of its historic breezeway. The street level will feature two thoughtfully designed restaurant spaces, with office space located above. “This development has truly been a team effort. We’re grateful to the City of Alamo Heights for supporting transformative development along the Broadway Corridor, to SHOP Companies for bringing best-in-class food and beverage operators to the project, and to Vandelay Companies for believing in our vision for this property and the community,” said Trebes Sasser, Jr., VP of Ridgemont Properties, Inc. “Hudson House is one of the state’s most recognized food and beverage brands, while Jack & Harry’s fills a real need for elevated dining in Alamo Heights. We’re proud to have both anchoring the development.” Hudson House will occupy approximately 6,360 square feet. Since opening the first Hudson House 2017, the East Coast-inspired neighborhood favorite has become a fixture across Texas for lunch, brunch, dinner and especially happy hour. The brand is known for its award-winning cheeseburger, flown-in-daily East Coast oysters, a robust raw bar and sushi program, and the cult-favorite “World’s Coldest Martini,” served on tap and chilled to a crisp 10 degrees. Interiors channel the charm of a traditional New England dining institution, with warm leather booths, a wraparound bar and a sit-down raw bar. Jack & Harry’s will occupy approximately 5,950 square feet and marks the concept’s first location outside of Dallas. An elevated Southern steakhouse inspired by the culture, cuisine and hospitality of New Orleans, Jack & Harry’s debuted in 2024 and quickly became known for its French-influenced cooking, dry-aged steaks, Gulf seafood, Bourbon Street-inspired cocktails and a French-forward wine program. The San Antonio location will carry the brand’s signature design language of imported New Orleans brick, warm wood paneling and antique finishes that evoke the French Quarter. “San Antonio has been on our radar for a long time, and Alamo Heights felt like the right place for us,” says Hunter Pond, Founder, Chairman & CEO of Vandelay Companies. “Broadway has a strong sense of history and a real neighborhood identity, which is something we value. Bringing Hudson House and Jack & Harry’s here together gives us the opportunity to introduce two distinct experiences while becoming part of a community we’ve admired for years.” The San Antonio expansion reflects Vandelay Companies’ broader approach to growth: identifying strong neighborhoods and markets, investing in each restaurant for the long term and building concepts designed to become lasting parts of the communities they serve. Additional details surrounding the menus, design and opening timelines will be announced closer to each restaurant’s debut. articles.title: 55 Seventy to Brings its Dallas Dining Concept to Houston in November
articles.titleKo: 55 Seventy to Brings its Dallas Dining Concept to Houston in November
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . 55 Seventy, the highly-anticipated private members’ club, announced today that its Houston location will open on Friday, November 27 at 3015 Richmond Ave, Houston, TX 77098. The private members club is designed for those who appreciate exceptional dining, world-class wine, and a strong sense of community. The club will debut with two dining concepts under one roof: its signature lounge and dining room and Canopy Bar, a 10,000 square foot rooftop restaurant overlooking Levy Park. Canopy Bar brings a Mediterranean menu to the rooftop, anchored by a pizza oven, with indoor and outdoor seating designed for long afternoons and unhurried evenings above the city. Downstairs, the main lounge and dining room offer a more intimate setting with an upscale American menu shaped by the culinary team’s years in Michelin starred kitchens, carrying forward the standard 55 Seventy has set in Dallas since 2022. Both menus move with the seasons, built around ingredients at their peak, so members find something new with each visit. Executive Chef Diego Fernandez and Executive Banquet Chef Jacob Solomon will lead the culinary program, bringing their impressive pedigrees and extensive experience to the club’s culinary vision across the signature lounge and dining room, Canopy Bar, private dining, and events. Born in Mexico City, Fernandez helped open his family’s acclaimed Azuca Nuevo Latino in San Antonio before cooking at San Francisco’s Quince and Chicago’s three Michelin starred Alinea. Most recently, Fernandez served as the research and development chef for Pappas Restaurants. Executive Banquet Chef Jacob Solomon oversees private dining and events. A Chicago native, Solomon was part of the team at NoMi when it earned its Michelin star, later served as a Corporate Executive Chef for Michael Mina across 20 operations, and opened Orla at the Regent Santa Monica Beach as Executive Chef. “Diego and Jacob have cooked in some of the most respected kitchens in the country, and they understand what makes 55 Seventy different,” said Tommy Shuey, Founder/CEO of 55Seventy. “In Dallas, we set out to serve the best food in the city, and we are holding Houston to that same standard. This team will make Houston’s 55 Seventy entirely its own.” Leading the wine program as Executive Director of Wine is Master Sommelier Justin Moore. Moore is one of just 305 professionals worldwide to hold the Master Sommelier title. For the past four years, he has led the wine programs at Rose’s Restaurant Group in Washington, D.C., including its Michelin starred restaurants Pineapple and Pearls, Rose’s Luxury, and Little Pearl. A former Executive Chef who oversaw four Charleston kitchens by age 25, Moore moved into wine in Nashville before advancing through the Court of Master Sommeliers and earning his Master Sommelier title in 2019. Following its successful UK debut, India’s iconic food brand Haldiram’s is set to open its first US restaurant in Frisco, Texas, on Sunday 11 October. Located at 7010 Preston Road, Suite 240, Haldiram’s Frisco will introduce the brand’s much-loved Indian dishes, and large repertoire of products across sweets and snacks to a new audience in a full-service, casual dining space designed for sharing, snacking and exploring aromatic Indian flavors. The 110-cover restaurant will span approximately 4,400 sq. ft., offering a welcoming dining destination designed to accommodate a variety of occasions, from family meals and group gatherings to casual dining experiences. Dallas marks the starting point of Haldiram’s restaurant expansion into the US, with the wider Dallas–Fort Worth region offering an opportunity to introduce the brand’s longstanding culinary heritage to the Indian diaspora and American consumers interested in exploring authentic Indian cuisine. On the menu are some of India’s most beloved dishes, spanning street food, traditional thalis and chaats. Favorites include Raj Kachori, Choley Bhature, Pav Bhaji and Pani Puri, alongside traditional Indian sweets such as Rasmalai and Gulab Jamun. The opening coincides with the auspicious festival of Navratri, during which the restaurant will also introduce a special menu of traditional fasting-friendly dishes, celebrating the festival’s cultural and culinary traditions. Beyond the restaurant menu, guests can explore a dedicated sweet counter and retail area featuring traditional Indian mithai and a selection of Haldiram’s packaged products. Sweets have long played an important role in Indian celebrations, festivals and gifting, and the offering brings this part of the brand’s heritage to the US, giving customers the opportunity to discover familiar favorites, festive treats and products to share with family and friends. The US expansion is headed by Mr Pankkaj Agarwal, Managing Director at Haldiram Snacks Pvt. Ltd., alongside Rhea Agarwal, Commercial Director – UK and EU. Together, they are leading the brand’s international growth, building on its established presence in the UK and Europe while introducing Haldiram’s to new markets. “Bringing Haldiram’s to the United States is an important milestone in our international journey. Food has always been about more than what is on the plate; it connects people to their memories, their families and their culture. Through our restaurant in Texas, we look forward to bringing familiar flavors to the Indian community while welcoming a new generation of diners to experience the richness and diversity of Indian cuisine. This is an exciting first step in our journey in America.” said Rhea Agarwal, Commercial Director – Haldiram’s UK & EU. Founded in 1937, Haldiram’s has grown from a small Bhujia shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan into a global food brand, now present in over 80 countries including the US and UAE, with more than 200 restaurants across North India. Its US debut marks a new chapter in the brand’s international growth, bringing together its longstanding connection with Indian food, sweets and snacks with a contemporary dining experience tailored to a new market.
