articles.title: The Blu Fin Introduces Seafood-Focused Fine Dining to Vero Beach in Florida
articles.titleKo: The Blu Fin Introduces Seafood-Focused Fine Dining to Vero Beach in Florida
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Windward Restaurant Concepts is sharing a first look at The Blu Fin’s debut menu ahead of its official opening on Tuesday, Oct. 13, the first of three culinary venues debuting in Vero Beach this fall. Previously announced as part of the 27,000 square feet development at 1410 South A1A, The Blu Fin will be followed by Turtle Cove Gourmet Market and The Motley Cow, together offering three distinct experiences from fine dining and celebratory dinners to market stops and afternoon cocktails under the palapa. The complex is the brainchild of Vero Beach native Anthony DeChellis, owner of Windward Restaurant Concepts. DeChellis tapped Argentine-born Sebastian La Rocca, whose career includes experience in MICHELIN-recognized restaurants in Europe and the Americas, to lead the culinary direction across all three venues. At the heart of the trio is The Blu Fin, a fine-dining restaurant rooted in Mediterranean cuisine with Latin inspiration. The Blu Fin will offer indoor and outdoor dining across 3,000 square-feet, with 78 seats total, including six at the bar and eight at bar tables. The restaurant is already planning an over-the-top celebration for its first New Year’s Eve, with details to be announced this fall. La Rocca’s opening menu moves between the Mediterranean and Latin America, with seafood playing a prominent role. Bright, fresh flavors lead the starters, including Cured Red Snapper , which pairs ajo blanco with Granny Smith apple vinaigrette, toasted buckwheat and shaved truffle, and Olive Oil-Poached Lobster with lettuce gazpacho and a charred yellow corn and cucumber salsa. The Blu Fin Tuna Crudo layers Cara Cara orange-vanilla sauce with Corona beans, celery, shallots and Calabrian chile, while Octopus Tonnato offers an unexpected take on the Italian classic with confit tuna sauce, caperberries, pickled shrimp, heart of palm and cured egg yolk. For a richer start, Bourbon Barrel Wood-Smoked Beef Tartare brings together lobster bisque sauce, caviar, Wagyu tallow and quail egg yolk with crisp rye. Seafood carries through the entrées, from Grouper Roasted on Cedar Wood Plank with Champagne clams, sea asparagus and sunchokes to Grilled Madagascar Tiger Shrimp paired with bok choy and piquillo pepper romesco. A luxurious Capellini combines Santa Barbara sea urchin with saffron cream and caviar, while Roasted Heritage Chicken gets a rich finish from foie gras velouté, Israeli couscous and wild mushrooms. Latin influences come through in El Secreto Iberic Pork , pairing the prized cut with Oaxaca mole, duck fat cipollini onions and a fresh fennel and herb salad. Two steak dishes are also on offer. Black Angus Ribeye gets layers of acidity and richness from roasted Jimmy Nardello pepper escabeche, confit garlic, chimichurri and Barolo onion jus, while Charley’s Steak , inspired by iconic 1970s Vero Beach favorite Charlie Brown’s, pairs Black Angus New York steak with a giant lump crab “fricassee.” The tableside experience includes the steak arriving beneath a cloche, the fricassee served separately and a presentation box from which guests select their steak knife. La Rocca plans to work with local fishermen, farmers and other suppliers whenever possible, allowing seasonality and local ingredients to guide the menu. articles.title: Chipotle Creates Original Track Played Entirely on Vegetables
articles.titleKo: Chipotle Creates Original Track Played Entirely on Vegetables
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Every note, beat and texture was performed using ingredients found in Chipotle restaurants. No guitars. No keyboards. No synthesizers. Just vegetables. Chipotle Mexican Grill today unveiled “From Ground to Sound,” an original song recorded inside Abbey Road Studios’ Studio Two using instruments made entirely from fresh vegetables, turning the same real ingredients prepared in its restaurants every day into the sound of the brand. The composition was first teased in the final frames of Chipotle’s 100 Creators ads that premiered in August (see here , here and here ) and will continue as a signature sound across select Chipotle campaigns. Fans can listen to the track now on Spotify and Apple Music and watch the full “From Ground to Sound” film at https://youtu.be/Uoq8sdfgupk. Every note, beat and texture was performed using ingredients found in Chipotle restaurants, transformed into playable instruments including flutes made from corn, trumpets built using jalapeños, a horn created from peppers and an avocado pit, lettuce percussion and an onion bass. Freshness You Can Hear To pull it off, Chipotle teamed up with the London Vegetable Orchestra , a five-member ensemble of classically trained musicians specializing in creating and performing with instruments made from vegetables. The process required three months of experimentation and dozens of iterations to determine how ingredients like corn, jalapeños and bell peppers could be transformed into instruments capable of producing the right notes, tones and textures. Even then, there was little room for error. Fresh produce continuously changes in shape, texture and moisture, meaning the instruments must be built and played at peak ripeness and remain usable for less than a day. That gave the musicians only a brief window to assemble, tune, rehearse and record before the sound began to change. The result turned the natural variability of fresh ingredients into part of the creative process, using the same real produce Chipotle serves every day, without artificial colors, flavors or preservatives. “Real food has always been at the center of Chipotle. We use only 53 real ingredients, with fresh preparation happening every day in our restaurants. So we took this principle in a completely new direction: creating our own signature sound,” said Fernando Machado, Chief Brand Officer at Chipotle. “Any brand can release a song or develop a sound mnemonic. What made this worth pursuing was the chance to create a track that felt impossible to separate from Chipotle itself. The instruments, the sound and the story are all rooted in what we do every day.” “No two vegetables ever behave exactly the same way,” said Patrick Johns of the London Vegetable Orchestra. “You can carve two identical instruments, but they can respond very differently. Part of the craft is learning not to force an ingredient to sound a certain way but to find the sound that’s already there and build the music around it.” From Ground to Sound Every day, Chipotle crew members prepare real ingredients by hand, from chopping vegetables to making fresh guacamole. For “From Ground to Sound,” those same ingredients became the creative medium. The original composition, created by Beacon Street Studios with creative direction from advertising agency KIDS, was inspired by the energy of vegetables growing from seeds into nourishment. “The role of creativity is to help people experience familiar things in unfamiliar ways,” said Icaro Doria, Founder and Chief Creative Officer at KIDS. “Millions of people know Chipotle’s ingredients by how they look, taste and smell. Very few have ever stopped to ask what they sound like. That question led us somewhere no one expected.” The post Chipotle Creates Original Track Played Entirely on Vegetables appeared first on QSR Magazine .

With Asia representing an important area of focus heading into 2027, Freddy’s is seeking experienced operators that can leverage local market expertise alongside the brand’s established operating model to drive long-term growth. Freddy’s has built a foundation around its commitment to quality and genuine hospitality, offering cooked-to-order steakburgers, shoestring fries, and frozen custard treats in a warm, family-friendly atmosphere. articles.title: Vitality Bowls Honors 15th Anniversary with Special Deal
articles.titleKo: Vitality Bowls Honors 15th Anniversary with Special Deal
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Fifteen years after opening its first café in the Bay Area, Vitality Bowls has grown a family-inspired mission into a nationwide superfood café brand serving communities across the country. This October, the brand known for its açaí bowls, smoothies and health-focused menu is celebrating its 15th anniversary while reflecting on the people, innovation and purpose that have shaped its growth since 2011. To thank guests for being part of the journey, Vitality Bowls is extending the celebration throughout its anniversary weekend. October 16 to 18, guests can receive $5 off orders of $15 or more when ordering through the Vitality Bowls app at participating cafés. “When Roy and I opened the first Vitality Bowls café 15 years ago, we were motivated by something deeply personal: creating a place where people could find nutritious, allergy-friendly food they could feel good about,” said Tara Gilad, Co-Founder and President of Vitality Bowls. “To see that idea grow from one café into 70+ communities across the country is incredibly meaningful. So much has evolved over the years, but the purpose that started Vitality Bowls continues to be at the heart of who we are today.” Founded by Roy and Tara Gilad in 2011, Vitality Bowls was born from the couple’s desire to find safe, healthy food alternatives after discovering their daughter’s severe food allergies. That personal mission became the foundation for a concept centered on high-quality ingredients, superfoods and meals designed to accommodate a variety of dietary needs. Since opening its first café, Vitality Bowls has sold 15,554,825 açaí bowls nationwide, including 973,703 in the past year alone. While açaí has remained at the heart of Vitality Bowls for 15 years, the brand has continued evolving alongside its guests. Its menu has expanded beyond açaí bowls and smoothies to include salads, wraps, grain bowls and other savory offerings, while innovations such as Harvest Kitchen, Vitality Bowls’ virtual brand offering protein-packed, nutrient-rich meals, have created new ways for guests to enjoy the brand throughout different parts of their day. This year, Harvest Kitchen introduced catering, providing an additional way for guests to enjoy its savory menu at meetings, gatherings and community events. That evolution has extended beyond the menu. Vitality Bowls continued expanding its national footprint in 2026 with new cafés in New Jersey, North Carolina and Texas while additional locations remain in development across new and existing markets. The continued growth builds on the brand’s 15-year commitment to bringing health-focused dining options to more communities nationwide. “Reaching 15 years is something we’re incredibly proud of, but we’re even more energized by where Vitality Bowls is headed next,” said Roy Gilad, Co-Founder and CEO of Vitality Bowls. “We’ve continued to evolve the menu, find new ways to serve our guests and bring Vitality Bowls into new communities, all while staying true to the mission that started the brand. There is still tremendous opportunity ahead of us, and we’re excited to build on everything we’ve accomplished over the past 15 years.” To learn more about Vitality Bowls, visit the company’s website at vitalitybowls.com . Uncommon Brands today announced the appointment of Douglas Kwong as Vice President of Marketing and Lucious Kimble III as Corporate Controller. The company also promoted Jack Franken to Vice President of Finance and Strategy. The Dallas-based restaurant group’s portfolio includes Fuego Tortilla Grill, a fast-casual concept known for its handmade tortillas and oversized tacos, and The Rice Box, a Houston-born Chinese American restaurant concept. “Douglas has helped grow some of the most respected brands in the restaurant industry, and Jack and Lucious bring the financial and operational experience we need,” said Garrett Mills, Chief Executive Officer of Uncommon Brands. “We’ve been intentional about bringing together people who understand what it takes to build strong businesses, including recognizing leaders like Jack who have already made a significant impact here. He’s helped build the financial and data foundation we run the business on. Douglas and Lucious also bring an established working relationship in marketing and finance from their time together at &pizza. We’re excited for what all three will bring to our portfolio.” As Vice President of Marketing, Kwong will lead marketing strategy across the Uncommon Brands portfolio, focusing on brand positioning, guest acquisition and loyalty. He brings more than two decades of experience driving brand transformation for restaurant and consumer brands. Kwong’s experience includes leadership roles at Pei Wei, Cicis Pizza, Urban Air Adventure Parks and, most recently, &pizza. At Pei Wei, Kwong played a key role in separating the brand from P.F. Chang’s and relaunching it with new positioning. During his tenure, e-commerce revenue increased from 8% to 30% of total sales. He also contributed to a 17% increase in average unit volume and 16% unit growth at Urban Air Adventure Parks. At &pizza, Kwong served as Head of Marketing, where he led guest acquisition and loyalty initiatives, including the launch of &pass, the brand’s pizza subscription program. Kimble joins Uncommon Brands as Corporate Controller with more than a decade of accounting and finance experience in the restaurant and hospitality industries. He will oversee companywide accounting and financial reporting. Prior to joining Uncommon Brands, Kimble served as Corporate Controller for &pizza, where he led the accounting function and supported financial operations for the restaurant portfolio. Franken has been promoted to Vice President of Finance and Strategy, where he will serve as a strategic partner to the Chief Executive Officer and leadership team. In his expanded role, he will lead financial planning and strategic analysis, as well as evaluate investment opportunities across the portfolio. His experience includes roles in corporate finance and investor relations at Wingstop. Since joining Uncommon Brands, Franken has led the development of its Snowflake data infrastructure and AI-enabled reporting platform. He also oversaw the financial onboarding of Fuego Tortilla Grill and The Rice Box and established a repeatable process for future acquisitions. The leadership moves strengthen Uncommon Brands’ capabilities across marketing, strategy and finance as the company scales its portfolio and supports each brand’s distinct identity. articles.title: The People Plan Fueling CAVA’s Expansion
articles.titleKo: The People Plan Fueling CAVA’s Expansion
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . CAVA has a clear career pathway for its employees. CAVA found a problem in its pipeline of future general managers. Some employees training for the job needed a second job to earn a full-time wage. The fast-casual Mediterranean chain’s GM in training position was hourly, offered no guarantee of full-time hours, and existed only in certain restaurants based on sales volume and traffic. It gave employees a route to promotion, but it also left gaps in their preparation and limited the time GMs could spend developing them. The roughly 500-unit CAVA responded by creating an assistant GM position with a commitment to full-time hours, higher compensation, and more demanding hiring criteria. The change gave restaurants a clear second-in-command and created more opportunities for employees to acquire the skills needed to run a location. According to chief people officer Kelly Costanza, the investment serves a practical need as CAVA adds restaurants. Opening a location requires people who can operate it and prepare the employees who will run the next one. “We realized too as we open restaurants and the number of restaurants that we’re opening every year, if we want to have a pipeline of talent, then we need to give our general managers time to develop people,” Costanza says. CAVA—which wants to reach 1,000 locations by 2032—tested the assistant GM position last year. Costanza says it freed GMs to spend more time on employee development, and the company has seen gains in restaurant operating metrics and retention. The assistant GM can open and close the restaurant, direct team members, and run the location in the GM’s absence. Tasks such as building schedules, handling progressive discipline, and documenting performance give the assistant opportunities to learn alongside the GM before assuming full responsibility. The hiring process changed, too. CAVA extended practices used to select GMs to the assistant role, including behavioral interview guides and questions tied to its competencies (i.e. service mindset, accountability, diversity cultivation, and people development). Candidates must offer examples of past actions that demonstrate their fit for the company. Increased compensation helps CAVA attract applicants with more experience. The position fits within Flavor Your Future, CAVA’s career development platform. But filling jobs is only one part of the work. The company also needs a consistent way to teach employees what success requires. Its Academy GM Program turns qualified GMs into trainers for incoming GMs and assistants preparing for promotion. Regional trainer coaches visit markets and certify participants, who must meet operating standards and demonstrate the company’s competencies. Academy GMs also gather for an annual summit. At the June event in Texas, participants completed additional certification through CAVA’s competency champion trainer program. The curriculum addresses workplace behaviors and teaching skills, adding another layer to their operational training. Employees receive an introduction to career opportunities as soon as they join the company. Onboarding modules show potential career paths and explain competencies at different job levels. Costanza has completed the hourly employee onboarding herself and sat with a team member working through the training during a restaurant visit. After 90 days, employees are introduced to an impact plan. These plans connect an individual’s ambitions to quantitative goals, development goals, and competency goals, giving the employee and their manager specific items to work toward. CAVA makes available jobs visible through Grow at CAVA posters on restaurant communication boards. A QR code links employees to opportunities across the company. articles.title: LIME Fresh Mexican Grill Launches New Loyalty Program
articles.titleKo: LIME Fresh Mexican Grill Launches New Loyalty Program
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . LIME Fresh Mexican Grill, the Florida-born fast-casual favorite known for its fresh, made-to-order Mexican cuisine and laid-back South Beach spirit, is showing its guests some love with the launch of LIME Lover, a new loyalty program created to reward the community that has supported LIME for more than two decades. Launched as part of the brand’s new “LIME Loves You Back” campaign, the program debuts Oct. 6 in celebration of National Taco Day, giving members the opportunity to earn points toward tiered rewards, receive personalized offers and enjoy special perks with every visit. To celebrate the launch, LIME is giving members an extra reason to stop in during National Taco Day week. LIME Lover members who dine at participating locations from Oct.6–9 will receive a free small guacamole reward in their account following their qualifying visit. New members get something right away, too; guests who enroll in LIME Lover will receive a free OG Taco reward upon signing up. After enrolling, members earn points on every eligible purchase and move through four tiers: L, I, M and E, spelling out LIME. Every member starts at the L or Local tier, earning 10 points per $1 spent. Members who spend $350 to $849 within the last 365 days move to the I or IYKYK tier and earn 11 points per $1 spent, while those who spend $850 to $1,749 reach the M or MVP tier and earn 12 points per $1 spent. Members who spend $1,750 or more reach the E or Elite tier and earn 13 points per $1 spent. Points can be redeemed for rewards starting at 500 points for a free soda or tea, side of guacamole or queso, or OG chicken or beef taco, up to free fajitas for 2,000 points, with additional rewards available at point levels in between. And there’s no race against the clock. LIME Lover points never expire, so members can keep accumulating points toward their next reward. Members can earn points by providing their phone number at checkout or when ordering online or through the LIME Lover app, and registered members can also receive personalized offers. Since opening its first taco spot on Alton Road in South Beach in 2004, LIME has built a devoted following around high-quality, made-to-order Mexican favorites and an easygoing approach to dining. Tacos, bowls and salads share the menu with made-from-scratch salsas and award-winning margaritas, staying true to the brand’s longtime “no freezers, no microwaves” approach. More than 20 years later, LIME operates eight locations across Florida and is preparing for further growth across the state through a new re-franchising effort. “Our guests have shown LIME a lot of love over the years, and LIME Lover gives us a way to return it,” said Patrick Fore, CEO of LIME Fresh Mexican Grill. “We wanted to create something that makes every visit a little more rewarding, whether you’ve been coming to LIME for years or you’re just getting to know us. It’s about recognizing our regulars, welcoming new guests into the community and giving everyone more reasons to keep coming back.” LIME Lover members can manage their rewards and order through the new LIME Lover app, bringing ordering and loyalty benefits together in one place. The program is powered by Olo Loyalty, formerly known as SpendGo, which integrates rewards directly into the ordering process so members can earn and redeem points as part of their regular LIME experience. For more information about LIME Lover, including sign-up details, points structure and FAQs, visit limefreshmexicangrill.com/rewards . For the latest from LIME Fresh Mexican Grill, visit limefreshmexicangrill.com and follow @LimeFresh on social media. articles.title: True Food Kitchen Declares Bankruptcy
articles.titleKo: True Food Kitchen Declares Bankruptcy
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . True Food Kitchen has 42.1 million in debt. Better-for-you concept True Food Kitchen announced Monday that it has declared bankruptcy. The casual chain shuttered 12 stores in conjunction with the court filing, leaving it with 34 restaurants across 14 states. True Food Kitchen will undergo a sales process and use court protection to improve its financial standing, restaurant footprint, cost structure, and operational improvements. The brand is supporting itself through bankruptcy with $20 million in debtor-in-possession financing from HumanCO TFK IV. The chain owes roughly $42.1 million in debt, including some merchant cash advance agreements with multiple lenders. “True Food Kitchen is a pioneering brand with a distinctive position in wellness-driven dining, a loyal community of guests, and a mission that is more relevant than ever,” CEO Jeff Chandler said in a statement. “This process is the best path forward to simplify the business and focus on what we do best: delivering craveable, health-forward food and genuine hospitality. We are confident this step will help us build a stronger True Food Kitchen for the future.” True Food Kitchen was founded 18 years ago in Phoenix, Arizona, by wellness author Dr. Andrew Weil and restaurateur Sam Fox. It is positioned as a healthier alternative, focused on an anti-inflammatory diet, minimal processing, and simple ingredients. The chain was originally a part of Fox Restaurant Concepts, but was spun off in 2017 when it reached 20 locations. By 2022, the company had announced a $100 million funding round , the largest investment in the chain’s history. True Food Kitchen reached 46 restaurants before closures began. The brand has been hampered by significant management turnover, which has in turn led to inconsistency around expansion strategies, brand direction, and menu innovation. Different leadership teams invested money outside of core markets and devoted resources to food and beverage lineups and restaurant concepts that were not aligned with the company’s original values, according to court documents. One of these ideas included the Tempe, Arizona-based True Food To-Go , a quick-service prototype that never gained traction. COVID disrupted operations as well. To make up for the loss of in-person dining, True Food Kitchen transformed some locations into ghost kitchens and opened an off-site kitchen for delivery only. These ventures have since been terminated so that the brand could focus on the main dining experience. Some restaurants are profitable, while others are in areas with low foot traffic because of shifting markets and demographics. Leading up to the bankruptcy, True Food Kitchen looked to resolve its financial woes by hiring Chandler in July 2026, engaging with consulting firms to help assess real estate and potential strategic alternatives, laying off corporate staff, renegotiating vendor contracts, looking for buyers to take over unexpired leases, and only keeping staff necessary to handle bankruptcy administration. “We know these decisions are especially hard on the team members affected, and we are deeply grateful for their contributions to True Food Kitchen and their communities,” Chandler said. “We are committed to approaching this difficult moment with care and respect, and we will share information on resources and next steps with affected team members.” The post True Food Kitchen Declares Bankruptcy appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Snooze Eatery Names Amy Hom COO
articles.titleKo: Snooze Eatery Names Amy Hom COO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Amy Hom stepped in as chief operating officer of Snooze Eatery on September 28, joining a brand known for its playful, retro-futuristic vibe and creative twists on breakfast classics. Snooze Eatery has named Amy Hom chief operating officer, effective Sept. 28. With more than two decades of restaurant and hospitality experience, Hom has led operations for some of the industry’s most recognized brands, building strong teams, developing leaders and driving consistent execution across complex, multi-unit restaurant organizations. At Snooze, Hom will lead restaurant operations and work closely with field leaders and teams across the organization to elevate hospitality, strengthen operational accountability and ensure restaurants have the tools and support to deliver an exceptional guest experience. Her appointment represents an intentional investment in experienced operational leadership as Snooze builds on its recent momentum and prepares for its next chapter. “Amy understands that great restaurant operations start with great people and ultimately show up in the guest experience,” said Josh Kern, CEO of Snooze. “She knows how to create accountability and operational discipline while developing leaders and protecting what makes a brand special. That combination is incredibly important for Snooze. As we look ahead, Amy will help us raise the bar on hospitality and execution while staying true to the culture and experience our Snoozers and guests love.” Hom joins Snooze after serving as chief operating officer of Barcelona Wine Bar, following leadership roles with Bluestone Lane, REEF, sweetgreen, Red Robin, Wolfgang Puck Catering and California Pizza Kitchen. She also co-founded LEAD, a community focused on leadership education, mentorship and connection and serves on the boards of Women in Restaurant Leadership, GLEAM Network and the Texas Restaurant Association. Her experience across a wide range of restaurant models and operating environments has shaped a leadership approach centered on strong field leadership, disciplined execution and developing high-performing teams. “I’ve always believed that great restaurant operations start with great people,” said Hom. “What drew me to Snooze is the passion its teams have for hospitality and the guest experience. My focus will be on spending time in our restaurants, listening to our teams, developing our leaders and making sure they have what they need to deliver at a high level every day. Snooze has something special, and I’m excited to help build on it.” Amy is passionate about developing the next generation of restaurant leaders. She co-founded LEAD, a community focused on leadership education, mentorship and connection, and serves on the boards of Women in Restaurant Leadership, GLEAM Network and the Texas Restaurant Association and a member of the Fast Casual Industry Council. Recognized among the Top 30 Women in Food multiple times and Top 25 Fast Casual Executives, Amy is a frequent speaker on hospitality, leadership and building strong workplace cultures. articles.title: The Flying Biscuit Café to Open in Katy, Texas
articles.titleKo: The Flying Biscuit Café to Open in Katy, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . An all-day breakfast and lunch café is coming to 1660 S Mason Rd in Katy, Texas, where franchise partners Mario Harper and Ifeoma Harper have signed a lease for their first The Flying Biscuit Café. The café is targeted to open in late November 2026 and will join five Flying Biscuit cafés already open across the Houston area, with two more Texas cafés in development. The Harpers were drawn to Katy’s sense of community and its growing, diverse neighborhoods — an area they describe as welcoming and full of people who appreciate good food and a warm, local dining room. They are also looking forward to building relationships with local community groups across Katy. The café will offer full-service catering, for team breakfasts, school events and family gatherings. “We chose this location in Katy because it’s a highly visible, convenient spot that’s easy for families and neighbors to reach — making it simple for guests to drop in for breakfast, brunch and those ‘just one more bite’ moments in between,” said Mario Harper, franchisee. “We’re most excited to serve the people who make Katy home, and the neighbors who love gathering around food and creating everyday traditions.” The Flying Biscuit Café in Katy will open at 1660 S Mason Rd, Katy, TX 77450, in late November 2026, serving breakfast and lunch daily. The menu includes stuffed French toast, shrimp and grits, omelets, vegan scrambles, burgers and wraps, and the café will have a full bar with brunch-forward cocktails. Hiring information and updates will be posted at flyingbiscuit.com. “Texas has moved fast for us, and Katy is a good example of why,” said Andrew Scherzer, partner and director of franchise development for Flying Biscuit Franchising. “Mario Harper and Ifeoma Harper picked a site they can actually run well — visible, simple to get in and out of, right in the middle of where people already are. That kind of decision-making is what we look for in a partner, and it is why the Houston market keeps opening up for us.” The franchisees were represented in the transaction by Littwitz Investments. Katy is the next step in a market the brand has been building out for years. A sixth Houston-area café, in Magnolia, Texas, opens next, which will make Katy the seventh in the market once its doors open in November. Beyond Houston, a café in Abilene, Texas, is planned for the second quarter of 2027. The Katy lease lands in a busy stretch for the Atlanta-founded brand. Owner-operator Chris Compton opened his second Flying Biscuit in downtown Knoxville, Tenn., on Sept. 12, 2026. John and Gisela Terranova are opening the brand’s first Orlando-area café, in Kissimmee, Fla., in the coming weeks. And in St. Charles, Mo., franchise partners Latrell Hayes, Kennon “Kip” Barber and Randy Barnes are targeting the fourth quarter of 2026 for the brand’s first café in the St. Louis metro and its first outside its core Southern footprint. Flying Biscuit now has 44 locations open and 12 in development. Operators interested in available markets can find territory information, requirements and a first point of contact at flyingbiscuitfranchising.com, or by calling the franchise sales line at 678-726-1884. The post The Flying Biscuit Café to Open in Katy, Texas appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: Chip City Cookies Closes Permanently
articles.titleKo: Chip City Cookies Closes Permanently
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chip City Cookies was founded in 2017. Chip City Cookies has shut down its remaining 22 stores, ending retail operations for a brand that grew from a small Queens storefront into a multistate chain backed by Danny Meyer’s Enlightened Hospitality Investments. In an email to employees on October 1, Chip City president Nicolas Baizan said the company could no longer fund its operations. “After almost 10 years of passionately serving our loyal customers, we have decided to cease all store operations,” Baizan wrote. “This means our 22 remaining stores will permanently close at close of business today. I am sorry to share that today will be your last day as a Chip City employee.” Baizan cited declining consumer spending and changing preferences as pressures on sales. “We made extensive efforts to address these challenges over the course of this year in partnership with our Board and investors,” he wrote. “Unfortunately, we no longer have the funding required to operate this business.” Chip City had 39 locations as of July, when it promoted Baizan to brand president. The shutdown follows a September 28 lawsuit filed in New York Supreme Court by cofounder and former CEO Peter Phillips against Chip City, two Enlightened Hospitality Investments entities, Baizan, and former interim CEO Fred LeFranc. According to the complaint, Phillips stepped down as CEO under a March recapitalization agreement that guaranteed nine months of transition compensation and family health coverage through December 2. He alleges the company stopped his pay September 18, then terminated his employment and scheduled cancellation of his benefits after he demanded payment. Phillips also alleges the defendants conditioned restoration of his pay and benefits on transferring four web domains and signing documents related to Small Business Administration loans he personally guaranteed. Phillips is seeking unpaid compensation, damages, continued health coverage, and legal fees. The end of store operations marks a reversal from the expansion plans Chip City outlined just over two years ago. In May 2024, the company announced a $7.5 million Series B investment from Enlightened Hospitality Investments, bringing the firm’s total investment in the brand to $17.5 million. Chip City said the funding would support restaurant openings, employees, services, and brand collaborations. At the time, it reported plans to grow to more than 50 nationwide. Phillips and cofounder Teddy Gailas started Chip City in Astoria, Queens, in 2017. The concept built its identity around oversized cookies and a rotating menu, using its app and social media to connect with customers and introduce specialty flavors. KYURAMEN has opened a multi-brand fast-casual destination at 40 Gold Street in Manhattan’s Financial District, bringing together the first Kyuramen Express, the debut of Bao Dumpling, and Aokō Matcha. The new fast-casual spot lets guests pair ramen and Japanese comfort food with Chinese-takeout-inspired dumplings, matcha drinks, and desserts under one roof. At the center of the experience is Kyuramen Express, KYURAMEN’s first fast-casual format. The menu offers a streamlined selection of Japanese comfort food favorites, with its signature offerings including the Tokyo Tonkotsu Shoyu Ramen, Sapporo Miso Ramen; Kyushu Spicy Tonkotsu Ramen. A selection of udon, rice bowls, sushi, onigiri, appetizers, and combination meals are also available giving guests the flexibility to build a quick and satisfying meal. The opening also marks the introduction of Bao Dumpling, a new concept created by the KYURAMEN Group that puts a fresh spin on familiar Chinese comfort food. At its core, Bao Dumpling combines the flavors of popular Chinese takeout dishes with dumplings, allowing guests to enjoy two beloved foods at the same time rather than choosing one or the other. Highlights include its Signature Dumpling Bowls, where guests can choose from a variety of flavors, including the signature Spicy Kung Pao Chicken Dumpling and the chef’s special Orange Beef Dumpling. The menu also includes classic rice bowls, bao, noodles, and shareable bites. Completing the trio is Aokō Matcha, a matcha-focused brand offering Japanese-inspired beverages and desserts serving “matcha reimagined – in every shade of green.” Signature offerings include its #8 Gelato, known to be the richest in the U.S., Aokō Parfait, and Aokō Matcha Soft Serve. The menu also features specialty matcha drinks including the Matcha Float with Mochi and Strawberry Matcha Latte, alongside mille crepe cakes and more. “This is our first opportunity to bring several KYURAMEN experiences together in one fast-casual setting,” said Gary Lin, Founder and CEO of KYURAMEN. “We wanted to create a space where guests can build the meal they want and enjoy Asian-inspired comfort food at one convenient location. articles.title: California Pizza Kitchen Offers 25,000 ‘Apology Pizzas’ for National Pizza Month
articles.titleKo: California Pizza Kitchen Offers 25,000 ‘Apology Pizzas’ for National Pizza Month
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . California Pizza Kitchen (CPK), the iconic restaurant brand that revolutionized pizza, is making amends with its fan base this National Pizza Month for failing to bring back all the beloved pizzas from its past menus. Responding to years of guest requests and social comments clamoring for the comeback of pizzas like Jamaican Jerk Chicken, Shrimp Scampi, or Pear and Gorgonzola – the brand is humorously offering a two-part appeasement to its guests. First, up to 25,000 so-called “Apology Pizzas” will be available to claim through the end of the month, followed by a promise to bring one fan-favorite pizza back to the menu in 2027. “We take full responsibility for the unforgettable pizzas that fans have loved and lost,” said Chef Paul Pszybylski, Vice President of Culinary Innovation at California Pizza Kitchen. “But this National Pizza Month, we’re making it right – with 25,000 free pizzas now, one returning pizza next year, and zero regrets about how seriously we’re taking this. So yeah, we’re sorry, but also you’re welcome.” To demonstrate the complete seriousness of its remorse, the brand has gone as far as hiring a CFO (Chief Forgiveness Officer) to record a special video message to guests, posted to CPK’s social channels today. The “Apology Pizza” Starting today, fans can claim their free pizza by simply commenting “Apology Accepted” on CPK’s Instagram (@cpk), TikTok (@calpizzakitchen) or Facebook (@cpk) in-feed social posts and videos. CPK will immediately respond with a direct message and redemption code valid for one free 7” pizza with any $20 online purchase. Up to 25,000 codes are available through October 31 while supplies last, and pizzas can be redeemed through November 10. Throughout the month, CPK will post multiple apology-accepting opportunities on its social channels, so fans should follow closely for their chance to participate. 2027 Bring Back In addition to the show of good faith during National Pizza Month, the brand is also gearing up to welcome a top fan-favorite pizza back to the menu in 2027. CPK executives will be monitoring social channels to identify the most cherished pizza of its past. “We’ll be listening even more closely this month,” said Dawn Keller, Chief Marketing Officer at CPK. “We invite all guests to speak up through comments or their own posts – your voice could decide the destiny of CPK pizza fans nationwide.” For more information, please visit www.cpk.com/apologypizza. The “Apology Pizza” offer is available from October 1 through October 31, 2026, and redeemable through November 10 at participating CPK locations. Valid for one 7” free pizza of select varieties (The Original BBQ Chicken Pizza, Mushroom Pepperoni Sausage, Pepperoni, Margherita, Wild Mushroom and Hawaiian) with a minimum net purchase of $20 on CPK.com or the CPK app (excluding tax, gratuity, delivery fee and alcohol). Johnstown, it’s time to slide thru as Smalls Sliders prepares to officially open its second Can in the state. Located at 4781 Thompson Pkwy & Eisenhower in Johnstown, the fast-growing cheeseburger slider brand will celebrate its grand opening on Oct. 2 at 10 a.m. To celebrate the opening, the Johnstown Can will give away 100 pairs of Smalls Sliders slides, available in various sizes while supplies last. Quantities of each size will be limited and distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. The event will also include a ribbon-cutting ceremony and recognize Boys & Girls Clubs of Weld County as the Can’s Smalls Town Hero with a check presentation. The organization supports kids and teens through after-school and summer programming focused on academics, leadership, mental and physical health, and healthy lifestyles, while also providing nutritious meals and snacks to help address food insecurity among local youth and families. The Johnstown Can builds on Smalls Sliders’ Colorado debut earlier this year in Northglenn and marks the next step in the brand’s expansion with Mountain Sliders and franchisee partners Nick and Alix Ralls. The group is continuing to grow its footprint across the state, with an additional Can planned for Green Valley Ranch. “Opening our first Can in Northglenn gave us the chance to see firsthand how Colorado guests would respond to Smalls, and Johnstown is an important next step in what we’re building across the state,” said Nick and Alix Ralls. “We’re looking forward to becoming part of the Johnstown community, introducing even more guests to Smalls and continuing to grow the brand throughout the state.” Mountain Sliders introduced Smalls Sliders to Colorado with the opening of its Northglenn Can in January. Johnstown represents the second location in the group’s multi-unit development plans and expands its presence into Northern Colorado as the team works toward its next opening in Green Valley Ranch. Smalls Sliders has taken the nation by storm, and Johnstown is next to join the Smaucy revolution ignited by the brand’s fan-favorite menu. Specializing in fresh, cooked-to-order cheeseburger sliders—small in size, big in taste—Frequent Sliders know they’re getting a quality product at Smalls Sliders. The menu also features fries, shakes, queso and Smalls Sliders signature Smauce. Smalls isn’t just known for its iconic menu; it is also spotted from miles away thanks to its Smorange Can, uniquely made from shipping containers, featuring streamlined ordering through the walk-up window or drive-thru. For more information on Smalls Sliders, slide thru to www.smallssliders.com or visit www.smallsslidersfranchising.com to learn more about franchising opportunities. articles.title: Two-Thirds of Consumers Are Spending Less at Restaurants, Popmenu Finds
articles.titleKo: Two-Thirds of Consumers Are Spending Less at Restaurants, Popmenu Finds
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . On average, consumers today spend $100 per week on restaurants, an improvement from earlier this year, but still trailing June 2025 by $15. Two-thirds (67%) are spending less on restaurants than last year as they look for ways to dine out while sticking to their budgets. Cutting alcohol, skipping delivery, dining earlier, drinking free water and ordering kids’ meals for adults are among tactics being used. Many are also tipping less and choosing quick service (ex: McDonald’s), fast casual (ex: Panera) and casual (ex: Chili’s) restaurants more often. This is according to a new report by Popmenu, a restaurant technology leader that serves over 12,000 restaurants globally. The report draws on six months of national research on 3,000 U.S. consumers to uncover how dining habits are changing, what guests value most and what this means for restaurant operators. Surveys ran in February, May and July 2026. See the full report here . “Around 30% of monthly food budgets go to restaurants today, down from a high of 40% in 2022,” said Brendan Sweeney, CEO and Co-founder of Popmenu. “What that tells us is consumers are spending intentionally, not reluctantly. Restaurants have pushed menu prices about as far as they can go. Consumers are looking for value and incentives to come back. They’re also looking for the whole experience to be easy, and that starts with the restaurant’s digital storefront.” How are budget pressures reshaping dining behavior? When asked how they are keeping restaurant dining affordable, consumers pointed to the following: 52% – drinking water instead of purchasing a beverage 50% – picking up orders more frequently than ordering delivery 48% – using coupons or rewards points 47% – choosing less expensive restaurants 29% – ordering an appetizer instead of a meal 28% – decreasing alcohol purchases 16% – ordering kids’ meals for adults Which restaurant meals are consumers cutting back on most? A majority (60%) of consumers are dining out less frequently. Dinner is taking the biggest hit, with 46% cutting back, followed by lunch at 37%, breakfast at 28%, and late-night snacking at 24%. What do consumers want from restaurants? When asked what makes them choose one restaurant over another, three factors emerged: visibility, affordability, and being easy to do business with. SEO and AEO are table stakes. 80% use Google and other search engines to find restaurants; 27% use AI tools such as ChatGPT. Restaurants that rank high are chosen more often. Visuals close the deal: 80% are more likely to choose a menu with photos, videos and reviews. Direct ordering is preferred: 94% would rather order from a restaurant’s own website vs. ordering from a thirty party where fees tend to be higher. Value drives spending: 62% prefer restaurants with affordable meal options and special deals; 58% will spend more if there’s a discount. A little VIP treatment goes a long way: 46% are more likely to choose restaurants with loyalty programs; 70% are willing to join a restaurant’s mailing list and 79% would download a restaurant’s app. AI is enhancing hospitality: 60% are ok with restaurants using AI to provide better, faster service, from answering phones and taking orders to preparing and serving food. How much are consumers tipping at restaurants? As belts tighten, 40% of consumers say they are tipping less this year. Of these consumers, 78% say they are cutting back on tips for restaurants and bars. The following shows how much consumers tip, on average, by restaurant type: Restaurant type Tip less than 10% Tip 10% Tip 15% Tip 20% Tip 25% or higher Sit-down restaurants with servers 7 % 17 % 26 % 38 % 6 % Carryout counters 25 % 20 % 12 % 7 % 2 % Coffee shop 23 % 19 % 12 % 8 % 2 % QSR/fast food 21 % 9 % 5 % 3 % 2 % Fast casual 19 % 14 % 11 % 6 % 2 % Survey Methodology Popmenu conducted three anonymous nationwide surveys of U.S

Tocaya is welcoming the season with a full fall and winter menu refresh, bringing new flavors and seasonal ingredients to the modern Mexican restaurant’s lineup. The latest additions include the limited-time Carnitas con Piña Taco, a new Manzana Salad, two beverages, an updated churro offering and two dishes making their permanent debut on the menu. The Carnitas con Piña Taco, available beginning Oct. 1, puts a seasonal spin on a classic pairing, layering slow-braised pork shoulder and smashed pinto beans with a vibrant piña salsa. Made with grilled pineapple, Tocaya’s signature “holy trinity” salsa, lime, escabeche, chipotle and cilantro, the salsa brings smoky sweetness, bright citrus and a subtle kick to every bite. The Fall/Winter Manzana Salad takes a heartier approach to the season, combining carne asada and mole with kale, cabbage, shaved radish, apples, roasted sweet potatoes and butternut squash, cilantro, queso fresco and pepitas, finished with an apple cider honey dressing. “We wanted this menu to feel comforting while still bringing the fresh ingredients and vibrant combinations Tocaya is known for,” said Oliver Plust, corporate executive chef at Tocaya. “The Carnitas con Piña Taco brings that balance through smoky grilled pineapple, bright citrus and subtle heat, while the Manzana Salad takes a different approach with roasted squash, crisp apples and mole. Both dishes show how Tocaya’s signature approach can turn familiar favorites into something unexpected.” For something sweet, Tocaya’s Vegan and Non-Vegan Churros now come with a new vegan chocolate dipping sauce. The churros are also now available through Tocaya’s catering menu. Two new beverages round out the additions: Tamarindo Agua Fresca and Hibiscus Ginger Tea, pairing hibiscus’ floral notes with ginger for a warm, refreshing finish. Alongside the new autumn favorites in the making, two dishes are officially becoming permanent on Tocaya’s menu. Chicken Flaquitos ($10.65 retail / $7.25 happy hour), featuring crispy flour tortillas filled with chicken tinga, smashed pinto beans and Oaxaca cheese, served with creamy salsa verde. Ceviche ($10.85 retail / $7.45 happy hour) pairs poached shrimp with a Tapatío and lime marinade, smoky heirloom tomato, jalapeño sauce and tortilla chips. Amos Durbin brings more than two decades of restaurant and franchise leadership experience. Whit’s Frozen Custard is welcoming an experienced franchise and restaurant operations leader to its team as Amos Durbin joins the company this week as chief operating officer. Durbin brings more than two decades of restaurant and franchise leadership experience to Whit’s, with a career focused on helping franchise partners grow, strengthening operations and building brands in new and existing markets. Most recently, Durbin served as chief operating officer of Viking Group, a Donatos franchise partner, where he led the company’s day-to-day operations. Before that, he joined JHG Pizza as chief operating officer, supporting the company’s Donatos franchise operations. He was named CEO and managing partner just 30 days later and subsequently helped guide that company through a transition to new ownership. Durbin previously spent 4½ years at Donatos as vice president of franchise operations, where he worked closely with franchise partners to strengthen their businesses, streamline operations and expand the brand. During his time with Donatos, franchise partners more than doubled EBITDA, average unit sales increased by more than $4,000 per week, and the brand expanded in both new and existing markets. Durbin’s time at Donatos also gives him a familiar connection to Whit’s CEO Bill Aseere, who previously worked alongside him. “I’ve had the opportunity to work with Amos before, and I saw firsthand the way he approaches franchise operations and, more importantly, the way he works with people,” said Aseere. “He understands that successful growth is about much more than opening more stores. It’s about giving franchise partners the tools, support and confidence they need to build great businesses while protecting what makes the brand special. Amos brings tremendous experience and energy to Whit’s, and I’m excited to have him on the team as we continue growing this brand together.” In addition to his experience with Donatos, Durbin served as a regional director at DineEquity, where he represented IHOP in the family dining segment and supported franchise business consultants, training consultants, and marketing consultants. Earlier in his career, Durbin also spent more than 12 years with Red Robin, where he led five district managers supporting 32 restaurants generating $106 million in revenue and played a role in opening 108 new restaurants. At Whit’s, Durbin will help lead the company’s operations and support its growing network of franchise partners as the brand continues expanding into new communities across the country. “I’m incredibly excited to join Whit’s at such an important point in the company’s growth,” said Durbin. “There’s something special about this brand. Whit’s has a great product, passionate franchise partners and a culture that is genuinely focused on the communities where its stores operate. My goal is to help build on that foundation — supporting our franchisees, strengthening our operations and creating the systems and resources that allow Whit’s to grow while staying true to who we are.” Durbin’s background in franchise operations and multi-unit restaurant leadership will help Whit’s strengthen its support for franchise partners as the brand expands its footprint while maintaining its local-owner approach. Whit’s growth strategy centers on franchise partners who bring the brand to their own communities and make each location their own. From scoop to smile, Whit’s Frozen Custard is committed to serving unforgettable frozen custard in spaces inspired by the communities it calls home. With frozen custard made fresh daily, a growing family of franchise partners and a focus on community, Whit’s continues to bring its down-home approach to more neighborhoods across the country. HTeaO, the nation’s leading iced tea franchise, is continuing its commitment to supporting Breast Cancer Awareness Month with the return of its annual October Round-Up campaign benefiting the Ryan Palmer Foundation Breast Cancer Initiative. Now in its sixth year, the campaign will run from October 1–31, 2026, giving HTeaO customers the opportunity to round up their purchase to the nearest dollar, with 100% of donations expanding access to early detection and support for breast cancer patients currently undergoing treatment. As part of the month-long campaign, HTeaO is bringing back its guest-favorite Pink Lemonade Tea, a blend of lemonade and HTeaO’s Sweet Cherry iced tea. Throughout October, locations will also swap out their signature blue straws for pink straws as a small but meaningful nod to the patients supported through the campaign. At the heart of the campaign are two initiatives: a mobile mammogram program that brings early detection to underserved communities and HOPE Kits for breast cancer patients currently in treatment. Each Hope Kit is designed to provide comfort, encouragement, and practical support during treatment. This year’s kits include fuzzy socks, a tumbler, tea, a Thrive Causemetics product, unscented lotion, lip balm, a HOPE journal and pen, an inspirational bracelet, breast cancer educational resources, and a handwritten note from Jennifer Palmer. For HTeaO, the six-year partnership is a reflection of its Brewing Purpose mission and its commitment to finding meaningful ways to show up for the communities it serves. The annual Round-Up gives guests a simple way to be part of that impact and directly support breast cancer patients undergoing treatment. “Over the past six years, we’ve seen how a simple round-up at the register can turn into saving lives, or providing something incredibly meaningful for someone going through breast cancer treatment,” said Brittany Knollmiller, Director of Marketing of HTeaO. “What makes this campaign so special is seeing our guests, team members, and franchise partners continue to show up year after year. Together, we’re helping put comfort, encouragement and hope directly into the hands of patients when they need it most.” The Ryan Palmer Foundation was founded in 2003 by Amarillo native and professional golfer Ryan Palmer, with a mission to provide opportunities for young people and uplift those in need. Inspired by his wife’s experience with chemotherapy, Palmer launched the Breast Cancer Initiative in 2019, which has since supported hundreds of breast cancer patients across the country. “The growth of our partnership with HTeaO each year fills me with tremendous gratitude,” said Ryan Palmer, PGA TOUR professional and founder of the Ryan Palmer Foundation, alongside his wife, Jennifer Palmer, a breast cancer survivor. “Thanks to the generosity of HTeaO and its customers, we’ve been able to provide mammograms to women in underserved communities and bring comfort and support to women facing a breast cancer diagnosis. This cause is incredibly personal to me because of Jennifer’s journey, and we are proud to partner with HTeaO to honor her and rally around the brave women in each of our lives who are affected by breast cancer.” For more information about HTeaO and its efforts to give back, visit www.hteao.com . Farmer Boys will offer Very Important Farmer (VIF) loyalty members a buy-one, get-one-half-off salad promotion on Monday, October 12, for National Farmer’s Day. The offer is available all day in-store and online. Members who purchase any salad can receive a second salad of equal or lesser value for 50 percent off. The promotion is limited to one discounted salad and is not available through third-party delivery platforms. The chain’s made-to-order salad lineup includes: Farmer’s Chopped Cobb Salad — Grilled all-natural chicken breast, hand-diced Hass avocado, hickory-smoked bacon, shredded cheddar cheese, diced tomato, a cage-free boiled egg, and greens, served with ranch dressing. Southwest Chicken Salad — Grilled all-natural chicken breast, fire-roasted corn, black beans, shredded cheddar cheese, hand-diced Hass avocado, house-made salsa, tortilla strips, and greens, served with house-made spicy-cool chili ranch dressing. BBQ Chicken Ranch Salad — A choice of crispy chicken tenders or all-natural chicken breast with greens, diced tomato, hickory-smoked bacon, shredded cheddar cheese, a cage-free hard-boiled egg, hand-battered onion straws, smoky BBQ sauce, and house-made ranch dressing. Grilled Chicken Salad — All-natural grilled chicken breast, diced tomato, shredded cheddar cheese, and a cage-free hard-boiled egg over greens, served with house-made ranch dressing. Farmer Boys says each restaurant hand-chops an average of 43 heads of lettuce and hand-cuts and smashes 63 avocados daily. The National Farmer’s Day promotion recognizes the farmers who supply the chain’s ingredients. Guests can join the free VIF rewards program by downloading the Farmer Boys app from the App Store or Google Play. articles.title: TOUS les JOURS Partners with Oatly to Launch Gochujang Caramel Latte
articles.titleKo: TOUS les JOURS Partners with Oatly to Launch Gochujang Caramel Latte
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . TOUS les JOURS continues to connect U.S. guests with Korean culture. TOUS les JOURS, the Korean bakery café brand blending French baking techniques with Korean flavors, is partnering with Oatly to launch the Gochujang Caramel Latte. Available October 1 through November 30 at participating bakery cafés nationwide, the limited-time beverage brings a sweet-and-spicy twist to the fall coffee menu. Served hot or iced, the Gochujang Caramel Latte combines espresso and creamy Oatly Barista Edition with sweet-and-spicy gochujang caramel syrup, vanilla oat cold foam, and Lotus Biscoff cookie crumbles. Gochujang, a fermented Korean chili paste, gives the caramel an unexpected spicy dimension. The beverage builds on the original iced Gochujang Latte created by Oatly with Brooklyn-based Korean-American artist, DJ, and producer Yaeji for Café Yaeji, a New York pop-up celebrating Korean café culture through music, art, and coffee. TOUS les JOURS has adapted the concept for its bakery cafés with a caramel-forward interpretation, bringing the experience to guests nationwide. “Our Korean heritage shapes how we create and what we bring to our guests,” said Max Gallegos, Chief Marketing Officer of TOUS les JOURS. “With Oatly, we’re taking a familiar Korean ingredient in an unexpected direction, pairing gochujang with caramel and coffee. It’s an invitation to discover a new flavor and experience the creativity behind our bakery cafés.” “We’ve always believed some of the most interesting things in beverage culture start in cafés, where people are willing to try something they’ve never tasted before,” said Michael Lee, EVP and Executive Creative Director, North America at Oatly. “Yaeji helped us turn gochujang into a completely unexpected coffee experience at Café Yaeji, and TOUS les JOURS gives us the chance to take that idea from one weekend in New York to people across the country. It’s exactly the kind of collaboration we love: culturally rooted, a little unexpected and, most importantly, ridiculously delicious.” To celebrate the launch, the Cerritos, Brea, La Habra, Union St., and Madison Square Park bakery cafés will offer an exclusive Oatly x TOUS les JOURS keychain with the purchase of a Gochujang Caramel Latte. Keychains will be available on a first-come, first-served basis while supplies last. Guests can also enter the #SipIfYouDare Instagram Sweepstakes from October 1 through November 15 for a chance to win one of five $100 TOUS les JOURS gift cards. For entry details, follow @touslesjoursusa on Instagram. No purchase or bakery café visit is required to enter. Winners will be announced November 18. The collaboration continues TOUS les JOURS’ efforts to connect U.S. guests with Korean flavors and culture. Earlier this year, the brand served as the Official Bakery Café Sponsor of BTS THE CITY ARIRANG NEW YORK and participated in KCON LA 2026. The Oatly collaboration brings that spirit of discovery into the everyday bakery café experience. For more information and bakery café locations, visit www.tljus.com and follow @touslesjoursusa on Instagram. Beverage availability varies by location. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The drinks are available through October 31. The Nightmare Shake and Green Ghoul Red Bull Infusion, two spooky and sweet drinks, are awakening at all 900+ Scooter’s Coffee locations nationwide to trick and treat your taste buds beginning today, Thursday, Oct. 1. But hurry, these unsettling sips are only available through the night of Halloween, or while supplies last. The Nightmare Shake blends tart cherry and strawberry flavors into a chillingly creamy blended beverage dressed to impress with strawberry drizzle circling the cup. This frightening new shake comes topped with whipped cream, more strawberry drizzle, and two gummy eyeballs to complete the delightfully eerie look. The Green Ghoul Red Bull Infusion is a hauntingly good drink that gets its ghoulishly vibrant green color from a combination of green apple and lime flavorings. A ghostly ring of mallow drizzle circles the cup to add an element of spooky and a shockingly tasty flavor. Mondays in October are the perfect time to Scoot On Around for these frightening new flavors. Visit each Monday in October after 11 a.m. and receive one of four spooky stickers with any purchase of a large or extra-large drink. A limited number are available each week, so snag yours before they disappear! Third-party delivery orders are not eligible for the sticker giveaway. articles.title: Jersey Mike’s Honors National Disability Employment Awareness Month and Best Buddies Partnership
articles.titleKo: Jersey Mike’s Honors National Disability Employment Awareness Month and Best Buddies Partnership
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Jersey Mike’s Subs, Inc. is honoring National Disability Employment Awareness Month this October, by marking the fourth year of its partnership with Best Buddies International (“Best Buddies”), a nonprofit committed to fostering one-to-one friendships, integrated employment, leadership development, inclusive living, and family support for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) such as Down Syndrome and Autism. Jersey Mike’s customers can support Best Buddies’ mission by rounding up their purchase to the nearest dollar or making a donation. Beginning October 1, Jersey Mike’s customers can support Best Buddies’ mission to build a more inclusive world where everyone can thrive by rounding up their purchase to the nearest dollar or making a donation in-store, in app, or on the website at participating US locations nationwide. Third-party orders are not eligible. 100% of customer donations will be sent to Best Buddies. Donations are tax deductible. “National Disability Employment Awareness Month is a time to recognize the value that people of all abilities bring to the workplace and our communities,” said Charlie Morrison, Chief Executive Officer of Jersey Mike’s. “Giving back is a core value at Jersey Mike’s and we’re proud to continue our partnership with Best Buddies for another year and support its work to expand opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.” Jersey Mike’s and Best Buddies have worked together since 2023 to expand employment opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. What started as a shared commitment has turned into real infrastructure, dedicated training, a candidate-matching process, and hiring practices that have helped bring Best Buddies participants into store teams across the country. Each year, the partnership has expanded its reach, signaling both organizations’ commitment to building workplaces where people with IDD can thrive. “Jersey Mike’s has been an incredible partner and true champion of the Best Buddies mission,” said Anthony K. Shriver, Founder, Chairman & CEO of Best Buddies International. “Together, we’ve opened doors to meaningful employment and given countless individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities the chance to thrive and make friends in the workplace. We’re incredibly grateful for this partnership and excited about what we’ll continue to accomplish together.” The post Jersey Mike’s Honors National Disability Employment Awareness Month and Best Buddies Partnership appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Cousins Subs Announces Return of Semi-Annual Round Up Campaign
articles.titleKo: Cousins Subs Announces Return of Semi-Annual Round Up Campaign
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Cousins Subs is excited to announce the return of its semi-annual Round Up Campaign benefiting the Make It Better Foundation, the brand’s nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting health and wellness, hunger and youth education in local communities. Throughout October, guests can support the Make It Better Foundation by rounding up their purchase at checkout. Contributions made through the campaign help fund grants and programs that strengthen communities throughout Wisconsin. “Every dollar our guests contribute has the power to make a real impact in the neighborhoods we serve,” said Christine Specht, CEO of Cousins Subs. “We are inspired by the generosity of our communities and proud that, together, we can help improve lives and make every day a little better.” The impact of those contributions can already be seen through the Make It Better Foundation’s most recent grant cycle. In the third quarter of 2026, the Foundation awarded $11,000 to five Wisconsin nonprofit organizations supporting youth education, hunger, health and wellness, veterans and families in need. Grant recipients include: Bernie’s Book Bank – $2,500: Supporting the expansion of its book distribution program in Greater Milwaukee, helping provide free, high-quality books to children in under-resourced communities and build at-home libraries. The organization distributes books directly to children through schools, early learning centers and other community partners. Blessed on Purpose – $2,500: Supporting its Pathways to College Tour, which provides mentorship, college and career exposure and essential resources to high school girls from under-resourced Milwaukee-area communities. HeadsUp Fox Cities – $2,500: Helping provide nutritious food and basic-needs support to young adults transitioning from foster care as they work toward greater stability and independence. The organization serves young adults in Winnebago, Outagamie and Calumet counties through transitional housing, mentorship and community-based support. Patriot Riders of America WI Chapter 2 – $2,500: Supporting Wisconsin active-duty military members, veterans and their families through programs that provide assistance with needs including housing, medical expenses and personal support. Shelter From the Storm Ministries – $1,000: Supporting its Mothers for Moms program, which assists homeless single mothers and their children in Sun Prairie and surrounding communities as they work toward self-sufficiency and a more stable future. Since the Make It Better Foundation was established in 2013, Cousins Subs has donated more than $1.4 million to local nonprofit organizations, funded college scholarships, provided nutritious meals to those in need and invested in programs that promote community health and wellness. Guests can round up their purchase at checkout throughout October to support the Make It Better Foundation. For more information on the Make It Better Foundation or to place an order, please visit www.cousinssubs.com. articles.titleKo: FSR Parent Company Arrowfly Acquires Prosper, Expanding Foodservice and Hospitality Portfolio
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Since its inaugural event in 2023, the Prosper Forum has drawn support from more than 300 founding partner organizations and has become a fixture on the foodservice leadership calendar. Arrowfly, an award-winning B2B media and marketing company, today announced it has acquired Prosper Company , including Prosper Forum and Prosper Accelerate, two leadership conferences that connect senior executives and emerging leaders across the restaurant, foodservice and hospitality industry. The acquisition adds two established, executive-level events to Arrowfly’s food, retail and hospitality portfolio. It also gives Arrowfly’s partners access to a highly engaged community of restaurant and foodservice decision-makers, from today’s C-suite to the leaders who will run the industry’s largest brands in the years ahead. Founded in 2023 around the mission of building “A Better Table,” the Prosper Forum is an invitation-only annual gathering. It brings together C-suite executives, operators and franchise owners from leading foodservice and hospitality organizations with the next generation of industry talent. The Forum is home to the Prosper Accelerator, its signature 24-month leadership program. Through the program, senior leaders are paired with emerging leaders nominated by their CEOs. Prosper Accelerate extends that mission through a three-day leadership conference. It combines keynotes with functional think-tank breakouts in leadership development, finance, operations, supply chain, technology, marketing and human resources. “Prosper Forum and Prosper Accelerate have built something rare in this industry: a room where the people running today’s biggest foodservice and hospitality brands sit down with the people who will run them next,” said Matt Logan , CEO of Arrowfly. “The people in that room are exactly who our partners in food, retail and hospitality want to build relationships with, and there is no shortcut to earning that kind of access. Our job is to invest in the foundation Prosper has built and expand its community to more of the industry.” Since its inaugural event in 2023, the Prosper Forum has drawn support from more than 300 founding partner organizations and has become a fixture on the foodservice leadership calendar. The 2026 Forum convened in August at The Ritz-Carlton, Orlando. Its programming spanned talent development, organizational culture, AI adoption, M&A and capital strategy, and workforce policy. Prosper Accelerate will convene October 28–30, 2026, at the Omni Dallas Hotel. “From day one, Prosper has been about elevating the foodservice and hospitality industry by building a better table to drive better business and create better lives,” said David Jobe, co-founder and CEO of the Prosper Company. “We brought together people who thought differently and wanted to win differently. Pairing CEOs and C-suite leaders with the next generation of talent makes the whole industry stronger. Arrowfly understands this industry and shares our commitment to the Connected Community we’ve built. Joining Arrowfly allows Prosper to focus on purposeful growth, widening our impact and growing the talent pipeline while staying true to the mission of inclusion that brought us together.” Restaurant and foodservice operators are navigating persistent labor constraints, rising structural costs, rapid technology adoption, and a generational shift in leadership. Those pressures are increasing the value of forums where executives can share what is working and invest in the leaders who will carry their organizations forward. articles.title: AI and the Future of Hospitality Workflows
articles.titleKo: AI and the Future of Hospitality Workflows
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Automating a single task has limited value if someone still has to manually carry the result into the next step. Much of the work behind the guest experience is administrative, not hospitality. Managers and teams spend valuable time coordinating schedules, processing inquiries, transferring information between systems, and keeping routine workflows moving. AI is a chance to rethink who does what. The real opportunity isn’t replacing hospitality jobs. It’s redesigning workflows so technology absorbs the repetitive coordination, and people spend more time on judgment, relationships, and service. What Hospitality Workflows Are Best Suited for AI? The best opportunities are often the least visible parts of hospitality. Repetitive administrative work behind the scenes pulls focus from what matters most. Tasks like collecting information, entering data, checking availability, and following up take away valuable time that could be spent contributing to the human experience. AI should reduce that burden, not the human interaction at the center of hospitality. Private events show this clearly. A single guest inquiry can trigger a chain of steps: scoping requirements, qualifying the opportunity, answering repeat questions, and passing details across teams. Similar patterns exist in reservations, scheduling, inventory management, reporting, and other workflows. Each one is a place where bottlenecks can form , and the guest feels it. There is a difference between good and poor uses of AI. Predictable workflows with recurring inputs, established business rules, and clear next steps are generally better suited to automation than situations that require empathy, creativity, and nuanced judgment. AI might help organize and qualify an event inquiry, for example, but an employee may still be better positioned to navigate an unusual request or build the relationship around a high-value event. How Does AI Change the Role of Hospitality Employees? Hospitality roles combine many kinds of work. AI is most valuable when it redistributes tasks, not when it replaces jobs. By cutting the manual time on repetitive tasks, automation frees up employee time for work that relies on judgment and human connection. For frontline employees, this may look like offering a more meaningful guest experience, resolving issues, or recognizing opportunities to personalize an experience. In sales and events, it means gaining more time to understand prospective guests. Productivity should mean shifting employee time toward higher-value work, not squeezing more out of every shift. Restaurant managers often hold disconnected processes together. AI that improves information flow and handles routine coordination frees managers to coach their teams, fix problems, and be present on the floor. As technology handles more routine work, employees will increasingly need to understand when AI-generated information or recommendations are sufficient and when a situation requires human intervention. Why Should AI Reduce Complexity Instead of Adding More Technology? Restaurant teams often work across reservation platforms, POS systems, inboxes, spreadsheets, scheduling tools, event systems, and internal communication channels. Even when each tool solves a specific problem, employees often end up connecting those systems themselves. AI should not become another destination they have to monitor. Automating a single task has limited value if someone still has to manually carry the result into the next step. Take an event inquiry as an example. The inquiry itself might be captured efficiently, but someone still has to re-enter details, update another system, notify operators, or track follow-ups elsewhere. Sweetwaters’ interior dining room seats 121, drawing guests in with soaring ceilings and oversized woven pendants that create a sense of drama, balanced by pale woods, richly veined stone, warm metallic finishes and abundant greenery. A luminous 12-seat bar anchors the room, while the open kitchen and four-seat raw bar bring energy and theater to the dining experience. Outdoors, a 90-seat riverfront patio flows toward the water, while a 44-seat second terrace faces Huizenga Park, connecting the restaurant to both sides of downtown life. Executive Chef Nicco V.
