articles.originalSummary: The closure of Adam Byatt’s British bistro and the Government’s new funding package to tackle the decline of town centres are among this week’s top hospitality news stories. - Adam Byatt has closed his Clapham neighbourhood restaurant Bistro Union after almost 15 years. Located on Abbeville Road, a short walk from Byatt’s flagship Trinity, the restaurant opened in 2012 with a more casual British offer. The closure follows a relaunch in March, when Bistro Union brought back its original 2012 menu and prices in response to the rising cost of dining out in London. The ‘new old’ menu featured dishes including chicken Kyiv and toad in the hole, alongside bar snacks and daily specials. - The Government has announced a £210m funding package aimed at transforming vacant high street shops, pubs and clubs into shared workspaces, cafes and community hubs. The investment includes a new £125m Derelict Buildings Fund, which will support local authorities in bringing empty shopping centres, former cinemas and other long-vacant properties back into use as commercial and community assets. A further £65m will help communities acquire and revitalise local assets at risk of closure, including pubs, sports clubs and other community venues. The funding is intended to tackle the decline of town centres while supporting local economic growth and job creation.

articles.title: Mi Vida Cantina and Taqueria Opens in Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport
articles.titleKo: Mi Vida Cantina and Taqueria Opens in Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Travelers at Reagan National can now taste modern Mexican food at the new restaurant, Mi Vida Cantina and Taqueria in Concourse B. The highly anticipated establishment is locally praised for its genuine Mexican flavors and lively atmosphere. Mi Vida is open every day from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m., expanding the variety of dining choices available at DCA. Jaimini Erskine, vice president for marketing and concessions at the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority (MWAA), stated that “Mi Vida brings a true sense of place to Reagan National, giving travelers an opportunity to experience a beloved Washington-area Knead Hospitality brand right here at the airport. Partnerships such as these allow us to connect travelers with authentic local flavors while supporting businesses that contribute to the vibrancy of our region.” Close to Gate B16, this attractive open-air restaurant and bar serves modern interpretations of traditional Mexican dishes for breakfast and throughout the day until late hours, along with signature cocktails and convenient take-out. Dominic Troilo, Vice President of Fraport Washington Partnership LLC, the company which manages the concessions program, stated: “We have worked with MWAA, Jackmont Hospitality, and KNEAD Hospitality + Design to bring Chef Santibañez’s well-known Mexican restaurant to Reagan National,” and added that “the outcome is a modern dining option which provides vibrant flavors and extra convenience for travelers who want a taste of sunny Mexico while on the move.” Mi Vida offers a variety of flavor-filled dishes, starting with breakfast options until 10 a.m. These include Egg and Cheese tacos, Burrito Tejano, and Steak and Eggs. Starters include Tortilla Soup, Alitas, and Tatanachos. Chips and Salsa and hand-crushed Guacamole dishes come with house-made tortilla chips. Rice and beans come with the taco and enchilada plates, served two together. For main courses, you can choose burritos, Grilled Salmon Mestiza, and the Guajillo Smashburger. Popular sides are plantains, sweet potato fries, and Ana’s white rice with refried black beans. There are also vegetarian options. The full bar features 12 premium tequila brands, plus signature cocktails such as Margaritas, Piñada, and the Ponche de Lola. Simon Lorady, Vice President, Business Development & Brands for Jackmont Hospitality said: “We are incredibly grateful to KNEAD Hospitality + Design and Chef Roberto Santibañez for trusting Jackmont to bring the Mi Vida brand to life at Reagan National, and to MWAA, Fraport Washington and our ACDBE partner, Trans Air, for their partnership in making this opening possible.” Adding, “Jackmont has long been committed to bringing authentic, local and chef-driven dining experiences into airports while preserving the quality, identity and integrity that make those brands special. Mi Vida at DCA is a great example of what we believe is the next generation of airport dining — bringing a celebrated local restaurant into the airport in a way that feels authentic to the brand, relevant to the community and memorable for the traveler.” In 2025, nearly 25 million passengers traveled through Reagan National. Eight airlines served the airport, providing over 400 daily departures to 108 destinations. Playa Largo Resort & Spa, Autograph Collection, announces the return of Chef Brian Archibald as executive chef. In his role, Archibald will lead the resort’s culinary operations across its four dining concepts, private dining experiences, seasonal programming and banquet offerings. Archibald returns to Playa Largo with 27 years of food and beverage experience at luxury hotels and resorts across the country. He most recently served as executive chef of Hotel del Coronado in San Diego, where he led the culinary team across 12 food and beverage outlets, including Nobu, and helped guide the resort’s culinary evolution during its multimillion-dollar renovation. His career also includes leadership roles at The Boulders Resort & Spa, The Phoenician, JW Marriott Desert Ridge Resort & Spa, JW Marriott Camelback Inn Resort & Spa and Renaissance Phoenix Downtown Hotel. Archibald has worked alongside acclaimed chefs including Daniel Boulud, Gary Danko and Jeremiah Tower, and he was invited to cook at the James Beard House in 2008 and 2009. In 2017, he competed on Food Network’s “Beat Bobby Flay,” where he defeated Bobby Flay. Known for his ingredient-driven approach, Archibald blends Mediterranean flavors with classic French techniques. At Playa Largo, he will bring that perspective to the resort’s dining collection, including waterfront restaurant Sol by the Sea, Mediterranean-inspired La Marea, poolside Sand Bar and cocktail and ceviche destination Las Olas. “Returning to Playa Largo feels like coming home, and I’m excited to build on the resort’s culinary identity,” said Archibald. “The Florida Keys offer endless inspiration, from the local seafood to the relaxed energy of Key Largo. articles.title: How Hong Kong New Wave directors hijacked martial arts and crime films to make art
articles.titleKo: How Hong Kong New Wave directors hijacked martial arts and crime films to make art
articles.originalSummary: It is easy to misremember the Hong Kong New Wave of the late 1970s and 80s. Nearly five decades after its inception, that iconic chapter in the city’s cinema history is generally thought of as a socially inclined art-house movement that addressed everyday issues – a stark contrast to the martial arts films that dominated the local box office at the time. While partially true, viewing New Wave films merely as local iterations of 1960s and 70s rarefied European art-house cinema misses the mark....

articles.title: Slim Chickens to open first UK drive-thru
articles.titleKo: Slim Chickens to open first UK drive-thru
articles.originalSummary: Fried chicken brand Slim Chickens is joining the raft of QSR players moving into the drive-thru space. Boparan Restaurant Group, the brand’s UK master franchise partner, will open its first UK drive-thru at Broughton Shopping Park in Flintshire, Wales, this month and says it plans to use the site as a model for further drive-thru locations. The restaurant will serve the full Slim Chickens menu, including buttermilk-marinated chicken tenders that are hand-breaded to order, alongside wings, sandwiches, wraps and salads. The menu also includes hand-spun shakes, Texas Toast and 15 signature house sauces.

articles.title: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.titleKo: Tigermilk Brings Hacienda Grandeur to the Heart of East London
articles.originalSummary: Their modern South American inspired interior brings life to their largest site to dat e Following its successful opening in May, Tigermilk Spitalfields’s interior has emerged as one of the defining elements of the new flagship restaurant by Alexis and Nina Melikov, the group’s largest site to date. Designed by Studio Leche, Tigermilk’s in-house design studio, the space brings together hacienda-inspired architecture, layered materials and a warm, transportive atmosphere that has become central to the guest experience. Conceived as an escape in the heart of Spitalfields, the ambition was to build an environment that guests would immediately want to stay in, rather than one designed purely to be photographed. Central patios, generous proportions, fountains, handcrafted materials and lush greenery give the space its structure and soul, evoking the kind of environment that takes decades to settle into its surroundings. Antique furniture sits alongside bespoke pieces, and reclaimed terracotta, natural stone, marble and aged timber are used throughout, materials that carry history and wear it well. “People rarely talk about specific design features. They talk about the atmosphere,” adds Alexis. “If people leave believing the space possesses a history, then we have succeeded in creating something that feels authentic rather than constructed.” A considered selection of suppliers and craftspeople underpins the interior. Sogni and Pooky provide the lighting, Pierre Frey and Morris the fabrics and upholstery, and Mandarin Stone the marble and stone surfaces. Flexhouse – responsible for custom joinery, millwork and bespoke fabrication – also contributed to the furniture alongside vintage pieces and Leta, while Resources delivered the decorative wall finishes. Together they bring a layered quality to the space, as though each element has its own provenance and story. With its new 280-cover restaurant, hacienda-inspired interiors and striking luminescent bar stocked with more than 2700 bottles, Tigermilk Spitalfields invites guests into what feels like the brand’s thirteenth home. Through a considered interior scheme full of texture and attention to detail, the restaurant offers a transportive South American-inspired experience designed to engage every sense.

articles.title: House of Tides Heads South for a One-Night Takeover at Solaya Hoxton
articles.titleKo: House of Tides Heads South for a One-Night Takeover at Solaya Hoxton
articles.originalSummary: Solaya , the French Mediterranean restaurant and bar on the 25th floor of art’otel London Hoxton, is delighted to announce a one-night takeover by Kenny Atkinson’s Michelin-starred restaurant Newcastle’s historic Quayside, House of Tides , on Wednesday 7th October. For one evening, Solaya’s concept chef Kenny Atkinson and his House of Tides team will bring a taste of the restaurant’s signature dining experience down to London. Kenny will present a specially curated five-course tasting menu that carries the House of Tides style to the heart of the capital, with every dish built on exceptional seasonal ingredients, refined technique and the creativity that has kept House of Tides its Michelin star since 2015. Menu highlights include a Steamed Lindisfarne Oyster with Bonito Butter Sauce, Caviar and Walnut; Pan-Roasted Sea Bass with Cauliflower, Ajo Blanco, Pickled Grapes and Sea Herbs; and a Slow-Roasted Saddle of Highland Venison with Smoked Beetroot, Salsify and Blackberry, before a Dark Chocolate and Hazelnut Mousse to close. It is an exciting opportunity for Londoners to experience one of the most highly celebrated Northern restaurants, set against panoramic views of the capitals skyline. The five-course tasting menu is priced at £95 per person, with an optional wine pairing (£70/95) and a vegetarian menu available. Tickets are available via the link HERE .

articles.title: Sybron Announces B Corp™ Status
articles.titleKo: Sybron Announces B Corp™ Status
articles.originalSummary: Sybron, a leading supplier to some of the largest names in UK hospitality today announces its certification as a B Corporation (B Corp ), making the company the UK’s largest B Corp certified cleaning, hygiene & catering distributor. Certification as a B Corp sees Sybron join a growing movement of companies that are reinventing business for the benefit of all people and our shared planet. The achievement demonstrates that Sybron meets high standards of social and environmental performance, transparency and accountability, alongside a commitment to goals beyond shareholder value. “We are thrilled to announce that Sybron has achieved B Corp certification,” says Sybron’s sales & marketing director, George Mason. “We’re incredibly proud to join the global B Corp community, marking a major milestone in our journey. Achieving B Corp Certification reflects our commitment to building a business that creates a positive impact for our people, our customers, our communities and the planet.” This latest news follows the recent announcement of Sybron’s joint venture with B Corp-certified Lime Sustainable Supplies (LSS), a data-driven supply chain business, to bring unrivalled service, support and sustainability initiatives to the cleaning supplies market. As part of this, Sybron’s group head of ESG, Matt Burtinshaw says: “I very much look forward to leading the business’ sustainability and ESG strategy moving forward, building on the progress already made and helping create even greater measurable impact across the business and wider supply chain.” Sybron is now part of a growing community of over 10,000 businesses globally certified as B Corps. The B Corp community in the UK is the largest and fastest growing in the world, with over 2,600 companies spanning a range of different industries and sizes. “This is about much more than adding a certification to our name,” says George. “It’s about continuing to challenge ourselves, improve the way we do business and make sustainability a bigger part of how we operate every day. This achievement says so much about our loyal and talented team, as well as our clients and the industries we serve.” Verified by B Lab, the not-for-profit behind the B Corp movement, B Corp Certification assesses the entirety of a business’ operations and covers impact areas related to practices around governance, workers, community, the environment and customers. The certification process is rigorous, with companies required to provide evidence on performance while legally embedding their commitment to purpose as well as profit in their company articles. Chris Turner, CEO of B Lab UK, says: “We are delighted to welcome Sybron to the B Corp community. Its commitment to doing business differently will be an inspiration to others and will help spread the notion that success in business is as much about people and planet as it is profit.” Home

articles.title: Corinthia London – Destination Dining in the Heart of London
articles.titleKo: Corinthia London – Destination Dining in the Heart of London
articles.originalSummary: At the heart of Corinthia London ’s five-star hotel is a collection of acclaimed restaurants and bar spaces, making the landmark hotel on the corner of Whitehall Place a destination for dining and drinking. From relaxed all-day menus to named chef restaurants, Afternoon Tea and late-night cocktails, its culinary collection brings together celebrated names in British and Italian food and drink. From Afternoon Tea, served beneath the sparkling glow of a Baccarat-crystal chandelier at the Crystal Moon Lounge , and the flavours of Southern Italy at Francesco Mazzei ’s Mezzorgiorno , to Tom Kerridge ’s celebrated British cooking at Kerridge’s and Georgie’s Bar , Corinthia London offers a wealth of dining options under one roof. The Garden brings seasonal, British-inspired dining to the hotel’s internal, open-air courtyard, while The Northall Bar moves effortlessly from breakfast through to evening drinks and classic dishes. As night falls, Velvet by Salvatore Calabrese comes to life, bringing a sense of glamour and theatre, with story-led cocktails alongside signatures from the renowned drinks expert. Kerridge’s and Georgie’s Bar This September, Tom Kerridge has unveiled an exciting new chapter at the hotel, with the introduction of Georgie’s Bar, alongside a thoughtfully redesigned restaurant. Reopening in a more intimate setting, the restaurant will sit separately from the new bar, offering guests a fresh way to experience Tom Kerridge’s warm hospitality and comforting dishes at Corinthia London. At the helm of the kitchen is Head Chef Tom Childs, who has led in championing this ethos at Corinthia London since opening in 2018. At Georgie’s, a dedicated bar menu sits alongside cocktails, wines, beers and ales. At the centre is Georgie’s Martini Club , featuring a selection of Martinis: Dry, Wet and Dirty . Food at Georgie’s Bar follows the same straightforward approach, with familiar dishes designed as the ultimate drinks pairing. Snacks include Pork scratchings, Beef jerky and Frickles , and larger plates such as the Cheeseburger with BBQ brisket, Fish and Chips, and Haddock fritters. Mezzogiorno by Francesco Mazzei Inspired by the regions of Calabria, Puglia and Sicily, Mezzogiorno is the Italian restaurant from acclaimed chef Francesco Mazzei, who is celebrated for introducing ‘nduja to the UK. Showcasing seasonal produce and nostalgic flavours, the restaurant marries rustic tradition with modern elegance, reflecting Francesco’s childhood and his signature style of ‘mamma’s cooking with a chef’s hands’. Guests can sit kitchen-side and watch as his team makes pasta from scratch like Carbonara to Fettuccine al funghi e tartufo, alongside seafood dishes such as Guernsey pink bream and Steamed bass, served with the best of the season’s vegetables. To finish, indulge in Tiramisu served tableside and other Italian signatures, from a Neapolitan babà to a Summer panettone and a selection of Gelato’s Crystal Moon Lounge Afternoon Tea at Corinthia London is a sumptuous affair, served in the decadent surroundings of the Crystal Moon Lounge. Beneath the spectacular Baccarat-crystal chandelier, a silver trolley arrives laden with an enticing selection of sweet and savoury delicacies. The experience begins with finger sandwiches and freshly baked scones, accompanied by a selection of sparkling wines and Champagnes. An extensive tea menu completes the ritual, with seasonal infusions alongside classic Black, Green and Oolong blends. articles.title: Dalmoros Fresh Italian Celebrates National Pasta Month with Daily Deals
articles.titleKo: Dalmoros Fresh Italian Celebrates National Pasta Month with Daily Deals
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Pasta lovers, this month is for you! The popular, fast-casual, fresh pasta and Italian restaurant Dalmoros Fresh Italian is celebrating National Pasta Month throughout October with a month-long lineup of daily specials, seasonal offerings and celebrations at all of its locations, leading up to even more perks and surprises on National Pasta Day. Known for its fresh pastas and homemade sauces made from scratch with each meal uniquely served in to-go boxes and ready within minutes, along with delicious toppings, Italian-style sandwiches called Paninos, salads, garlic bread sticks, meatballs, tiramisu and more, Dalmoros is giving guests more reasons to indulge throughout October. This month, guests of Dalmoros Fresh Italian at all locations can enjoy the following daily specials: Meatball Monday: Free meatball (3 pc) add-on with any fresh pasta purchase Tasty Tuesday: BOGO fresh pasta with Sunday sauce or Alfredo; BOGO half sandwiches Midweek Amore: BOGO fresh pasta after 5pm Free Tiramisu Thursday: Free tiramisu with purchase of $22 or more Feel-Good Friday: Every 25 th customer surprised with a free meal Saucy Selfie Saturday: Post and tag a Dalmoros pasta photo or leave a review to earn loyalty points Sunday Supper: Kids receive free fresh pasta (half portion) after 5pm in-store Seasonal offerings Pumpkin Spice Tiramisu and Fresh Black Pasta are available all month at all locations too. Also new this October, Dalmoros is introducing half-size portions of its signature fresh pasta at all locations. Whether it’s a lighter lunch, a smaller craving or simply saving room for tiramisu, the new portion size adds another delicious and convenient option to the Dalmoros menu. The celebration gets even bigger on National Pasta Day, Saturday, October 17. Guests who sign up through Dalmoros revamped app will receive $5 off a future purchase, plus an additional 100 rewards points. Current members can also get in on the National Pasta Day perks by scanning a special code in-store to receive the additional 100 points. Surprise giveaways, including Dalmoros favorites like tiramisu and more are also planned throughout the day. Plus, in Tampa, National Pasta Day comes with another reason to celebrate. Dalmoros will mark the anniversary of its location at Armature Works with a special appearance by the brand’s beloved mascot, Tony Rigatoni. “National Pasta Month is the perfect opportunity for us to celebrate what Dalmoros is all about and have some fun with our guests along the way,” says David Caruso Jr., President of Dalmoros Fresh Italian. “Fresh pasta is at the heart of our brand, so we’re excited to make the entire month of October extra exciting with daily specials, our new half-size pasta portions and even more to celebrate on National Pasta Day. Whether you’re already a Dalmoros regular or trying us for the first time, we hope everyone comes out, has some fun, and, of course, enjoys some great pasta!” In addition, Dalmoros is gearing up for the exciting re-launch of its app and website, giving fresh pasta fans even more ways to get their pasta fix through online and app ordering while earning rewards and incentives. Expected to be available by National Pasta Day on October 17, the Dalmoros app is available for download through the Apple App Store, Google Play for Android, as well as through the Dalmoros website. Enjoy National Pasta Month and National Pasta Day all this month at all Dalmoros locations: Florida – Downtown St. Petersburg, Armature Works in Tampa, The Mall at Millenia in Orlando; Boston – CanalSide Food Hall, Faneuil Hall Marketplace/Quincy Market and South Station. (Jacksonville, Florida and additional locations in Midtown Manhattan, Texas Walmart Stores, Pentagon City Mall in DC and Philadelphia on the horizon are also scheduled to open in the remainder of 2026 and throughout 2027.) Potbelly, the iconic neighborhood sandwich shop known for its great food and good vibes, announced today the opening of a new location in Franconia, at The Festival at Manchester Lakes, the Southern Fairfax County shopping center just southwest of Washington, D.C. Opening on Wednesday, September 16, the new shop is anchored by major grocery and retail, as well as a diverse mix of family entertainment and popular dining options. Minutes from the Franconia-Springfield Metro Station and several of Northern Virginia’s major commuter routes, the shop is a perfect destination for local families, community organizations, professionals and businesses to enjoy the brand’s signature oven-toasted sandwiches and wraps, fresh salads, hand-dipped shakes and other craveable menu options. “We’re proud to bring Potbelly to The Festival at Manchester Lakes for everyone in Franconia and the surrounding communities to get their Potbelly fix. This is such a warm and welcoming neighborhood, which makes it a natural fit for us,” said Ebou Jagne, Regional Director at Potbelly. “Potbelly is built on bringing people together over great food and good vibes. We know longtime fans and new Potbelly guests will appreciate the shop’s signature friendly service, craveable food and neighborhood atmosphere that the DMV has always loved.” The Festival at Manchester Lakes shop joins more than four dozen locations in the Washington D.C. metro area. To celebrate the opening, Potbelly will host a celebration on Saturday, October 3, from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. The first 50 guests in line at the Grand Opening will receive Free Potbelly for a Year. Guests can also enjoy a lively celebration, including a ribbon cutting, Potbelly Perks Plinko game for chances to win exclusive merchandise, free food and other prizes. The Franconia shop will offer convenient options for lunch, dinner and everything in between. Regular operating hours are 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Delivery, order ahead and catering are available in-shop, through Potbelly.com and in the Potbelly App, with third-party delivery services also available. For exclusive offers and rewards, Potbelly invites guests to join the Potbelly Perks program, where members can unlock free sandwiches, cookies and special offers throughout the year. articles.title: Davis Fresh-Mex Named Pancheros Franchisee of the Year for Second Time
articles.titleKo: Davis Fresh-Mex Named Pancheros Franchisee of the Year for Second Time
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Pancheros Mexican Grill—the Iowa-based fresh-Mex brand known for its Burritos Better Built, creamy queso and fresh-pressed tortillas—is celebrating Davis Fresh-Mex as its 2026 Franchisee of the Year, marking the group’s second time receiving the honor in just three years. Led by industry veteran Dick Davis, his son, Joseph Davis and their operating partner, Kim Schoening, Davis Fresh-Mex is a top-performing, multi-unit Pancheros franchisee and the exclusive operator of all Pancheros restaurants throughout Missouri. The award, which was presented during Pancheros’ annual Franchise Conference, recognizes the team’s commitment to operational excellence, the guest experience and continued growth of the brand. A longtime franchise operator with previous experience with Taco Bell, KFC and Huddle House, Dick Davis joined the Pancheros franchise system in 2023, acquiring all four existing restaurants in the Missouri market. Since then, he has continued creating strong guest experiences and growing the business alongside his partners Joseph and Kim. Today, Davis Fresh-Mex has expanded to now operate seven restaurants across Missouri, with three new locations opening in Rolla, Springfield and most recently, Lebanon, MO in the past 18 months alone. Together, the team has continued to build on the foundation established in 2023 while expanding Pancheros’ presence in key communities across the state. “Davis Fresh-Mex has continued to raise the bar for what strong franchise leadership looks like,” said Rodney Anderson, President and Founder of Pancheros. “Dick has built a team that knows how to take care of its guests while creating successful restaurants that are engaged in the community. Their growth over the past year has been impressive, and we are excited to recognize them as our Franchisee of the Year for the second time and celebrate the impact they continue to make on the Pancheros brand.” In 2026, the Davis Fresh-Mex restaurants delivered strong results across several key areas, including +8.8% sales growth and +28.04% in digital sales across all seven restaurants, as well as a staggering top restaurant sales growth at +20.39%. Separately, compared to the system average of a 26.06% loyalty participation rate, Davis Fresh-Mex is seeing a 31.10% rate across their entire restaurant portfolio. Davis Fresh-Mex has also implemented second-make lines to improve operational efficiencies and support digital sales growth at all locations. Additionally, as Missouri State University alumni, the Davises are proud supporters of local campuses and university athletics programs in all their Missouri communities. These results highlight the factors powering Dick and his team’s continued growth throughout Missouri and the team’s focus on delivering a strong experience for Pancheros guests. “We’re incredibly proud to be named Pancheros’ Franchisee of the Year for a second time,” said Dick Davis. “This recognition reflects the hard work and dedication of our entire team, especially our operations team, who work every day to keep our restaurants running at their best. Since joining Pancheros, we have seen great opportunity to grow the brand in Missouri, and we’ve always believed in the brand and the experience it delivers to our guests. I’m so proud of what we have and will continue to accomplish together.” Beyond the success of their restaurants, Davis Fresh-Mex continues to strengthen Pancheros’ presence in communities across Missouri. Davis and his team have remained active in supporting their communities, with an emphasis on building local connections and growing catering opportunities for Pancheros. As their portfolio continues to grow, the group remains focused on building strong relationships within the community while bringing the simple and delicious Pancheros experience to more Missourians than ever before. articles.title: Star Burger Becomes Official Burger of Miami Hurricanes Sports
articles.titleKo: Star Burger Becomes Official Burger of Miami Hurricanes Sports
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Star Burger, located at 4901 SW Eighth St., has entered into a partnership with the University of Miami Athletics as the Official Burger of the Miami Hurricanes, a title that covers all the university’s sports teams. The Canes Burger is double-stacked, made with 100% U.S. grass-fed and grass-finished beef patties, smashed to order, and then topped with aged Cheddar cheese, a crunchy tostón round, and Star Burger’s signature Cat 5 Sauce. All served on Martin’s potato buns, toasted to perfection. It pairs with the restaurant’s signature fries or Dillies, both fried exclusively in natural beef tallow for that unmistakable, healthier flavor. The Canes Burger was created with input from one of the Hurricanes’ own stars, Malachi Toney, who gave it his approval. It was designed to represent University of Miami Athletics in its own colors, and it wears them well. Star Burger’s Cat 5 pesto brings the deep green, and the crunchy tostón round the bright golden orange. Stacked together on the bun, the burger comes out of the kitchen in full Hurricanes colors. Each topping was chosen for the partnership. “We wanted Miami Athletics and the Estrella family to come through in the flavors, with the American cheddar for UM and Cuban plantains for the family,” said Gianluca Piccolo, general manager of Star Burger. “The idea for pesto sauce came from my own Italian roots, and it ties all the flavors together.” The partnership makes Star Burger the Official Burger of Miami Hurricanes Athletics for the 2026-2027 season, the restaurant’s first tie to the university. It comes less than two months after Star Burger opened its doors on Southwest Eighth Street, just minutes from campus. The Canes Burger is a permanent menu item, not a limited run tied to the season. “We built this one to stay,” said Joey Estrella, president of Star Burger. “Partnering with University of Miami Athletics is an honor for our family, and we wanted to give it something more than a name on a menu board. This burger will be here long after the season ends.” Since the burger went on the menu, customers have been ordering it by name. “We have people come in every day, asking for the Canes Burger,” Piccolo said. “The sauce is different from anything else on the menu, and they want to try it.” This season guests can order one with the game on. Star Burger will be broadcasting Miami Hurricanes football games LIVE all season long. Fans are welcome to stop in, try the burger, and cheer on The “U” with fellow Canes fans. articles.title: The Boiling Crab to Raise Funds for Pediatric Cancer Research
articles.titleKo: The Boiling Crab to Raise Funds for Pediatric Cancer Research
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Boiling Crab, the nation’s go-to destination for Louisiana-style Cajun seafood boils, is turning its dining rooms into fundraising engines for pediatric cancer research once again. Now in its third consecutive year, the seafood chain is teaming up with the National Pediatric Cancer Foundation (NPCF) throughout Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, aiming to build on the more than $160,000 the partnership raised together last year. “The Boiling Crab has always been a family establishment, so this cause is dear and true to our hearts. Watching our guests rally behind it last year reminded us why we do what we do,” said Dada Ngo, Co-founder of The Boiling Crab. “We’re glad to be back at the table with NPCF this year.” The need remains significant. Cancer is still the leading cause of death by disease among children in the United States, with an estimated 43 kids a day expected to be diagnosed in 2026 alone, according to NPCF. Research has moved survival rates in the right direction, from about 58% in the mid-1970s to 85% today, but partnerships like this one are what keep that number climbing. From September 14 through October 11, a portion of proceeds from select menu items, including boiled shrimp and crawfish, will go directly toward NPCF’s research programs. Guests can take part simply by dining in or ordering takeout. “The Boiling Crab has been in this fight with us for three years now, and that kind of sustained commitment is rare,” said David Frazer, CEO of the National Pediatric Cancer Foundation. “It’s exactly the kind of long-term partnership that moves pediatric cancer research forward. We’re proud of what we’ve built together, and we’re far from done.” This Year’s Campaign at a Glance Dates: September 14 through October 11, 2026, aligned with Childhood Cancer Awareness Month In-restaurant experience: Coloring placemats for families, stickers, and bibs, featuring designs by RIF LA, plus a direct link to NPCF’s donation page. T-shirts for purchase. Where It Goes NPCF puts approximately 89 cents of every dollar donated directly toward clinical research trials and treatment. The Boiling Crab invites guests to grab a bib, dig into a boil, and help fund research that gives kids fighting cancer a better shot at tomorrow. Visit TheBoilingCrab.com to find a location, and NationalPCF.org to learn more about NPCF’s work. Bad Daddy’s Burger Bar is taking over the deli counter and bringing the best of autumn in the latest installment of its Big Bad Monthly Drop series. Available Oct. 1-31, The Deli Stackhouse brings together the savory, tangy flavors of a classic deli sandwich with the over-the-top build the brand’s scratch kitchen is known for. Built on a pressed brioche bun, The Deli Stackhouse starts with a layer of deli mustard under a smash patty and melted Swiss, then piles on hot pastrami and another layer of Swiss. Sauerkraut and Russian dressing finish the stack, bringing a mix of rich and salty flavors to every bite. “The Deli Stackhouse is a fun way to bring some classic deli flavors into the Bad Daddy’s lineup,” said John Masterson, culinary director for Bad Daddy’s Burger Bar. “The pastrami and Swiss give you that familiar foundation, while the sauerkraut, Russian dressing and deli mustard bring the punch that makes the whole thing work. In all other locations, a $6 tall of Angry Orchard offers a crisp, refreshing complement to the burger’s rich flavors. Cinnamon Toast Crunch Iced Coffee and Donut Bites are all available now at participating Bojangles locations. Bojangles is kicking off the fall season with the launch of two new menu additions: Cinnamon Toast Crunch Iced Coffee and Donut Bites. Rounding out the fall lineup, Bojangles also is bringing back one of its most requested breakfast items, the Pork Chop Griller, now available all day at participating locations. Prepared in-house using a smooth, medium roast cold brew, the new Cinnamon Toast Crunch Iced Coffee is served over ice with sweet cream and Cinnamon Toast Crunch syrup for a nostalgic, seasonal flavor. It builds on the iced coffee platform Bojangles introduced earlier this year, giving fans a new way to enjoy their coffee break any time of day. Pairing perfectly with the new coffee is the brand’s Donut Bites, made with real buttermilk biscuit dough, fried crispy, tossed in sugar and served with salted caramel sauce for dipping. The new treat gives Bojangles’ scratch-made biscuit dough a sweet, snackable spin, and is available in six-piece and 12-piece sizes. For fans craving something heartier, the Pork Chop Griller hits the spot. The fan favorite features a tender pork chop, marinated and seared to perfection and served on a made-from-scratch buttermilk biscuit. Made the Bojangles way with the brand’s signature 49-step scratch-made biscuit and available all day, guests can grab one for breakfast, lunch or anytime the craving hits this season. “Now that we’re officially into the Fall season, we’re celebrating the harvest months our way, with the classic flavors of cinnamon, sugar and salted caramel,” said Marshall Scarborough, Vice President of Menu and Culinary Innovation at Bojangles. “Our Cinnamon Toast Crunch Iced Coffee makes the perfect complement to any of our breakfast sandwiches, or a tasty afternoon treat. The Donut Bites dipped in the salted caramel has just the right amount of sweet butter milky caramel goodness that will make you forget all about the pumpkins.” The Pork Chop Griller, Cinnamon Toast Crunch Iced Coffee and Donut Bites are all available now at participating Bojangles locations, while supplies last. articles.title: honeygrow to Celebrate National Noodle Day with Buy-One-Get-One-Free Stir-Fry
articles.titleKo: honeygrow to Celebrate National Noodle Day with Buy-One-Get-One-Free Stir-Fry
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . National Noodle Day is October 6. honeygrow isn’t waiting. The Philadelphia-born fast-casual restaurant known for its freshly cooked-to-order stir-fry is kicking off a week-long celebration of all things Noods, with hidden gift cards, surprise Nood Drops, limited-edition merch, citywide scavenger hunts and Big Nood, honeygrow’s larger-than-life walking stir-fry, roaming the streets of Philadelphia. It all leads to October 6, when honeygrow Rewards members at all honeygrow locations can buy one stir-fry and get one free, all day long. Because great Noods should be shared. “National Noodle Day gives us an excuse to go completely overboard celebrating something that’s been at the heart of honeygrow since day one,” said Justin Rosenberg, founder and CEO of honeygrow. “We cook our noodles fresh to order every day, so we’re turning one day into an entire week. We’re dropping Noods, hiding Noods, sharing Noods and, on October 6, giving people more Noods. Because great Noods should be shared.” THE NOOD LINEUP: September 30: Nood Week Begins The first Nood Drops hit, kicking off a week of giveaways, limited-edition merch, surprises and more. September 30 – October 5: The Great Nood Hunt honeygrow will be hiding prizes across Philadelphia, Washington D.C., Boston, Cleveland and other honeygrow markets. Clues will drop through @honeygrow on Instagram and TikTok. Find the Noods. Keep the goods. October 6: National Noodle Day honeygrow Rewards members can buy one stir-fry and get one free all day on October 6. Not a Rewards member? Fans can sign up at honeygrow.com or through the honeygrow app. October 6: The Nood Party – Philadelphia honeygrow’s UPenn location will become Nood headquarters with photo ops, merch drops, giveaways and more. And somewhere on the streets of Philadelphia, keep an eye out for Big Nood, honeygrow’s larger-than-life walking stir-fry. HOW DOES AMERICA NOOD? Saucy in Philly. Spicy in New York. Crunchy in the Midwest. To celebrate National Noodle Day, honeygrow analyzed ordering behavior across its 80+ restaurants to create the first-ever National Noodle Index, revealing how noodle preferences differ from region to region. Greater Philly leads all honeygrow regions in extra sauce requests, with 12% of orders getting saucier, while 5% of Greater New York/New Jersey orders add spicy toppings and 35% of Midwest orders include crispy toppings. The full National Noodle Index, including the regions with the Biggest Nood Energy, Most Extra Noods, Meatiest Noods and Late Night Noods, is available at honeygrow.com/noods. articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Taco Bell has a history of making more of National Taco Day. Turns out, “taco” needs no translation. The word remains nearly the same across more than 30 languages, a common thread, all for the love of tacos. Spanish? Taco. French? Taco. German? Taco. Japanese? タコス (Takosu). Hindi? टैको (Taiko). This National Global Taco Day, October 6, Taco Bell and Duolingo are putting that universal language to work, taking the annual celebration global for the first time ever and calling on taco fans around the world to go all out in the name of taco. Global Taco Day kicks off with an all-new, limited-edition Duo Habanero Sauce, taco-fueled language lessons, and plenty of Duo-fueled fun, including a Duolingo x Taco Bell restaurant takeover in New York City and fans may see Duo in surprising places around the world. “National Taco Day is about more than just food. It’s about the shared love of tacos and the connections they create between people. This year, we’re taking that love global,” said Luis Restrepo, Chief Marketing Officer, Taco Bell North America. “The fact that ‘taco’ is understood in more than 30 languages proves just how universal it is, and together with Duolingo, we’re turning that shared language into an invitation for even more fans to join the Global Taco Day celebration.” Duo Enters His Habanero Era Introducing Duo Habanero Sauce, an all-new, limited-time sauce created exclusively for the Taco Bell x Duolingo collaboration. Bright and tangy with fruity notes and a kick of habanero heat, the sauce delivers a vibrant balance of flavor and spice that builds with every bite. Bold enough to match its namesake, Duo Habanero isn’t one to go unnoticed. And because no Taco Bell sauce packet is complete without a little wisdom, Duo Habanero is getting multilingual. The limited-edition packets bring Duo’s language-learning world to Taco Bell’s iconic sauce wisdoms with taco-inspired sayings across nine languages, including English, Spanish, French, Hindi, Portuguese, German, Korean, Mandarin, and Japanese. Internationally, packet assortments will reflect the native language and some of the most popular languages Duolingo users are learning in each participating market. Every packet is a reminder that the love of tacos is universal. Duo Habanero launches October 6 at participating Taco Bell restaurants across the U.S., Canada, Australia, China, India, Spain and the UK, while supplies last. U.S. fans can score one free Duo Habanero Sauce packet with the purchase of a Doritos Locos Taco, with additional packets available à la carte for $0.20 each*. Internationally, fans can score free Duo Habanero Sauce through participating Global Taco Day offers at Taco Bell restaurants in Canada, Australia, China, India, Spain and the UK, with offers varying by market*, while supplies last. “Language and food are two of the most powerful ways we connect with culture and with each other,” said Emmanuel Orssaud, Chief Marketing Officer, Duolingo. “Taco is a rare word that travels easily across cultures, making it a fun starting point for getting people curious about language.” More Ways to Speak Taco Duo Habanero is only one way fans can get in on the global celebration. Taco Bell and Duolingo are giving fans even more ways and reasons to say taco this Global Taco Day, whether they’re keeping their streak alive, trying the new Duo Habanero sauce or getting their hands on Duo’s latest look with the Duolingo x Taco Bell plushie. Keep the streak going on us: From October 1 through October 6, Taco Bell Rewards Members can unlock one month of Super Duolingo for free, giving fans even more reason to keep learning the love language of tacos and beyond. articles.title: Marco’s Pizza Brings Back Large Margherita Magnifico Pizza
articles.titleKo: Marco’s Pizza Brings Back Large Margherita Magnifico Pizza
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . The Margherita Magnifico is available for a limited time while supplies last at participating Marco’s Pizza locations nationwide. Marco’s Pizza brings back its large Margherita Magnifico pizza for a limited time, available beginning today for $12.99*. Featuring thick slices of fresh mozzarella, Roma tomatoes sliced in-store and Marco’s signature basil drizzle, the Margherita Magnifico proves that simple does not mean settling for less. When a pizza is built from only a few ingredients, every choice matters, from how each ingredient is sourced to the flavor it brings to every slice. Chef Kathleen Kennedy, Director of Culinary Innovation for Marco’s Pizza, set out to create a Margherita she would be proud to serve friends and family, guided by three principles: Select ingredients that deliver bright, fresh flavor. Source carefully to meet Marco’s quality specifications. Create a pizza that is unmistakably Marco’s. The result begins with dough made fresh in-store daily and proofed for at least 18 hours to develop deeper flavor before being hand-stretched into a thinner crust. It is topped with Marco’s signature sauce, thick slices of fresh mozzarella and a shredded three-cheese blend. Next, extra-large, perfectly ripened Roma tomatoes sliced in-store are carefully placed around the pizza between the fresh mozzarella. Finally, the pizza is finished with Marco’s signature basil drizzle, made from fresh chopped basil. This first-or second-cut basil is grown specially for Marco’s in California’s Central Valley, then chopped and transformed into the drizzle shortly after harvest to deliver a fresh, bright burst of basil flavor on every slice. The crust is topped with garlic sauce and the pizza is sprinkled with romesan seasoning – a finish that is distinctively Marco’s. “I have to say that, as a chef, I cannot make a better pizza at home,” said Chef Kennedy. “We tried more than 20 different recipes and carefully selected every ingredient to ensure our Margherita tasted fresh and delicious. What I am most proud of is our signature basil drizzle. I like to call it a magic basil elixir.” The Margherita Magnifico reflects Marco’s belief that simplicity is not the absence of something. It is confidence that nothing else is needed. On a pizza this simple, the quality of each ingredient comes through, which is why each one is selected with intention and prepared with care. That same simplicity carries through to the guest experience. Guests feeding a family between school and practice, picking up dinner on the way home, or settling in for a relaxing evening should not have to sacrifice freshness, convenience, or value. “We live in a world where more is often mistaken for better, but the Margherita Magnifico takes a different approach,” said Steve Kennedy, Chief Marketing Officer for Marco’s Pizza. “It brings together quality, convenience, and value through a few thoughtfully selected ingredients. When every choice is made with care, nothing else is needed. That is simplicity at its finest.” For a closer look at the care behind each ingredient and the choices that make the Margherita Magnifico distinctively Marco’s, viewers can go behind the scenes with Chef Kathleen on Marco’s Pizza’s YouTube channel. The Margherita Magnifico is available for a limited time while supplies last at participating Marco’s Pizza locations nationwide. Guests can find their nearest location and more information at marcos.com or through the Marco’s Pizza app. The post Marco’s Pizza Brings Back Large Margherita Magnifico Pizza appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Kubbly Launches Preview Tool for Branded RCS Marketing

articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Kubbly launched RCS Brand Preview at rcs.kubbly.com , helping marketers see how they can engage their customers with branded, interactive RCS messages instead of sending generic SMS texts. Marketers paste their brand’s public website URL and sign in to see a preview of RCS marketing on their own phone in under five minutes. RCS is an upgrade to SMS that supports recognizable branding, rich media, and buttons. Kubbly powers RCS marketing with two-way conversations, turning messaging apps into a direct channel for ordering and booking. RCS Brand Preview gives marketers a first look at how Kubbly helps bring existing customers back by building on brand equity and acting on customer signals quickly. Marketing teams already have customer data and campaign ideas, but it often takes too long to turn those signals into relevant campaigns. For franchise and enterprise brands, back-and-forth between corporate and local teams adds more delay. By the time messages reach customers, they are no longer relevant or, worse, feel like spam. By reducing manual campaign work and using advances in business messaging such as RCS, Kubbly helps teams send timely, branded messages that build trust and drive repeat visits, purchases, and bookings. Kubbly can deliver approved campaigns through RCS, where customers can recognize the brand and respond. Across connected messaging channels such as Apple Messages, Google Messages, and WhatsApp, Kubbly agents can answer questions. When the required workflow is connected, they can also help complete orders, bookings, or support requests. Recorded outcomes help guide the next retention decision. “A customer who already knows your brand shouldn’t feel like they’re hearing from a stranger. They should recognize you and have a reason to respond,” said Piyush Jain, CEO of Kubbly. “We built RCS Brand Preview so marketers can experience what it would mean to have a brand that their customers trust like they trust a friend.” The post Kubbly Launches Preview Tool for Branded RCS Marketing appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Stoke Park To Enter A New Chapter This Autumn
articles.titleKo: Stoke Park To Enter A New Chapter This Autumn
articles.originalSummary: Stoke Park, the historic 300-acre Buckinghamshire estate that is regarded as the UK’s first country club, is embarking on a new phase in its journey from autumn 2026. The news follows the estate’s acquisition by Reliance Industries Limited in 2021 and comes after a period of integral renovation and restoration. Stoke Park’s new dining offering will launch in October. Chef Tom Sellers has created a collection of five dining and drinking spaces for this landmark chapter in the estate’s history, working alongside chefs Dom Robinson and Tom Phillips and HiStory Hospitality – the creative force behind the two-Michelin starred Restaurant Story in London. The estate’s wine cellar has been curated by Carolina Seibel, Group Head of Beverage at HiStory Hospitality, and the estate’s bar and cocktail offerings by Giuseppe Masala, Beverage Manager. The Penn , named after John Penn, will be the estate’s new flagship restaurant, with a 48-cover dining room and private dining room seating eight. The Penn will serve an à la carte menu shaped by British culinary history, seasonality, provenance and classical French technique. Dishes will include terrine of spiced pig’s head with Scottish langoustine, roast wild sea bass with Orkney scallop, fish of the day en papillote, and venison Wellington Rossini. Produce from the Stoke Park Kitchen Garden, led by former Head Gardener of Le Manoir aux Quat’Saisons, Kate Mannery, will inform the menu as the seasons change. Alongside The Penn, the estate will introduce a range of social concepts for every occasion, from formal to informal. These will include The Piano Bar , The Terrace & Glasshouse, The Tea Room and The Clubhouse. The Piano Bar will focus on classic cocktails, including an elevated martini selection, alongside 100 Hills English sparkling wine and a list with a strong representation of American wines. The Terrace & Glasshouse will bring a lighter, more informal food style to the estate with dishes including sourdough flatbread with wildflowers and herbs, seasonal salads, rigatoni with venison ragu, and fish of the day. A casual offering including pizzas and barbecue will be served on the terrace. The Terrace & Glasshouse will open each spring and summer with private hire available throughout the year. The Tea Room will offer teas, coffees and a selection of freshly baked viennoiserie, a tart of the day using estate fruit, and signature Stoke Park scones. The Clubhouse will be open daily serving a menu of pub classics alongside Indian cuisine. articles.title: Unifocus Unveils New AI-Powered Capabilities to Enhance Performance Visibility for Hotels
articles.titleKo: Unifocus Unveils New AI-Powered Capabilities to Enhance Performance Visibility for Hotels
articles.originalSummary: New corporate analytics, a unified operations experience, enhanced Inspection capabilities, and AI-powered labour insights give hotel groups greater visibility and enable faster decisions to improve performance across their portfolios. Hotel groups are under increasing pressure to standardize quality across properties while reducing operational costs. Yet, their technology stack remains fragmented at the property level, giving hoteliers limited visibility into what is happening across their portfolio. Today, Unifocus, the global leader in hospitality workforce management technology, announced a series of enhancements across its workforce management and operations suites. These enhancements extend the platform from property-level operations to portfolio-wide visibility and bring AI-driven insight to enable hoteliers to executive day to day operations more efficiently. Unifocus specializes in end-to-end workforce management and operations, connecting labour planning, scheduling, time and attendance, and hotel operations. By modernizing and streamlining these processes, Unifocus equips teams with an integrated approach that creates more visibility for business leaders, better working environments for staff and, in turn, a better experience for guests. The enhancements include: Corporate Operations analytics dashboard: Hotel groups can now gain a single, portfolio-wide view of operational performance across the Maintenance, Housekeeping, Inspection, Service, and Glitch modules. This allows corporate and regional leaders to benchmark one property against another, achieving full visibility and easy comparison across all properties. Enhanced reporting and a unified operations experience: Operational workflows now come together in a single application, the Unifocus Operations App, so frontline teams no longer need to switch between separate tools to see assigned tasks. Housekeeping, maintenance, service, glitch, and inspection sit in one place, reducing friction, simplifying training, and giving managers clearer visibility into performance. New reporting capabilities allow that activity to turn into insight leaders can action. AI-powered labour insights: AI interprets labour variance for leaders, pinpointing the root cause behind it and classifying each issue as a cost, quality overtime, operational, productivity, or forecast risk, then recommending specific actions most likely to improve the outcome. This intelligent analysis gives leaders forward-looking visibility into labour performance and helps identify risks earlier and improve decisions across the business. A redesigned home screen in Unifocus Workforce Management brings the most important labour, schedule, and operational signals together the moment a user logs in, answering a single question: what needs my attention right now. Enhanced Inspection capabilities: A redesigned Inspection experience introduces standardized templates, weighted scoring that separates critical standards from minor issues, richer analytics, collaborative multi-user inspections, and improved auditability. “Our customers are managing tighter margins and higher guest expectations than ever, and they need technology that helps them confidently and proactively take action to keep business on track,” said John Lockyer, CEO of Unifocus. “These enhancements bring AI-driven insight to solutions hoteliers already trust, built on more than 25 years of hospitality insight and expertise. This is not about doing more with fewer people. It is about giving teams the clarity to deliver the best possible guest experience with the people they have, while better managing the two largest cost lines in any hotel: labour and operations.” The enhancements reflect a broader investment across the Unifocus portfolio. The most memorable restaurant experiences often are rooted in recognition, in the small signals that tell a guest this place knows them. “The best hospitality is personal,” says Brittany Baldwin, CMO of Upward Projects, a Phoenix-based restaurant group. “It’s a great bartender who remembers what you drink or a great server who knows that you like to sit on the patio.” That idea is central to Upward Projects, which specializes in adapting historically significant or architecturally distinctive buildings for new restaurant lives. Its largest and most prominent flagship, Postino, began in a historic 1940s-era Arizona post office. Twenty-five years later, the neighborhood wine bar chain has more than 30 locations across seven states, built around wine spanning a bevy of varietals, beer and cocktails, and an eclectic menu of snacks, soups, salads, paninis, and a dozen kinds of bruschetta. This summer, Postino marked its 25th anniversary with the Postino Pass, a complimentary, digital-first membership program intended to make that recognition more scalable without making it feel automated. A short, playful “get to know you” quiz informs spontaneous, tailored treats delivered directly to members’ phone wallets. The pass lives in that digital wallet and unlocks surprises throughout the year, from wine-bottle upgrades to special bites. The distinction is intentional. Rather than relying on the familiar “spend X, get Y” equation, Postino organizes the program around occasions and lifestyles. Think date nights, catching up with friends, trying something new, or bringing a dog to the patio. The goal is to reflect the ways people actually use the brand, rather than force them into a points-driven transaction. “It’s not about loyalty,” Baldwin says. “It’s about personalization and hospitality.” For Baldwin, that framing responds to a wider paradox facing restaurants. Brands have access to an expanding pool of signals—mobile data, credit card data, behavioral information from demographic and data-platform partners. The opportunity is not simply to use those inputs to accelerate a transaction or amplify a promotion, but to make an interaction more considerate. It also arrives as guests show renewed interest in experiences that feel “analog, handcrafted, and one-of-one” rather than algorithmically produced. “There’s a fundamental difference between broadcasting mass marketing and a one-to-one interaction where you say, ‘Okay, this person likes Chardonnay. We’re going to talk to them about a new Chardonnay Blanc they’d really enjoy exploring and tell them the story behind that winery,’” Baldwin says. “That feels hospitable. That makes someone feel seen.” The Postino Pass is the outcome of a broader two-year digital transformation led by director of digital Ellie Ovsenik. Before that work, the company’s view of a guest was fragmented. Different systems held different angles, complicating efforts to create a coherent engagement strategy. “We knew we needed to have a tech stack that was modular and would scale with us,” Baldwin says. “But we also needed to have a central view of the guest, versus different angles of the guest through disparate systems.” Postino rebuilt toward that central view with a more integrated tech stack. A centralized CRM consolidated guest data and enabled more sophisticated lifecycle communications, while an offer-management platform organized the perks and benefits behind Postino Pass. Guest analytics tools gave the team a clearer read on behavior, visit frequency, and lifetime value, including the traits of its most engaged guests. articles.title: How BJ’s Restaurants is Building a Better Business Over Time
articles.titleKo: How BJ’s Restaurants is Building a Better Business Over Time
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . BJ’s Restaurants CEO Lyle Tick has observed today’s customer dynamic unfolding through a couple of avenues. If you look at the endless string of data reports on the subject, you’d assume, understandably, the diner was under some degree of stress. He views what’s taking shape differently, however: One, is what Tick refers to as “durable and disposable transactions.” The kind of traffic a brand like BJ’s, and other casual-dining chains, competes for falls under this distinction. Or, “the social splurge space.” “Whether it’s the weekly, a couple of times a month, I’m going out with friends. I’m going out with family. It’s an experience-based thing. And I think people protect those things,” Tick said during the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference. “Disposable transactions” are occasions more like weekday lunch or grabbing a quick dinner on the way home. Customers, he said, tend to shed such visits in favor of guarding their social trips. “And so, that’s where we compete,” Tick said. “That’s where we do well. And I think that’s potentially a dynamic why we’re doing well.” It’s a present landscape, he continued, favoring some of BJ’s peers (like Chili’s) where a spread of winners and losers has formed among full-service chains; a time where consumers, when they do decide to open their wallets, are prioritizing a great exchange for their dollars. The brands thriving, Tick said, are those investing in their value proposition holistically. “Their product, their service, their atmosphere, and making sure they have a place where their team members and their guests want to be,” he said. “And those folks are winning more. I think, thankfully, over the past couple of years, we’ve made pretty significant progress across those areas.” This larger macro picture might be fueling BJ’s, but it’s merely a piece of much-larger jigsaw for a brand coming off one of its best periods in years. The chain posted same-store sales growth of 6.5 percent in Q2 as traffic leapt 8.3 percent. It marked BJ’s eighth consecutive run of comps and traffic growth and the loftiest comps bump in three years and highest traffic in four. Mother’s and Father’s Day sales spiked north of 8 and 3 percent, respectively, year-over-year, and more than 80 stores broke daily or weekly records. And regarding Tick’s notion of a pressured consumer, BJ’s didn’t feel it—it notched growth through all geographies, dayparts, and channels. Sales increases were evenly distributed across the week as well. Again, he feels guests are simply doing what they have to so they can socialize and indulge. BJ’s is there to fill that need-state when it arises. And in recent quarters, as Tick, who was named CEO last June after serving as president and chief concept officer (he was formerly brand president of Buffalo Wild Wings from 2018 to 2023), kept sharing industry-fronting results with investors, he was often asked to compartmentalize BJ’s success. Bj’s has been on a sales and traffic run. In other terms, was there one thing driving the surge? That’s a byproduct of life on Wall Street, where analysts value quarter-to-quarter recaps as much as long strips of growth. Tick said, from his view, it doesn’t quite work that way. BJ’s doesn’t have a “one thing” to explain its upturn. Over the past two years, it’s been a combination of foundation-setting plans alongside marketable wins, starting with operations. Pillar fixes showed in guest and employee metrics, Tick said. BJ’s then followed by unlocking “the power of the Pizookie,” building an everyday value platform, improving product—beginning with pizza—and moving through burgers and its chicken sandwich. Also, “putting a fair bit” of money back into facilities and driving BJ’s remodel program. articles.title: The 2026 QSR® Drive-Thru Report
articles.titleKo: The 2026 QSR® Drive-Thru Report
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . For years, “the drive-thru of the future” was a physical asset story, explains Dane Mathews, Taco Bell’s global chief digital and technology officer. More lanes. More screens. More automation. But is that where innovation is leading fast-food’s most enduring channel? It’s not a simple answer, yet the end goal is the consumer thinking it is. “The next evolution runs on intelligence, but intelligence isn’t the story,” Mathews says. “Intelligence is table stakes, not the breakthrough. The breakthrough is turning that intelligence into a real brand conversation with our fans.” Over the past few QSR Drive-Thru Reports, our data partner, Intouch Insight, has begun to mystery shop a shifting lexicon of success. To Mathews’ point, it originally meant finding a crop of fresh prototypes ideated out of contactless COVID trends—including a Taco Bell “Defy” concept with two stories and chutes that dropped food down to guests. Chick-fil-A built a four-lane, double-decker model itself. And brands from Burger King to McDonald’s started tweaking sites to include additional lanes as capacity soared, refreshed ordering technology that centered on accuracy, and sprinkles of AI, either directly facing the consumer, or behind the curtain with employees. MORE DRIVE-THRU COVERAGE: Download Intouch Insight’s full guide to the Drive-Thru Report Check out last year’s QSR Drive-Thru Report That AI dusting, though, steadily became a more prevalent character in drive-thru observations. Taco Bell in July announced it spread the technology (automated voice ordering in this case) to nearly 900 U.S. stores across 38 states through an expanding partnership with provider Omilia. It happened in about three years. As we’ve tested locations since 2021, AI has been a blurry data set. A lot of intrigue alongside an immaterial sample size. Customers weren’t always eager to try it, but they also didn’t know what they were being asked to express excitement or trepidation about. Had they actually seen a QSR with voice AI? More “maybes” than tangible narratives. Naturally, that’s less true now than it was, and this year’s QSR Drive-Thru Report found a clear and emerging pattern from the surging landscape: AI is leaving behind a hospitality gap. “The biggest change over the past year isn’t necessarily a broad expansion in where voice AI is being used,” says Sarah Beckett, VP sales and marketing at Intouch Insight. “It’s an improvement in what the technology can do once it’s engaged.” Along with our typical KPI tests, like speed and accuracy, Intouch Insight sent shoppers to 120 targeted shops at three confirmed AI-equipped brands (95 AI interactions for Burger King, Taco Bell, and Wendy’s). Combined with 79 moments when a shopper found AI deployed without seeking it deliberately (McDonald’s joined in), the total sample was 174 AI engagements. Voice AI was seen in 13 percent of mystery shopped Wendy’s visits in 2026, up from 12 percent in 2025. Taco Bell came in at 21 compared to 27 percent, year-over-year. And Burger King was essentially flat at 3 versus 4 percent. Across all, the combined rate was 12.5 percent over 14.1 percent last year. But, Beckett points out, within the voice AI encounters tallied by shoppers, the technology did more of the work in 2026. The share of interactions where AI handled the full order or engagement jumped from 20 to 40 percent, while the share consisting only of an AI greeting followed by an immediate employee handoff fell from 70 to 50 percent. Order accuracy increased from 84 to 89 percent, and overall service satisfaction rose from 91 to 95 percent. Direct perceptions of AI were mixed. Endo Kazutoshi has launched ENDO and Moga, an intimate two-storey restaurant and listening bar in a Chelsea townhouse formerly home to Michelin-starred restaurant Five Fields. The ground floor is home to the 10-seat omakase restaurant ENDO, while upstairs Moga will operate as a listening bar. Following extensive trips back to Japan with his team, the cooking at ENDO will see Kazutoshi, a third-generation sushi master, return more closely to the time-honoured traditions of his training. The multi-course omakase experience will reflect his commitment to ‘purity, seasonality and discipline’, with details of the menu held back from guests in keeping with the traditions of omakase. 8-9 Blacklands Terrace, London SW3 2SP / https://www.endo-chelsea.com/ Quaglino’s St James’s restaurant Quaglino’s will reopen this October, nearly a century after it was founded, following a major restoration. At the heart of the relaunch will be a menu created in collaboration with group culinary consultant Miller Prada, combining Italian provenance, French classical technique and British dining traditions. The restaurant’s Q Bar will return with a new cocktail programme alongside three new bars: a Champagne Bar offering 24 champagnes by the glass and bottle; a Fruits de Mer seafood counter serving molluscs and crustacea alongside ceviche and tiradito small plates; and a dessert bar inspired by a Cannes tabac, with smoke-filled edible helium balloons, cannoli cigars and chocolate ashtrays. 16 Bury Street, London, SW1Y 6AJ / https://quaglinos-restaurant.co.uk/ Beaufort Wine Bar A wine bar offering more than 250 wines from 18 countries will open at The Savoy this month. articles.title: FAT Brands Becomes OHG Brands Under New Ownership
articles.titleKo: FAT Brands Becomes OHG Brands Under New Ownership
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . FAT Brands is ready for its next chapter, and that means an entirely new name as a new company. The restaurant group has officially relaunched as OHG Brands (Original. Honest. Good). The move follows the company’s bankruptcy and subsequent acquisition by a lender group earlier this year. The updated branding is already reflected in the company’s new website . Ownership said additional details will be released in November. OHG operates Round Table Pizza, Fatburger, Marble Slab Creamery, Johnny Rockets, Fazoli’s, Great American Cookies, Buffalo’s Cafe & Express, Hurricane Grill & Wings, Pretzelmaker, Native Grill & Wings, and Ponderosa and Bonanza Steakhouses. The 1,700 restaurants span fast food, fast casual, and casual dining. The company describes itself as a group that “strategically develops and grows a diverse portfolio of fast-casual, quick-service and casual dining concepts around the world, using brand heritage as the foundation for growth and innovation that resonates with the next generation of fans.” FAT Brands was formed in 2017 by Andy Wiederhorn. The publicly traded company spent years acquiring concepts, spending nearly $1 billion between 2020 and 2023. The group had over 2,200 restaurants worldwide before filing bankruptcy in January due to piling debt and mounting financial pressure. During court proceedings, Wiederhorn agreed to step away from the business, and his family members, who held several seats on the board of directors, were fired. During court proceedings, the company was divided up in multiple bankruptcy sale transactions. Ownership behind OHG acquired its concepts for $595 million . Amazing Brands purchased Hot Dog on a Stick for $8 million, and a Kuwait-based Elevation Burger franchisee bought the burger concept for $2.5 million. Another group of lenders acquired Twin Peaks for $359.5 million. Meanwhile, Smokey Bones—which at one point served as a conversion strategy for Twin Peaks—shuttered permanently. articles.title: CAVA Names John Ludeke CMO
articles.titleKo: CAVA Names John Ludeke CMO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . John Ludeke is a marketing leader with more than 17 years of experience. CAVA, the category-defining Mediterranean fast-casual restaurant brand, today announced the appointment of John Ludeke as Chief Marketing Officer, strengthening its leadership team as the company deepens its relationship with guests, expands nationally and continues to build one of the most distinctive brands in the restaurant industry. In this role, effective October 12, Ludeke will lead CAVA’s marketing organization and partner closely with key functions to strengthen brand differentiation, deepen guest loyalty and engagement, advance digital experiences and more directly connect marketing to the restaurant experience as the company continues its rapid growth. Ludeke is a marketing leader with more than 17 years of experience building high-growth, culturally relevant, consumer brands and transforming them into category leaders. Most recently, he served as Chief Brand Officer at Dr. Squatch, where he led global brand, creative, brand and retail media, social, public relations, retail marketing, partnerships and marketing strategy as a member of the Executive Leadership Team. During his tenure, he helped grow Dr. Squatch to $500 million in revenue, establish it as a leading men’s personal care brand, guide marketing through its acquisition by Unilever and expand its social presence through large-scale campaigns and celebrity, creator and entertainment partnerships. Prior to Dr. Squatch, Ludeke spent more than a decade at Monster Energy. Based in Shanghai and Seoul for more than six years, he led marketing across the Asia-Pacific region, including Japan, Korea, China, India and Vietnam. As a senior global marketing leader, he also helped shape strategy across dozens of countries and developed talent-driven campaigns and partnerships with global brands including Adidas, Ford, Activision, Tencent, Sony and DJI. His work has been recognized by Adweek, The Drum and the Marketing Agencies Association Worldwide, including placement on the Adweek 50, Adweek Creative 100 and The Drum Rebel 50. “John is a proven builder of culturally relevant consumer brands and a thoughtful, passionate leader who knows how to turn brand belief into business momentum,” said Brett Schulman, Co-founder and CEO of CAVA. “One of the things that stands out about John is his ability to quickly understand the essence of a consumer brand and translate it into a meaningful marketing strategy that is relevant, distinctive, and true to the brand. We have a unique, category-defining opportunity at CAVA to bring the flavors, hospitality, and generosity of the Mediterranean to even more people. John brings the experience to help us do that, along with a leadership style grounded in curiosity, agility, positivity, and collective ambition. Those qualities reflect how we lead at CAVA, and we’re thrilled to welcome him to the CAVA table.” Ludeke has a track record of scaling consumer brands, building culture and creating meaningful connections with audiences around the world. In his new role at CAVA, he will help translate the company’s unique Mediterranean ethos into brand experiences that deepen guest connection, strengthen loyalty and support the company’s continued growth. “CAVA has built something truly special: a brand rooted in great food, warm hospitality and a clear point of view on how food should make people feel,” said John Ludeke, CAVA’s newly appointed Chief Marketing Officer. “The company has tremendous momentum and a powerful opportunity to shape the future of the industry. I’m excited to join this team, learn from the team who has built CAVA and help bring CAVA’s Mediterranean spirit to even more guests and communities.” The post CAVA Names John Ludeke CMO appeared first on QSR Magazine .
