articles.titleKo: Ruby Slipper Adds First Pasta Dish as Part of Fall Menu Rollout
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Ruby Slipper’s fall menu will be available at participating locations beginning Sept. 30, while supplies last. Autumn is ushering in several seasonal delights at Ruby Slipper, as the New Orleans-born breakfast and lunch café adds a new savory option, breakfast savings and plenty of pumpkin. Headlining the fall menu is the debut of Ruby Slipper’s first pasta dish, Pumpkin Ravioli. The savory item (priced at $16.50) pairs cheese ravioli tossed in a creamy pumpkin sauce with bacon and Parmesan, then topped with roasted pepitas for a hearty crunch. By popular demand, the limited-time Patty Melt ($15) earns an extended stay after becoming a September favorite. The double smashed beef patty is layered with American cheese, pepper jack, caramelized onion and remoulade, then griddled on sourdough for a crisp, melty finish. Weekday morning guests will enjoy the new Rise & Ruby Sunrise Special, a $10 offer available in-restaurant Monday through Friday from 7-9 a.m. The special includes the Sunrise Standard — two eggs any style, your choice of Bacon, pork sausage or chicken sausage, a buttermilk pancake and fruit — plus a hot or iced coffee. “We always want to give our guests more reasons to choose Ruby throughout the week,” said Chef Marla Chua, culinary director for Ruby Slipper. “We’re always thinking about how we can build on what guests already love while creating room to try something different. This time, that meant extending an overwhelmingly popular lunch item and finding a way to add value for guests looking to start their day with us midweek.” In addition to its new pasta dish, Ruby Slipper is giving pumpkin its annual moment with new Pumpkin Praline Beignets ($7.25). Its signature warm beignets are topped with pumpkin mascarpone and pecan praline sauce, and finished with raspberry pomegranate coulis. The combination layers creamy pumpkin and toasted praline with a bright fruit note cutting through the richness. “Pumpkin is usually associated with the sweeter side of fall, but it’s a surprisingly versatile ingredient,” Chua added. “We wanted to play with that this year and show how well it can work in both sweet and savory forms.” The fall lineup also includes Pumpkin Bread Pudding Pancakes ($12.50), topped with spiced pecan praline sauce and whipped pumpkin mascarpone. On the drink menu, the Pumpkin Spice Latte ($6.50) combines espresso, pumpkin spice syrup, milk and whipped cream, while the Pumpkin Cream Chai Latte ($6.50) pairs chai tea with milk and cream, topped with pumpkin-infused cold foam. For something bubbly, the Whipped Raspberry Pomegranate Mimosa ($10) blends raspberry and pomegranate purée with lemon, coconut and sparkling wine, topped with cold foam. Ruby Slipper’s fall menu will be available at participating locations beginning Sept. 30, while supplies last. For more information about Ruby Slipper’s seasonal menu and ongoing updates, visit rubybrunch.com or follow @BrunchWithRuby on Instagram, TikTok, X and Facebook. Ruby Slipper fans can brunch like a VIP with the Ruby Bennies loyalty app — earn points every time you order directly online or dine in, redeem them for rewards, place orders with ease in the app and be the first to know about upcoming specials. Savvy Sliders and 5-hour Energy Launch Caramel Apple Drinks. Fall flavors get an energizing twist starting today, as Savvy Sliders and 5-hour Energy team up to introduce two limited-time-only creations inspired by one of the season’s most iconic treats: caramel apples. Designed to capture the nostalgia of crisp fall days, orchard visits, and caramel dipped apples, the menu collaboration features two new beverages: the Dirty Caramel Apple Refresher and the Caramel Drizzle Pie Shake – bothinfused with the boldness of 5-hour ENERGY’s new Caramel Apple flavor. Available September 30 through November 30 at Savvy Sliders locations throughout the U.S., these drinks offer guests a new way to enjoy the flavors of the season while incorporating the functional lift consumers have come to expect from 5-hour ENERGY. “We really wanted to create something that reinforces to our guests that fall has arrived, but in a new and exciting way for the Savvy Sliders brand,” said Sonny Asker, COO for Savvy Sliders. “Our guests already love our hand-spun custard shakes and lemonade, but collaborating with 5-hour ENERGY and incorporating their delicious Caramel Apple flavor allowed us to create two completely new drink options in very popular categories that we think our guests are going to love.” The Dirty Caramel Apple Refresher combines Savvy Slider’s lemonade with approximately 1/2 bottle (115mg of caffeine) of 5-hour ENERGY Caramel Apple, topped with a scoop of Savvy’s vanilla custard and caramel drizzle for a sweet-tart, refreshing take on the classic fall flavor. The Caramel Drizzle Pie Shake blends Savvy’s Slider’s hand-spun vanilla custard with approximately 1/3 bottle (70 mg of caffeine) 5-hour ENERGY Caramel Apple, topped with whipped cream, caramel drizzle, and crushed graham cracker crumbs for a rich-and-creamy taste of fall. “Caramel Apple is one of those flavors that immediately evokes that fall is here, and our collaboration with Savvy Sliders gives both core audiences two unique ways to experience it while enjoying the flavor, energy boost and other added benefits they have come to expect from 5-hour ENERGY,” said Leah Key, President of Living Essentials, LLC, the maker of 5-hour ENERGY products. 5-hour ENERGY’s new limited-edition Caramel Apple flavor energy shot is inspired by the quintessential fall treat, pairing the crisp and sweet-yet-tart taste of green apples with rich, buttery caramel. It’s a craveable combination that brings the flavor of caramel-dipped apples straight from the orchard, without the sugar. Each 5-hour ENERGY Caramel Apple shot contains 230 mg of caffeine along with B vitamins and other essential nutrients with zero sugar and zero calories. It is available online at 5hourENERGY.com , Amazon and TikTok Shop, as well as in-store at Walmart, Target and select retailers nationwide. The Savvy Sliders and 5-hour ENERGY partnership reflects a shared desire to bring consumers innovative, flavorful experiences that fit into their everyday routines. Guests can enjoy them alongside Savvy Sliders’ menu of never-frozen Certified Angus beef sliders, hand-breaded chicken, and seasoned fries. These limited-time creations will be available at all Savvy Slider’s locations while supplies last. A list of Savvy Sliders locations can be found at www.SavvySliders.com. WiRL is proud to continue and expand the WiRL Awards, honoring the leaders of today and tomorrow. Launched in 2023, WiRL was created as a national community to elevate, educate, and empower women in restaurant leadership. The platform includes digital and print features, a weekly newsletter, a biweekly podcast, monthly webinars, and virtual #WiRLPowerHour happy hours. Its signature annual event, the WiRL Together Summit—held each February in a safe, authentic environment—brings together women from across the industry to connect, learn, build mentorships, and gain career-advancement insights. The WiRL Awards extend that mission by celebrating women who are driving progress in the restaurant industry—especially those who have not yet been formally recognized. Nominations for the 2027 WiRL Awards open on October 1, 2026, and close on November 1, 2026. Winners will be honored during the 2027 WiRL Together Summit in Scottsdale, Arizona, with complimentary access to the event, and will be featured in WiRL’s February special issue and February webinar alongside members of the WiRL Advisory Board. Award Categories: Rising Star—For emerging leaders who are already making waves. Trailblazer—Recognizing those transforming the industry, challenging conventions, and driving innovation. Community Champion—For those who are the heartbeat of their communities, lifting others up and making a meaningful difference. Investing in equity, mentorship, and the next generation of women leaders is critical to building a stronger, more inclusive future. The WiRL Awards are open to women working in a restaurant brand or organization at any level of leadership or experience. Know a woman driving real change in this industry—or is it you? The honor recognizes the KBP Inspired team’s leadership, operational excellence and culture, which together deliver exceptional experiences for Arby’s guests. “Being named Arby’s Operator of the Year is a tremendous honor,” said Matt Hansen, Chief Operating Officer at KBP Brands. “Thank you to Arby’s for this recognition and for the partnership behind it, and to every KBP Inspired team member, from our restaurant crews to our operations leaders. articles.title: Michelin-Starred Chef Atul Kochhar Heads to Jashan in Plano, Texas
articles.titleKo: Michelin-Starred Chef Atul Kochhar Heads to Jashan in Plano, Texas
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Jashan, the Plano restaurant celebrating the depth, history and evolution of Indian cuisine, will welcome Chef Atul Kochhar, one of the most influential figures in modern Indian dining, for a three-day culinary collaboration October 3–5. Rather than repeat a single menu throughout his visit, Kochhar and the Jashan team will present three completely different dining experiences over three nights, each offering a distinct perspective on Indian cuisine, technique and hospitality. Kochhar made culinary history in 2001, when Tamarind in London earned a Michelin star, making him the first Indian chef to receive a Michelin star. He later opened his own London restaurant, Benares, which earned a Michelin star in 2007. Over the course of his career, Kochhar has helped bring Indian cuisine into the international fine-dining conversation, showcasing its complexity and regional diversity to audiences around the world. For Jashan Chef, Founder & President Prasanna Singaraju, Kochhar’s visit represents a particularly meaningful moment. Long before opening Jashan, Singaraju looked to chefs like Kochhar as examples of what could be possible for Indian cuisine on the world stage. Kochhar’s approach to Indian cuisine — treating it with seriousness, precision and reverence rather than as something that needed to be explained or made more accessible — helped inspire Singaraju’s own ambitions and ultimately his vision for Jashan. His visit brings that influence full circle, with the two chefs now sharing a kitchen and creating an experience together. The weekend begins on Saturday, October 3, with Chef Atul Kochhar at Jashan, when Kochhar takes over the restaurant’s tasting-menu experience for one evening. Guests will experience an exclusive seven-course menu created by Kochhar, replacing Jashan’s signature Jashan 101 and Taste of India tasting menus for the night. The experience is $140++ per guest. On Sunday, October 4, Jashan will host 10 Hands — The Sunday Supper, bringing five chefs together in one kitchen: Chef Atul Kochhar, Chef Akshraj Jodha, Chef Ashish Bhasin, Chef Ramesh Thangaraj and Chef Prasanna Singaraju. Representing different generations, backgrounds and journeys through Indian cuisine, the five chefs will collaborate on a menu designed to be shared around the table. Limited to 60 guests, the Sunday supper will emphasize the communal nature of Indian hospitality, with dishes meant to be passed, discussed and experienced together. Tickets are $160++ per guest. The three-day collaboration concludes on Monday, October 5, with Dil Se — Chef Atul Kochhar × Chef Prasanna, the weekend’s most intimate experience. Limited to just 20 guests and one seating, the dinner brings Kochhar and Singaraju together for a deeply personal collaborative menu. Dil Se , meaning “from the heart,” reflects both Singaraju’s admiration for a chef who helped shape his own ambitions and Jashan’s belief that food is inseparable from memory, culture and connection. Tickets are $225++ per guest. To make a reservation for these experiences go to https://jashan.us/atul-kochhar. For more than 50 years, Buddy’s bar-b-q has brought East Tennesseans together over hickory-smoked favorites, Southern hospitality and a tradition that feels like home. Now, CEO Mark Lemoncelli has been named in VIP Knoxville Magazine’s 50 Under 50 list, recognizing his leadership, business success and commitment to the community as he helps carry the beloved hometown brand into its next 50 years. Lemoncelli’s path to leading Buddy’s bar-b-q began long before he stepped into his role as CEO. Raised by a father who owned a successful chain of restaurants, he knew early on that the business would be part of his future. Years later, that path led him to Buddy’s through his wife Jaime, granddaughter of Buddy’s bar-b-q founder Buddy Smothers, bringing together his lifelong connection to the restaurant industry with the opportunity to carry forward a well-established East Tennessee brand. “I want to move the Buddy’s brand forward while always preserving the roots it was built on,” said Lemoncelli. “I have great respect for Buddy Smothers and the mission behind the very first restaurant — to make authentic Southern classics and serve them to the community at a great value. Even as things change, it’s important that we don’t deviate from that very simple standard. It’s at the heart of who we are, and it’s given me a great sense of purpose.” Today, Lemoncelli is focused on honoring the history and values that built Buddy’s while continuing to evolve the company for the future. Over the past year, Buddy’s earned first-place recognition across multiple categories in the Knox Stars Community’s Choice Awards and Anderson County Best of 2025 Awards. The franchise has also continued to expand its menu with new offerings including Mac & Cheese, Chicken Tenders, Banana Pudding and seasonal shakes, while staying rooted in the slow-cooked bar-b-q that has defined Buddy’s for generations. For more than five decades, Buddy’s has served communities throughout East Tennessee, growing from humble beginnings into a beloved regional brand known for authentic, hickory-smoked bar-b-q. Pork, chicken and ribs are smoked on-site daily and served alongside classic Southern sides including coleslaw, baked beans and potato salad. Hushpuppies, seasonal shakes, desserts and other menu favorites round out the offerings, all centered around generous portions, approachable prices and family-friendly appeal. As the restaurant industry continues to evolve, Lemoncelli remains focused on helping Buddy’s grow while staying true to what has made the brand successful for generations. His recognition as one of VIP Knoxville’s 50 Under 50 underscores that balance between preserving Buddy’s longstanding legacy and positioning the franchise for what comes next. Vandelay Companies continues its growth across Texas and beyond with the next two Houston-area Hudson House locations in Katy at LaCenterra at Cinco Ranch and in Memorial City at the Greenside development. The Katy location at 2643 Commercial Center Blvd is slated to open early 2027 with the Memorial City location at 1085 Gessner Rd, Suite 290 set to open Spring/Summer 2027. The upcoming locations of the East-Coast inspired neighborhood restaurant represent another step in the continued expansion of one of Vandelay Companies’ most established concepts. Since opening the original Hudson House in 2017, the brand has grown from a neighborhood restaurant into a defining concept within the Vandelay portfolio, earning a loyal following for lunch, brunch, dinner and its celebrated happy hour. This continued growth reflects Vandelay Companies’ broader approach to expansion: identifying strong neighborhoods and markets, investing in each restaurant for the long term and building concepts designed to become lasting parts of the communities they serve. “Since opening our first Houston-area Hudson House in 2023, we’ve seen a tremendous response from guests across the market,” said Hunter Pond, Founder, Chairman & CEO of Vandelay Companies. “The success of our two existing Houston-area locations has continued to reinforce what a strong fit Hudson House is for the market, and with two more locations on the way, we look forward to bringing the experience to even more neighborhoods across the area.” Known for its polished interpretation of a classic East Coast neighborhood restaurant, Hudson House combines a seafood-driven menu, expansive raw bar, sushi, signature cocktails and timeless American favorites within a warm, energetic setting. Among the restaurant’s best-known dishes are Hudson’s Avocado Dip, made with whipped avocado, green onion, herbs and ranch chips; The Cheeseburger, featuring thin patties, American cheese, pickles and Hudson’s signature house sauce; Chicken Parm, served with creamy tomato pasta and Reggiano; and the Hudson Salad, made with popcorn chicken, avocado, cherry tomato, bacon, sharp cheddar and green goddess dressing. Hudson House’s seafood program remains central to the experience, with East Coast oysters flown in daily, a dedicated raw bar and a sushi menu that includes the Sunset Roll, with spicy tuna, cucumber and avocado topped with salmon, lemon and ginger vinaigrette; the riceless Signature Roll, featuring salmon, tuna, crab, avocado, tempura flake and spicy ponzu; the Pressed Ahi Tuna Roll, with tuna sashimi, spicy tuna, avocado, spicy mayo, eel sauce and truffle oil; and Spicy Tuna Crispy Rice with chili mayo and eel sauce. The beverage program is equally defining, led by Hudson House’s signature “World’s Coldest Martini,” featuring Grey Goose vodka served on tap and chilled to a crisp 10 degrees for an exceptionally cold, smooth pour. Martini selections include The Classic, Bleu & Gold, made with vodka, olive juice, bleu cheese salt and housemade bleu cheese olives; The Lemon Drop, finished with limoncello foam; and The Espresso, made with vodka, espresso, Kahlúa and Baileys. Additional cocktail favorites include the Frozen Bellini, Strawberry Spritz, Spicy Mexican and a classic Manhattan. The restaurant will bring Hudson House’s signature design language in both the 6,000-square foot Memorial City location and the 5,600-square-foot Katy location. The design features warm leather booths, a large wraparound bar, a spacious sit-down raw bar and an outdoor patio. The space is designed to balance the familiarity of a traditional New England dining institution with the polished, energetic atmosphere that has become synonymous with the Hudson House brand. articles.title: Inside DoorDash’s Push to Connect Every Restaurant Channel
articles.titleKo: Inside DoorDash’s Push to Connect Every Restaurant Channel
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . DashOS is meant to link marketplace discovery with future transactions. DoorDash wants to become more than a delivery marketplace for restaurants. Its new DashOS platform connects ordering, reservations, loyalty, customer data, and marketing. The goal is to help restaurants recognize the same guest across delivery, direct ordering, and dine-in visits, then use that information to bring the customer back. That is difficult for many operators today. Guests move easily between channels, but their activity often lands in separate systems. One person can appear to be several unrelated customers, leaving restaurants without a clear picture of what led to another purchase. Restaurants also have to oversee numerous technology products in addition to running their kitchens and dining rooms. DoorDash data shows 40 percent of surveyed U.S. operators use four to five systems, and 83 percent believe better-connected technology would improve profitability. “The idea is really to become the growth partner for merchants, period, and be the one-stop shop for merchants to look to when they say I wanna grow,” says Parisa Sadrzadeh, DoorDash’s vice president of strategy and operations. DoorDash introduced DashOS during its Dash Forward 2026 event. The platform connects DoorDash Marketplace with the company’s direct ordering, loyalty, reservation, and marketing products. Customers must opt into a restaurant’s loyalty program or agree to share their information for marketing. Once they do, the restaurant can see eligible activity across the DoorDash products it uses and communicate with that customer directly. DoorDash sees its marketplace as the starting point for many of those relationships. A customer might discover a restaurant through delivery, return through its website, and later visit in person. DashOS is designed to connect those transactions instead of treating each one as a separate relationship. The early loyalty results provide DoorDash’s clearest evidence for the model. More than one in five customers who visit the DoorDash page of a participating restaurant enroll in its loyalty program. Those members order 1.8 times as often and spend approximately 1.75 times as much per person as customers who have not enrolled. DashOS can use purchasing history to recommend menu items and support marketing through email, text messages and push notifications. Campaigns can run automatically for restaurants without dedicated marketing employees, or operators can customize them. The information can follow customers to a restaurant’s direct ordering site. Once logged in, a customer can see previous DoorDash orders, receive recommendations, and use saved payment information. DoorDash can also provide delivery for the direct order. Reservations are another piece of the customer record. DoorDash said AI-powered recommendations increased total bookings by more than 15 percent in early tests. SevenRooms marketing products using blinded, aggregated DoorDash Marketplace information have produced more than $150 million in restaurant sales this year. DoorDash acquired SevenRooms in 2025. The platform works with technology restaurants already use. DoorDash is expanding connections with Clover, Qu, Checkmate, Chowly, Deliverect, Stream and UrbanPiper. Starting in 2027, more than 80,000 restaurants using those providers are expected to gain access to SevenRooms customer profiles, online ordering, in-store rewards and omnichannel loyalty products. DoorDash still has work to do to make the products operate as one system. The company has connected its merchant portal more closely with its customer relationship software and plans more automation. “The idea is to simplify this into one platform,” Sadrzadeh says. “We need to continue to improve it and continue to simplify it.” DashOS is one piece of DoorDash’s effort to play a larger role in local c

articles.title: Prince St. Pizza Opens First Louisiana Location
articles.titleKo: Prince St. Pizza Opens First Louisiana Location
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Prince St. Pizza, the New York City-born pizzeria known for its Sicilian-style square pies and signature pepperoni-loaded slices, will open its first Louisiana location Friday, Oct. 9, at 6556 Siegen Lane. The walk-up counter and late-night hours land on one of Baton Rouge’s busiest retail and dining corridors, a short drive from LSU and the game-day traffic that fills the area every home game. Siegen Lane also marks the first Prince St. Pizza in the state of Louisiana for development partner Lawrence Kourie , the founding and largest franchise owner of Dave’s Hot Chicken, who came aboard in March to lead the brand’s push into new markets. The Baton Rouge shop will celebrate its grand opening Friday, Oct. 9, at 11 a.m. with a free slice of pizza for the first 50 people in line. Jon Jones , the former two-division UFC champion who signed on as a partner in the shop in August, will also appear at the grand opening. Louisiana gets the full lineup from day one, including the Spicy Spring, a fra diavolo square with thick-cut pepperoni cups baked onto focaccia-style crust, and The Naughty Pie, layered with spicy vodka sauce, ricotta, mozzarella and hot honey. Classic New York rounds, Caesar and Italian chopped salads, smoked mozzarella sticks and desserts round out the board. Sauce is made in-house daily, and the dough runs through a water filtration process built to mimic New York tap water. “We designed this kitchen around volume, because nothing in this city happens quietly,” said Kourie. “Every person behind that counter was put through the same training our New York crews get. Opening on a Friday in October was intentional. Football weekends, a campus a few minutes up the road and a town that stays out late is about as close to Manhattan hours as the South gets.” Founded in Manhattan’s Nolita neighborhood in 2012 and rooted in the Morano family’s generations-old recipes, Prince St. Pizza built its following on SoHo Squares and the philosophy that if you can put it on pasta, you can put it on pizza. Siegen Lane joins a map that already includes Las Vegas, Chicago, Los Angeles, Dallas, Nashville, Toronto, Miami, San Diego and Arizona. “Prince St. Pizza was built on a simple idea: make a slice people can’t stop talking about,” said Lawrence Longo, CEO of Prince St. Pizza. “Hand someone a square with the pepperoni curled up at the edges and they will call three friends before they finish it. That is how this thing traveled out of Nolita, one market at a time.” The Baton Rouge pizzeria will be open from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, with extended hours until midnight Friday and Saturday. Dine-in seating, takeout and catering are available. For more information, visit princestreetpizza.com. The post Prince St. Pizza Opens First Louisiana Location appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: Denny’s Raises More Than $1.24 Million for Childhood Cancer Research
articles.titleKo: Denny’s Raises More Than $1.24 Million for Childhood Cancer Research
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Denny’s and its franchise owners, restaurant teams, and Guests presented more than $1.24 million to Cookies for Kids’ Cancer during Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, a 30% increase over the Brand’s inaugural systemwide campaign last year. With total support now approaching $4 million since 2011, Denny’s is calling on restaurant brands across the industry to join the growing effort and help bring even more resources to childhood cancer research. “I lost my brother to cancer at a young age, so this is personal to me,” said Chris Bode, president and chief executive officer of Denny’s. “Our franchise owners brought this cause into Denny’s, and our teams and Guests helped it grow into a hometown movement across the country. Denny’s is committed to sustaining that support because families facing childhood cancer need better treatment options. Denny’s also named Gretchen Holt Witt, co-founder and executive director of Cookies for Kids’ Cancer, the first recipient of its Humanitarian Leadership Award during the Brand’s annual franchisee convention on September 23. The award recognizes Witt’s leadership in turning her family’s experience with childhood cancer into a national movement to fund research, bringing families, businesses, and communities together to help advance better treatments for children. Witt and her husband, Larry, founded Cookies for Kids’ Cancer in 2008 to help other families fighting pediatric cancer after their 2-year-old son, Liam, was declared cancer-free. Liam’s cancer later returned and he lost his battle in 2011 at age six, but his parents continued their work so other children and families could have more treatment options. “These are the children of our team members, Guests, owners, and neighbors. This matters because they matter,” said Fasika Melaku, chief people, enterprise communications, and social impact officer of Denny’s. “Every restaurant brand has a community it can mobilize. We’re asking our industry to turn that reach into more funding for childhood cancer research.” Cookies for Kids’ Cancer supports peer-reviewed research and clinical trials at leading pediatric cancer centers across the United States, including a Texas Children’s study exploring a potential treatment approach for children with recurrent ependymoma, a type of brain or spinal cord tumor that has returned after treatment. While Denny’s fundraising is rooted in communities across the United States, the potential impact of the research extends beyond national borders. Discoveries made here can inform care and help advance new, improved and less toxic treatments for children around the world. “People do not have to work in a laboratory to help move research forward,” said Gretchen Holt Witt. “Cancer remains the leading cause of death from disease among children in the United States, and the cancers children face are different from those most commonly diagnosed in adults. Support from Denny’s helps us fund promising work toward new, improved and less toxic treatments. Every contribution gives researchers more resources to pursue better answers for children.” Restaurant brands interested in joining the effort or learning more about Denny’s partnership with Cookies for Kids’ Cancer may contact Colton Grace, manager of enterprise PR, at cgrace@dennys.com. Add protein. Energy in the afternoon? Add protein. Smoothie after a workout? Go for it. Whatever the 7 Brew order is, our guests can add protein.” The nationwide launch marks the final phase of the 7 Brew Protein Boost rollout following initial introduction in select Dallas-Fort Worth stands in August. It also kicks off the brand’s October “Booost Your Brew” campaign, featuring a lineup of limited-time Halloween-inspired beverages and even surprise product drops. The new lineup of Booost Your Brew drinks includes: Pumpkin Blondie : A cozy blend of the signature Blondie with warm pumpkin pie flavors, serving a sweet taste of fall in every cup. Drizzled Apple 7 Fizz Soda: Crisp green apple topped with a rich caramel drizzle for a bubbly twist on a classic caramel apple. Boo Raspberry Smoothie : A refreshing Blue Pom smoothie blended with blue raspberry, pomegranate and strawberry for a frightfully fruity sip. Along with the new Protein Boost and seasonal drink lineup, guests can look forward to several fun surprises throughout October, including: Jackpot Day | October 7 : Guests who purchase any two medium or large drinks will receive a free limited-edition, Halloween-themed sticker sheet, while supplies last, the perfect keepsake during spooky season and beyond. Surprise Drink Drop | Date To Be Announced :A surprise drink drop, featuring seasonal flavors, arrives for a limited time that’s sure to make Frankenstein rise from his slumber. Fill-A-Tray | October 31: Celebrate Halloween with four medium drinks for just $17, making it easy to treat the whole boo crew before heading out for trick-or-treating, parties or a spooky movie night. articles.title: Kutlerri.ai Raises $4 Million to Put a Team of AI Agents to Work on Restaurant Revenue and Cost
articles.titleKo: Kutlerri.ai Raises $4 Million to Put a Team of AI Agents to Work on Restaurant Revenue and Cost
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Take a limited-service restaurant turning over $1.5 million a year. In 2019 an operation that size kept roughly $75,000 of it. To break even on the same four walls today it has to push about $1.93 million through them. The old arithmetic at least fits in an operator’s head: a third of every sales dollar to food, a third to labor, most of the rest to occupancy and supplies, and about a nickel left at the bottom. Then costs climbed and the sales dollar did not.[2] Payroll is where the gap opens widest. Limited-service operators who lost money in fiscal 2024 spent 34.1 % of sales on wages and benefits. The ones who turned a profit spent 30.0 %.[3] Four cents in every dollar separates them, and on a business that keeps a nickel, four cents is nearly the whole thing. Almost nothing that goes wrong in a restaurant today gets fixed by hiring somebody to fix it. A thin margin is also an easy one to move. When a restaurant keeps five cents on the dollar, finding one more cent does not make it 1 % better off. It makes it 20 % more profitable. Two cents, and that becomes 40 %. Most of the software a restaurant pays for every month does not add a cent to that margin. Restaurants are not short of software. They are short of anyone to act on it. A single restaurant already pays for a point-of-sale system, scheduling, payroll, inventory, online ordering, reservations and accounting. All of them are good at telling the operator what happened. None of them does anything about it. The unanswered catering inquiry shows up in a report. So does the ad spend that brought in nothing, and the entrée that loses money on every ticket. Somebody still has to fix each one, and in most restaurants that somebody was let go years ago and never replaced. Kutlerri.ai is built for the part that comes after the report. It builds one AI agent per problem, runs it on the restaurant’s behalf, and draws its fee from what the agent produces rather than a monthly license: a %age of the revenue it creates, or of the cost it strips out. Houston-based Narahari Investments has put $4 million behind that model. The round scales the Catering Sales Agent and the agents behind it. Every agent is delivered as a managed service today, with a mobile-first app in development for operators who would rather run them in-house. “Every restaurant software company sells the same two things: a tool, and the assumption that somebody inside will use it,” said Trisha Narahari, Managing Director at Narahari Investments. “That somebody left the industry years ago. Kutlerri.ai sends the worker, not just the tool, and takes its fee out of what that worker brings in. They ran it that way on a real restaurant’s books for 10 months before selling it to anybody. That is what we backed.” “An agent has to earn its own line on the P&L, or it does not ship,” said Payal Tripathy, Co-Founder & COO of Kutlerri.ai. “That is the rule we build to, and our fee comes out of the line it earns. The bar we hold ourselves to is 20 % more revenue and 10 % less cost. No single agent gets a restaurant there, which is exactly why there is a team of them and why they go out one at a time.” Why the first agent was built to sell catering Catering is the largest single order a restaurant writes, and the one with the least selling behind it. Smaller operators have nobody assigned to it. Larger brands have a catering team that spends its day quoting, confirming and servicing the orders already coming in. In both cases the same work goes undone: going out and finding new business. The kitchen can already make the food. Finding the buyer is sales work, not kitchen work. It is also unusually winnable, because catering demand does not spread evenly. Across more than 8,000 locations and 2 million catering orders, 5 % of customers placed 60 % of the orders.[4] A restaurant does not need a thousand catering ac

articles.title: Prince St. Pizza Teams Up with Xbox for Gears of War Collaboration
articles.titleKo: Prince St. Pizza Teams Up with Xbox for Gears of War Collaboration
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Prince St. Pizza, the New York City-born pizzeria known for its Sicilian-style square pies and signature pepperoni-loaded slices, is joining forces with XBOX and Gears of War for the Emergence Pie, a limited-time collaboration hitting menus systemwide Sept. 28 and staying through Nov. 1, a month built around Gears of War: E-Day , the origin story set to define generations of gaming, arriving Oct. 6. E-Day goes back to the beginning. Fourteen years before the 2006 original, Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago watched the Locust Horde erupt from below and take the surface of their planet apart in three days. Built for the day everything changed, the Emergence Pie stacks spicy vodka sauce and fresh mozzarella beneath a heavy layer of ground pepperoni and sausage, then closes with the new Carbone Fine Food Aglio e Peperoncino Italian Chili Crisp. Every order travels inside custom packaging modeled on the ruins of Kalona, the fictional city at the center of the story. “Gears fans and pizza lovers have been the same crowd for a long time,” said Lawrence Longo, CEO of Prince St. Pizza. “Working with XBOX gave us a way to build for that overlap instead of putting two names on a box and calling it a day. The pie, the emblem, the cutter, all of it started with what the fans would actually want.” A physical card comes with each slice and full-size order, and the code on it unlocks an in-game pizza emblem. Marcus and Dom went into that first fight with nothing but each other, and now a crest earned at a pizza counter can join them on the battlefield. Additionally, rewards members who order the full-size version between Sept. 28 and Oct. 5 will be entered to win one of 100 digital copies of the game*, delivered as download codes. The lineup also extends to a limited-edition pizza cutter modeled after the Prototype Lancer, the chainsaw-mounted rifle an entire era of players use to carve through monsters clawing up from underground. Now, that legendary design takes shape as a tool for tackling a much more delicious target. The limited-edition pizza cutter is available online at shop.princestreetpizza.com . Ahead of the E-Day release, XBOX and Gears of War will take over Hollywood and Vine on Sept. 29 with a set pulled straight from the world of Sera, featuring a life-size display playing game footage and giving attendees an early opportunity to get hands-on with a limited edition controller. Ten Auntie Anne's exclusive Golden Pretzel Passes will be awarded to guests at random throughout opening weekend. Auntie Anne’s and Activate Games are teaming up to kick off National Pretzel Month as Activate, the world’s first active-gaming experience, celebrates the grand opening of its first Nevada location at Las Vegas Town Square on Saturday, Oct. 3. The partnership brings Auntie Anne’s golden, hand-rolled pretzels into Activate’s opening weekend at 6611 S. Las Vegas Blvd., Suite A143, creating a one-of-a-kind, interactive experience for locals and visitors just steps from Auntie Anne’s Town Square location. As part of the collaboration, Activate will debut a limited-edition Auntie Anne’s version of its signature Supermarket, Scan game. Players will race the clock to grab Auntie Anne’s famous pretzels and other recognizable menu items that match their player color, then scan their wristbands at the drop-off screens to fill their basket before time runs out. Like every Activate game, each round lasts one to three minutes. The Auntie Anne’s edition of Supermarket Scan is available only at Activate Las Vegas during grand opening weekend, Oct. 3-4. The activation will also include an Auntie Anne’s-inspired custom photo booth background that gives guests a digital collectors keepsake from opening weekend. “Auntie Anne’s and Activate are both about bringing people together, whether that’s sharing a warm pretzel with friends or teaming up to beat a room,” said Rachel Smith, vice president of marketing at Activate America. “Las Vegas is our first location in Nevada, so it was important to create a one-of-a-kind experience exclusively for this opening weekend. Both brands are built on experiences you can’t get through a screen, which made this partnership a natural fit.” To add to the weekend, 10 Auntie Anne’s exclusive Golden Pretzel Passes will be awarded to guests at random throughout opening weekend. Each Golden Pretzel Pass unlocks a free Original or Cinnamon Sugar Pretzel every week for a full year* through the Auntie Anne’s Rewards app. “At Auntie Anne’s, we love finding new ways to bring a little joy to our fans, and there’s nothing quite like seeing our pretzels come to life in a game,” said Nathan Baldwin, president of Specialty Brands at GoTo Foods. “National Pretzel Month is our favorite time of year, and kicking it off inside Activate’s first Las Vegas location is a fun, unexpected way to celebrate with fans. Whether you’re chasing a high score or chasing a Golden Pretzel Pass, we hope everyone leaves with an experience unlike any other.” Grand opening weekend also marks the U.S. debut of Alpha Mode at Activate. Alpha Mode gives players an early look at new games before they launch globally, and Las Vegas will host the first-ever American play of two new games, Swarm and Legend, both played in the Strike room. Until now, Swarm and Legend have never been played outside Activate’s home location in Winnipeg, Canada. Alpha Mode is available only at Activate Las Vegas during the grand opening weekend. The grand opening celebration kicks off at 10 a.m. on Saturday, Oct. 3, with a ribbon-cutting ceremony scheduled for 9:30 a.m. The first 100 guests in line at open will receive a free Auntie Anne’s pretzel and a signature Auntie Anne’s lemonade, in addition to a reserved half-off play time to play before anyone else, and a premium wristband for weekly play at Activate. Across 15 interactive game rooms, players can take on more than 55 game varieties, including challenges involving lasers, light-up grids, puzzles and strategy. The agreement brings the brand together with an experienced local development team whose portfolio spans grocery stores, convenience retail, gas stations, restaurants and other multi-unit businesses. For la Madeleine, the partnership provides an opportunity to establish a presence in a new region through an operator with established knowledge of communities in both Kansas and Missouri and experience developing customer-focused retail concepts. “We’ve spent years building businesses in the Kansas City area, and we know how much this community values quality, convenience and places that bring people together,” said Musallet. “la Madeleine brings something unique to the market, from its French-inspired menu and fresh bakery offerings to the welcoming atmosphere of its cafés. We’re excited to introduce the brand to Kansas City and grow with it.” The Musallet Group is a diversified, multi-unit business group with a growing portfolio of grocery, convenience retail, franchised businesses and other customer-focused operations across the Kansas City metropolitan area. With a strong track record of developing and operating businesses that serve the everyday needs of local communities, the group has established a growing presence throughout the region. Its portfolio includes nine Mercado Fresco locations and an additional 65,000-square-foot Fresh Market location currently under development at 75th Street and Quivira Road, along with convenience stores and other franchise businesses throughout the Kansas City area. The group also owns and operates Market locations and two World Fresh Markets in Overland Park and Kansas City Northland. These approximately 40,000-square-foot international grocery stores offer customers a broad selection of fresh meat and seafood, bakery items, produce and prepared foods. Together, the group’s diverse portfolio reflects its experience in multi-unit operations, real estate development and creating retail concepts tailored to the communities they serve. “Growth into a new market is most successful when the brand is matched with partners who understand the community and know how to build for the long term,” said Mark Ramage, senior director of franchise development and real estate for la Madeleine. “Eddie has demonstrated that expertise throughout their careers, and their experience in multi-unit retail and food-related businesses makes them an ideal fit to introduce la Madeleine to Kansas City. This agreement gives us a strong foundation for our Midwest debut and future growth in the region.” The Kansas City agreement is part of la Madeleine’s broader franchise expansion strategy, with multi-unit developments helping the brand enter new markets while building a consistent presence across surrounding communities. As development moves forward, the first Kansas City-area café is expected to open in late fall 2027, followed by additional locations. The cafés will offer la Madeleine’s menu of French-inspired breakfast, lunch and dinner selections, freshly baked breads and pastries, and coffee and other beverages in the brand’s signature neighborhood café setting. Whit’s Frozen Custard opened its newest location on Monday, September 28, at 464073 State Road 200, Suite 8, bringing fresh-made frozen custard and a welcoming hometown atmosphere to the Nassau County community. Locally owned and operated by Barb and Ken Porter, Whit’s Frozen Custard of Yulee is designed to be more than a place to grab dessert. The Porters envision a welcoming gathering place where families, friends, sports teams and neighbors can slow down, connect and enjoy a scoop together. “Whit’s Frozen Custard of Yulee is where small-batch craftsmanship meets genuine Southern hospitality,” said Ken Porter. “Every scoop is made fresh daily and served in a space built intentionally for families, teams and neighbors to gather. Guests can enjoy classic flavors, rotating selections and a variety of toppings and creations. Among the signature menu items are Whitsers, custom frozen custard creations blended with guests’ favorite toppings, and Whitties, frozen custard cookie sandwiches that combine creamy custard with freshly baked cookies. With plenty of ways to customize each visit, guests can create a different favorite every time. The Yulee location will be open daily from noon to 9 p.m., giving families plenty of time to stop by after school, following a game or activity, or simply when the craving for something sweet strikes. “Whit’s is all about bringing a little joy to the communities we call home,” said Bill Aseere, CEO of Whit’s Frozen Custard. “Barb and Ken are excited to make Yulee their own and create the kind of welcoming, community-focused shop that makes Whit’s special. articles.title: Surf Bagel Helps Teachers Encourage Reading with Free Bagel Coupons
articles.titleKo: Surf Bagel Helps Teachers Encourage Reading with Free Bagel Coupons
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Surf Bagel recently announced the launch of its new Reading Program “Books to Bagels,” designed to help teachers incentivize students to reach their reading goals. The program is simple for educators to implement and exciting for students to participate in. Teachers set reading goals for their students, and when those goals are met, students receive a special Surf Bagel coupon redeemable for their choice of a bagel and cream cheese. “Supporting local schools has always been a priority for us,” said Matt Patton, President of Surf Bagel. “We are stoked to extend that support to our local teachers by offering a simple incentive that encourages students to meet their goals, and hopefully develop a love for reading too.” Surf Bagel first introduced a pilot version of the program last spring at a few local schools to test the program. The response from teachers and students was amazing. “Teachers, parents, and especially students absolutely loved the program,” Patton said. “And it makes our team happy to see excited students come to the store ready to enjoy a bagel and cream cheese as a reward for their hard work in the classroom.” Since April, Surf Bagel has redeemed more than 250 Books to Bagels coupons from just the 75 pilot classrooms. With strong interest from educators throughout Delaware, over 1,000 classrooms are participating this school year. The Books to Bagels Program is free for schools and teachers to join, and all reward coupons are provided at no cost by Surf Bagel. Teachers interested in bringing the Books to Bagels Program to their classroom or school can complete the interest form available on the Surf Bagel website. articles.titleKo: Momo & Co to open third London site at Tower Bridge Road
articles.originalSummary: Momo & Co, the Himalayan street food restaurant brand, will open its third London location at Tower Bridge Road later this week. The new restaurant will be located on Tower Bridge Road, joining its locations in Lewisham and Bexleyheath. Founded in 2025 by Tenzing Sherpa and Chhong Sherpa, who is also the founder of made-to-order sushi brand IRO Sushi, Momo & Co specialises in Nepalese-inspired fast-casual food. Momo dumplings sit at the centre of its menu and are available steamed, fried or pan-seared, with chicken, pork and vegetarian fillings. They can also be served with jhol, a tangy broth made with peanut and sesame. “What started as an idea to create a modern fast-casual restaurant around momo has quickly transformed into a brand with huge scalability. In our first two locations, we’ve seen strong demand for our authentic momo, great for lunch, an afternoon bite, or dinner, and now see an opportunity to expand our UK footprint with more openings,” says Tenzing Sherpa.

articles.title: TGI Fridays Inks First U.S. Franchise Agreement in Over 10 Years
articles.titleKo: TGI Fridays Inks First U.S. Franchise Agreement in Over 10 Years
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . TGI Fridays has 69 U.S. locations. TGI Fridays signed its first domestic development agreement in more than a decade, partnering with Bliss Bites LLC to open five restaurants across New York State over the next three years. The franchisee also acquired the brand’s existing restaurant in Central Islip, New York. Once the planned openings are completed, Bliss Bites’ portfolio will include six TGI Fridays locations in the state. The agreement gives TGI Fridays an early domestic expansion commitment under its “1-2-3 Strategic Vision,” which targets more than 1,000 restaurants and $2 billion in annual revenue by 2030. It also brings new development to the state where the chain opened its first restaurant, on Manhattan’s Upper East Side, in 1965. “Growth only matters when it’s built with the right partners, and this five-restaurant development agreement is exactly what we envisioned for our ‘1-2-3 Strategic Vision,’” COO Ashley Kirkley in a statement. READ MORE : TGI Fridays Announces Vision for 1,000-Plus Restaurants, $2 Billion in Annual Sales TGI Fridays Plots 1,000-Unit Comeback Under New Ownership Bliss Bites is led by owner and managing director Vinod Chand, who brings more than 35 years of hospitality experience. According to TGI Fridays, Chand was attracted to the brand’s hospitality culture, menu, guest experience, and franchisee support. “Between our restaurant in Central Islip and the new locations we’re planning across New York, we’re building on a brand I already believe in, backed by the kind of corporate support that makes long-term growth possible,” Chand said in a statement. “This is just the beginning.” The announcement did not identify the markets or sites for the five planned restaurants. For TGI Fridays, the deal is a step toward translating its global growth ambitions into new U.S. development. Its strategic plan covers brand activation, flexible expansion across markets, a stronger franchise system, and investment in employees and leadership. TGI Fridays has 69 U.S. restaurants, according to its website—all of which are franchised. The brand shuttered a net of 212 shops from 2023 to 2025. Globally, the brand has nearly 400 locations. The company’s expansion strategy includes traditional full-service restaurants alongside airport locations and smaller hotel concepts. TGI Fridays also plans to support growth through menu and beverage innovation, everyday value offerings, digital improvements, and restaurant atmosphere upgrades. “Guests are increasingly looking for casual dining that delivers real value without sacrificing experience, and Fridays is well positioned to meet that demand as we grow,” Kirkley said. “New York is an important part of our domestic growth story, and we’re excited to welcome our newest franchisee.” The post TGI Fridays Inks First U.S. Franchise Agreement in Over 10 Years appeared first on FSR magazine .

Hawkers Asian Street Food is bringing fresh energy to its dynamic menu with a limited-time selection that puts a playful spin on familiar favorites and hard-to-find flavors across meats, rice and curry, noodles, cocktails and spirit-free sips — all designed to encourage discovery without sacrificing craveability and available now at all locations. At the heart of the new menu is Nasi Lemak, a Malaysian staple and the national dish of co-founder and chef Allen Lo’s home country. Coconut rice comes together with spicy sambal, crispy anchovies, roasted peanuts, a soft-boiled egg and cucumber for a plate built around contrast — creamy and crunchy, savory and spicy, warm and cool. Traditionally eaten by hand, it’s the kind of dish where every bite can be a little different and difficult to find done well in the U.S. “We don’t want the menu to sit still,” said Lo. “Nasi Lemak is a dish I grew up with, so bringing it to our guests is especially meaningful to me. From there, we wanted to keep exploring — there’s so much to pull from across Asia, and we’re always looking for new flavors, dishes and techniques that give our guests a reason to come back and see what we’re cooking up next while maintaining the bold, approachable spirit that defines Hawkers.” The rest of the lineup builds on that foundation with dishes and drinks centered around slow-braised meats, layered spices, fresh herbs and thoughtful ingredient pairings: Bò Tái Chanh: Thinly sliced, seared steak with barrel-aged fish sauce and fresh greens. Lamb Rendang: Slow-braised, spiced lamb with pickled vegetables and toasted coconut. Rich and comforting, it’s made for cooler-weather cravings and pairs naturally with Nasi Lemak. Spiced Lamb Udon: Udon noodles tossed with lamb, chili crisp, sesame and fresh herbs. Pho Two, Please: An aromatic cocktail for two made with Roku gin, RumHaven, pho simple, passion fruit and fresh herbs. Fish sauce adds an unexpected savory note that brings the flavors into balance. Each sip is completely customizable for the guest. Put a Wing on It: Wild Turkey 101 Bourbon, Grand Marnier and gochujang hot honey deliver a smooth cocktail with a spicy edge. Garnished with a fan-favorite: a crispy and flavorful Korean Twice Fried Wing. Coco Kopi: Iced Vietnamese coffee with coconut miso, milk and black sesame whipped cream. Orange Sunburst: Fanta Creamsicle, popping boba and whipped cream for a nostalgic, spirit-free sip. Beyond what’s on the plate, the menu itself has been reimagined to encourage exploration. Founder handwriting and hidden photos add personality, while a streamlined format makes it intuitively easier for guests to navigate the menu and get to the good stuff faster. articles.title: Rich Products Announces Completion of Redesigned Customer Innovation Center
articles.titleKo: Rich Products Announces Completion of Redesigned Customer Innovation Center
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Global, family-owned food company Rich Products (Rich’s) today announced the completion of its newly redesigned Customer Innovation Center at its global headquarters in Buffalo, a $3.2 million investment transforming underutilized space into a modern, digitally powered destination designed to create greater value for customers. Blending hospitality, culinary expertise and advanced production capabilities into one integrated environment, the center enables Rich’s to deliver more immersive, flexible customer experiences with greater speed and vitality, both in person and online. The redesigned space features cutting-edge technology, including video walls, ultra-wide screens and smart displays, creating a highly engaging environment for visitors. Functional, high-end culinary and hospitality areas, along with thoughtfully designed collaboration spaces support a growing demand for dynamic hybrid customer experiences that meet today’s evolving industry expectations. “Innovation doesn’t happen in isolation,” said Richard Ferranti, CEO, Rich Products. “It happens when our associates and customers collaborate to solve real challenges. This center is designed to accelerate that process, bringing together people, technology, culinary expertise and creativity in one place. It’s an investment in our customers, the future growth of Rich’s and Buffalo – the city we’ve proudly called home for more than 80 years.” Enhancing the center is an updated production space, which includes photography and videography studios that give teams a dedicated environment to create on-demand content, including live events, webinars, trainings and podcasts. Additionally, an innovation studio featuring custom-designed sets that represent various kitchen configurations supports commercial and home cooking demonstrations, product showcases and advanced digital production. Not only does this help drive stronger storytelling, but it strengthens Buffalo’s role as an innovation hub within Rich’s global network. This renovation is the latest investment Rich’s has made in its world headquarters’ campus in Buffalo. In 2025, the global food company announced the strategic expansion of its Niagara St. campus and continued investment in the surrounding neighborhood with subsidiary business ROAR Logistics relocating its corporate headquarters to 1120 Niagara St. and Rich’s acquisition of the historic Curtiss Malt House property at 1100 Niagara St. The total projected investment in both sites is approximately $10 million. As Rich’s continues to grow and evolve for the future, the company remains deeply committed to Western New York and making strategic investments that enable it to remain a private, family-owned company, headquartered in Buffalo, that’s successful over the long term. Since its inception, Topgolf has redefined what a party or group event can be, combining sport, entertainment and hospitality into a single, unforgettable experience. This rollout marks Topgolf’s first major update to its event menu program in recent years, arriving just ahead of peak holiday booking season. “Events are core to the Topgolf experience, and this update takes that experience to the next level, right as we head into our busiest events season of the year,” said David McKillips, CEO at Topgolf. “This evolution gives planners more flexibility and a smoother experience from booking to the last bite. Cantina Kitchen: a southwest-inspired taco, nacho and bowl bar with chicken tinga and fajita beef protein options. Taste of Topgolf: crowd favorite shareables that include sliders and a Roman-crust pizza spread spanning global flavors, with vegetarian options. Event planners can customize menus further with a new à la carte list of add-on proteins, sliders, sides and whole pizzas. articles.title: How AI is Influencing Independent Restaurant Dining Decisions
articles.titleKo: How AI is Influencing Independent Restaurant Dining Decisions
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Menufy, the online ordering and digital growth platform designed for independent restaurants and small chains, recently released new consumer research showing that AI is changing how diners find places to eat and opening a new path to visibility for independent businesses. The survey found that 80 percent of consumers would try an independently owned restaurant they had never heard of if it were recommended by AI. Consumers also see a clear advantage for local discovery, with 78 percent saying AI makes locally owned restaurants easier to discover compared with national chains. Together, the findings point to AI as a new visibility channel that could help independent restaurants get in front of consumers beyond traditional search habits. “Independent restaurants have always had an advantage when it comes to having a distinct identity and a strong connection to their local communities,” said Aman Devgan, President and General Manager at Menufy. “AI gives consumers more ways to search around the details that matter to them, which can help the right restaurant surface for a much more specific need or occasion. For operators, the opportunity is to make what already makes their restaurant special clear and accessible online so the technology can understand it too.” AI is already influencing where consumers eat Restaurant discovery through AI is already part of how many consumers decide where to eat. Sixty percent say they use AI-powered tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode, or Perplexity to help make that decision, while another 19 percent have not used AI this way yet but would consider it. That use is translating into real restaurant visits and orders, with 35 percent saying an AI recommendation introduced them to a restaurant they had not previously heard of and they went on to visit or order from that business. Another 14 percent discovered a new restaurant through AI without ultimately placing an order or visiting. Consumers also see AI as useful across a range of dining decisions. More than half (54 percent) would use it to find restaurants nearby, while 31 percent would use it to search for a specific cuisine or dish and 30 percent would turn to AI when looking for restaurants in a new city. The results show how conversational search can help consumers narrow a broad set of choices around the details that matter to a particular meal or occasion. Independent restaurants have an opportunity to reach new diners This is where smaller, independently owned restaurants have an edge. Among respondents, 76 percent said they would be likely to try a local restaurant recommended by AI, compared with 65 percent who said the same of a national chain. The gap shows AI can help diners look beyond the familiar brands that often come to mind first and consider local options they may not have otherwise found. AI is also gaining credibility alongside established restaurant discovery sources. Sixty-four percent of consumers trust AI restaurant recommendations at least as much as traditional Google Search, and 59 percent trust AI at least as much as Google Reviews. Personal recommendations remain particularly influential, with 59 percent saying they trust friends or family more than AI. This suggests AI is becoming an increasingly credible part of the decision process, alongside sources consumers already use when choosing where to eat. Digital fundamentals still help turn discovery into an order While independent restaurants and smaller chains have a real opportunity to win when it comes to AI search and discovery, AI is only one piece of the pie. For most consumers, it serves as a starting point before they take additional steps to validate whether a restaurant is right for them. Moroch, a leading full-service marketing and communications agency, continues to expand its representation and legacy relationship with McDonald’s, adding over 300 locations in North Carolina to its existing AOR representation in 14 other major market regions. This latest win showcases the strength of the Agency’s work with McDonald’s, building on the recent additions of Atlanta, Columbus and Southern VA markets. New regions incorporated under Moroch’s purview include Raleigh-Durham (Fayetteville), Greensboro-High Point-Winston-Salem, Greenville-New Bern-Washington, and Wilmington. “McDonald’s, as our longest-tenured, ongoing client, inspires true passion for the brand and what it represents, which sits at the core of our team and agency,” said Matt Powell, CEO Moroch Partners. “Our unique ability to tap into local culture brings an authenticity to messaging in every market McDonald’s trusts to us, and we’re excited to become immersed in North Carolina’s incredible regional heritage.” “Our team is incredibly proud to extend Moroch’s legacy and partnership with McDonald’s to North Carolina, and create an even stronger bond between the brand and the region,” said Moroch Group Account Director Tricia Cherrison. Moroch will take the lead as both creative and media buying leads for the new accounts, led by Moroch Senior Partner Cristina Vilella, who oversees Moroch’s national McDonald’s efforts. Other markets and ownership groups in which Moroch applies its “local changes everything” approach for McDonalds include: the California Nevada Marketing Assoc., Albuquerque – El Paso, the Illinois/Iowa Operators Assoc., North Texas Advertising Assoc., South Central Texas Syndicate, High Plains Assoc., Greater Houston Operators Assoc., Empire, Greater Wisconsin Operators Syndicate, Ohio Regional Operators Assoc., Three Rivers Assoc., New York Metro McDonald’s Owner/Operators Assoc., Southern Virginia Assoc., Greater Indiana, and Greater Atlanta McDonald’s Owner / Operators Assoc. articles.title: Nick the Greek Opens Doors in Santa Clarita, California
articles.titleKo: Nick the Greek Opens Doors in Santa Clarita, California
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Nick the Greek is now open in Santa Clarita, California, meeting local demand for fresh and convenient Mediterranean food. The new location is locally owned and operated by experienced restaurant operator Nader Shenouda, who plans to open another Nick the Greek restaurant in the region. For more than a decade, Nick the Greek has proved that “The Best Things in Life are Greek” through a diverse and enticing menu of tasty pitas, bowls, salads, desserts and more — now available to Santa Clarita locals and visitors at the brand’s newest Nick the Greek location. “Santa Clarita is a vibrant, growing community that values great food and meaningful connections, and I’m excited to introduce our neighbors to the fresh, authentic flavors that have made Nick the Greek a favorite across California,” said Shenouda. “Whether guests are stopping in after a day at Six Flags Magic Mountain, spending time at Castaic Lake or simply looking for a delicious, convenient meal, we look forward to becoming a go-to destination where friends and families can gather over great Greek food.” Established in 2014 by cousins Big Nick, Little Nick and Baby Nick Tsigaris — all named after their grandfather per Greek tradition — Nick the Greek satisfies the desire for healthy, flavorful and authentic Greek cuisine in a fast casual environment without compromising quality. Drawing on multigenerational restaurant entrepreneurship and countless visits to Greece, the street-food-inspired menu boasts flavorful gyro meats cooked in-house on a traditional vertical rotisserie, charbroiled souvlaki skewers, zesty sauces, fresh vegetables and authentic Greek treats, including baklava and Greek donuts. In meeting the high demand for Greek street food, Nick the Greek has carved out a sizeable and attractive niche in the ultra-competitive fast casual space — a marketplace differentiator that continues to underpin the brand’s rapid growth. Since 2023, Nick the Greek has nearly doubled its store count and continues to accelerate expansion efforts throughout the nation. Today, guests can find Nick the Greek restaurants in eight states, including Arizona, California, Kansas, Missouri, Nevada, Tennessee, Texas and Utah. By thoughtfully establishing locations in high-visibility downtown metro areas, Nick the Greek has reached large audiences and steadily developed a diverse and devoted fan base. To view the full menu and nutritional information, and to find your nearest Nick the Greek location, go to www.nickthegreek.com . Nick the Greek’s new Santa Clarita restaurant is located at 19335 Plum Canyon Road, Suite A, and can be reached by telephone at (661) 360-3039. articles.title: El Pollo Loco Plans to Grow in New York
articles.titleKo: El Pollo Loco Plans to Grow in New York
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . El Pollo Loco announced its planned entry into New York, including a signed lease for its first restaurant in the region, targeted to open in Queens in mid-2027. The company has agreed to terms for three development agreements for 15 area restaurants over the next five years, and also announced two leadership appointments that strengthen the team supporting El Pollo Loco’s next phase of growth. New York development will be led by one longtime El Pollo Loco franchise partner and two new franchise partners. The expansion marks an important step in El Pollo Loco’s evolution into a national brand and builds on three consecutive quarters of positive same-store sales growth, improved restaurant economics and continued progress against the company’s transformation plan. The agreements also reflect growing consumer interest in protein-forward meals made with quality ingredients. With its signature fire-grilled chicken, El Pollo Loco believes it is uniquely positioned to meet that demand and introduce its differentiated offering to new communities across the country. “New York represents an important milestone for El Pollo Loco and a clear proof point in our disciplined growth strategy,” said Liz Williams, Chief Executive Officer of El Pollo Loco. “We have strengthened our brand and operations, enhanced our business model, and assembled an experienced leadership team to support sustainable expansion. With committed franchise partners and our first New York lease secured, we are excited to introduce the East Coast to the fire-grilled flavor and hospitality that have defined El Pollo Loco for five decades.” El Pollo Loco Appoints Damon Thomas as Chief Operating Officer and Tara Hinkle as Chief Development Officer To support this growth, Damon Thomas has been appointed Chief Operating Officer. Thomas brings extensive experience scaling high-growth restaurant brands across the country and leading operations across large, multi-market systems. His experience includes senior operations leadership roles at Shake Shack and Raising Cane’s, two high-growth restaurant concepts. “El Pollo Loco has a distinctive brand, a strong operating foundation and significant room to grow,” said Thomas. “I look forward to partnering with our company and franchise teams to drive operational excellence, strengthen the guest experience and build the systems that will support the brand as it enters New York and expands into other new markets.” Further support for the brand’s growth trajectory comes from new Chief Development Officer Tara Hinkle. Hinkle joined El Pollo Loco in July 2026 and brings nearly 20 years of experience in franchising, development and operational planning. She most recently served as President and Head of Americas for The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf and previously held franchise strategy and business partnership leadership roles at Taco Bell and Starbucks. “Entering New York is a meaningful step in building a thoughtful, scalable development pipeline for El Pollo Loco,” said Hinkle. “We are working with experienced franchise partners who believe in the brand, known for delicious fire-grilled chicken and fresh, high-quality ingredients, and understand the opportunity in this market. We are focused on choosing the right sites, selecting and supporting strong operators, and growing in a way that creates lasting value for our guests, franchisees and shareholders.” The company plans to share additional location, franchisee and opening details as East Coast development progresses. Starbird is adding a new layer of flavor to its signature crispy chicken this fall with the launch of a new limited-time Honey Chili Crisp lineup. Beginning Sept. 29, guests can enjoy five new menu items featuring the brand’s sweet, sticky and spicy take on chili crisp. Inspired by the bold flavors and distinctive crunch of chili crisp, traditionally made with infused chili oil, peppers, garlic and other aromatics, Starbird incorporates sweetness with honey and ginger, along with the brand’s Nashville Spice for an extra kick. The Honey Chili Crisp lineup is available across tenders, wings, a sandwich, salad and wrap, bringing the dynamic flavor combination to a range of Starbird guests favorites. “We’re always looking at flavors and culinary trends that give us an opportunity to put a distinctive Starbird spin on chicken,” said Greg Levin, chief executive officer of Starbird. “Honey chili crisp brings the perfect mix of sweet heat, crunch and savory flavor, and it pairs naturally with our crispy chicken.” The Honey Chili Crisp lineup includes: Honey Chili Crisp Tenders — Crispy chicken tenders with honey chili crisp, green onion, cilantro and sesame seeds, served with ginger aioli and additional honey chili crisp on the side. Honey Chili Crisp Sandwich — A crispy chicken fillet topped with honey chili crisp, ginger aioli, cucumber, shredded iceberg lettuce and green cabbage, sesame seeds, green onion and cilantro on a toasted brioche bun. Honey Crunch Salad — A romaine and cabbage blend topped with shaved red cabbage, shredded carrot, cucumbers, edamame and sliced crispy chicken tenders, finished with ginger aioli, green onion, chopped cilantro and Honey Crunch Crumble. Served with honey soy dressing on the side. Honey Crunch Wrap — Two crispy chicken tenders and a romaine and cabbage blend wrapped in a grilled flour tortilla with red cabbage, carrot, cucumbers, edamame, green onion, cilantro, ginger aioli, honey soy dressing and Honey Crunch Crumble. Honey Chili Crisp Wings — Chicken wings with honey chili crisp, green onion, cilantro and sesame seeds, served with ginger aioli and additional honey chili crisp on the side. The Honey Chili Crisp launch is the latest addition to Starbird’s ongoing limited-time menu program, giving guests new offerings to explore throughout the year alongside the brand’s core favorites. articles.title: Bonrue Bakery to Make Utah Debut on October 10
articles.titleKo: Bonrue Bakery to Make Utah Debut on October 10
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Bonrue Bakery will make its Utah County debut on Saturday, October 10, at 1545 N. Canyon Road in Provo, bringing its European-style pastries, fresh-baked bread, coffee and sandwiches to a location within walking distance of the Brigham Young University football stadium. The grand opening will kick off at 9 a.m. with a celebratory ribbon-cutting featuring BYU mascot Cosmo, music, and Bonrue founders on hand to welcome the bakery to Provo. The Provo opening represents the next chapter for Bonrue, which has grown its presence in Southern Utah since launching in 2021. Founded by Chris Connors, Li Hsun Sun and the late Chris Herrin, the bakery — formerly Farmstead — is known for its European-inspired pastries, scratch-made breads, specialty coffee and full menu of breakfast and lunch fare, from buttery croissants and its signature kouign amann to sandwiches and fresh salads. Bonrue is also known for its speedy service, with the capability of serving 100+ guests in the space of 10 minutes. “Provo is an exciting next chapter for Bonrue because it gives us the opportunity to bring what we’ve built in Southern Utah to a new community and become part of the daily rhythm here,” said Chris Connors, co-founder of Bonrue Bakery. “We’re looking forward to welcoming students, families, neighbors and visitors through the doors and building something that feels like it belongs in Provo.” The Provo bakery is the first of three Bonrue locations planned for Utah County by the end of 2026. Additional locations are slated for Orem and Spanish Fork, with a Central Baking Kitchen planned in Springville to support the bakery’s growing presence along the Wasatch Front. For fall, the Provo menu will feature seasonal favorites including Pumpkin Pie, Chocolate Chip Pumpkin Bread and Pumpkin Cheesecake, alongside everyday options such as the Roasted Veggie Sandwich and Kale and Ancient Grain Salad. The menu gives guests plenty of choices for a morning pastry and coffee, breakfast, lunch or an afternoon bite. Bonrue Bakery Provo will be open from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday, giving the local community a new spot for morning coffee and pastries, breakfast and lunch throughout the week.
