articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Sueño Coctelería Mexicana, the Snider Plaza destination known for its elevated Mexican cuisine and craft cocktails, is expanding its offerings with weekday lunch and weekend brunch. The new midday menus showcase Sueño’s approach to modern Mexican cuisine, rooted in its in-house masa program and deeply traditional flavors while incorporating refined global techniques. Lunch is now served Monday through Friday from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., while brunch is served Saturday and Sunday from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. A standout lunch option is the Ejecutivo Lunch for $20, featuring white rice and black beans, a choice of one taco or enchilada, and a choice of soup or the Ensalada de la Tierra al Plato. Guests can select from any taco, enchilada or soup currently featured on the menu. Soups and salads include Sopa de Lima, a chicken lime broth with carrot, corn, celery, chayote squash, avocado, tortilla strips and a blend of cheeses; Pozole Verde, featuring a pre-Hispanic poblano and tomatillo chicken broth, white pulled chicken, hominy, green cabbage, red radish, avocado and oregano; Mexican Caesar, with romaine, chorizo, shaved Parmesan, crumbled croutons, cherry tomatoes, red onion and Caesar dressing; Cilantro Pesto Salad, with mixed greens, jicama, green apple, chayote, grapes and avocado; and Bol de Huerta, with ginger-cilantro rice, mixed cabbage, yellow corn, bell peppers, cherry tomatoes, and avocado chipotle aioli with the option to add chicken, sirloin or shrimp for an additional cost. From the Barra de Mariscos Fríos, guests can enjoy Ceviche Fresco, featuring lime-cured flounder, cherry tomatoes, red onion, jicama, cucumber, avocado and cilantro, as well as Tiradito de Camarón, made with shrimp, avocado, red onion, serrano peppers, red radish and cucumber, served with a choice of serrano cucumber or mango-lime chiltepin sauce. Other lunch highlights include Jalisco Birria Tacos, with oven-braised lamb, Jalisco consommé, melted cheese, red onion, cilantro and lime, and Tacos de Camarón, featuring sautéed Gulf shrimp with jalapeño cucumber slaw, tomato relish and chipotle aioli. Enchiladas include Mole Poblano Enchiladas, with chicken, crema Oaxaqueña and queso añejo, and Birria Stack Enchiladas, layered with oven-braised lamb, melted cheese and a sunny-side-up egg. From the Platos Fuertes, guests can choose from dishes such as Seafood Chile Relleno, filled with Pacific shrimp and bay scallops, and Wood-Fired Fajitas a la Parrilla, served with sautéed red onion and peppers and a choice of pollo, sirloin, pork belly or a combination. On weekends, Sueño’s brunch menu leans into regional Mexican breakfast staples with an elevated twist, paired with a bright, agave-forward cocktail selection. Brunch favorites include Chilaquiles, available with salsa verde, chile morita or mole and served with grilled chicken, tomato relish, avocado, mixed cheese, crema Oaxaqueña, queso añejo and sunny-side-up eggs; Huevos Machacados, featuring thinly dried shredded beef, black beans, scrambled eggs and tatemado sauce; Molletes, made with telera bread, huevos con chorizo, pinto beans, tomato relish, melted cheese, avocado and crema Oaxaqueña; and Potato & Chorizo Hash, served with sunny-side-up eggs, black beans, bacon, chile morita sauce and queso añejo. The centerpiece of the brunch bar is the Mimosa Flight, featuring three flavors: tamarind, passion fruit and guava. The cocktail menu also includes the Bloody Mary, made with Weber Ranch vodka and housemade Bloody Mary mix; Bloody Maria, with Espolón Blanco tequila and housemade Bloody Mary mix; Cantarito Mexicano, made with a choice of Racho mezcal or Espolón Blanco, salted grapefruit cordial, agave, citrus, Sangria Señorial and grapefruit soda; and the Zócalo Spritz, featuring Weber Ranch vodka, lemon, agave, honeydew cordial, St-Germain, Midori, soda and prosecco. articles.title: SAN-J Introduces SESAMO Toasted Sesame Oil
articles.titleKo: SAN-J Introduces SESAMO Toasted Sesame Oil
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . SAN-J, the legacy producer of authentic Japanese Tamari Soy Sauce since 1804, announced its expansion into a new product category with the release of SESAMO. This launch marks the brand’s first-ever toasted sesame oil, bringing its centuries-old commitment to Japanese culinary excellence into a premium finishing oil. SESAMO is a 100% pure, Japanese-style sesame oil crafted using the traditional teion baisen (low-temperature roasting) method. By gently roasting carefully selected sesame seeds low and slow before pressing, SAN-J preserves the seeds’ delicate, nutty flavor and rich aroma while minimizing harsh bitterness. The result is a smooth, balanced finish that enhances any dish. Positioned as a clean alternative to industrially refined seed oils, SESAMO is produced without the use of chemical extraction. The gentle pressing method protects the oil’s integrity, retaining nutrients like beneficial omega fatty acids, vitamin E, and sesamol, a powerful antioxidant unique to sesame. SESAMO functions primarily as a finishing oil, packaged in ergonomic squeeze bottles for precise drizzling. SAN-J engineered this versatile seasoning to elevate everyday American cooking, moving far beyond traditional Japanese and Asian cuisine. Home chefs can easily add a gourmet touch to salad dressings, eggs, grain bowls, pasta, pizza, and more. “For generations, SAN-J has crafted authentic Japanese tamari to help people create exceptional meals at home. Expanding into sesame oil felt like a natural evolution of that mission,” shares Takashi Sato, President of SAN-J International. “My grandmother’s family has been in the sesame oil industry for over a century. SESAMO connects my rich family heritage with SAN-J’s promise to deliver high-quality, accessible Asian pantry staples to every kitchen.” SAN-J SESAMO Toasted Sesame Oil is available at Whole Foods Market stores nationwide in 6-oz bottles for $6.79. Haven Hot Chicken, the fast-casual concept known for its high-quality ingredients and five distinct levels of heat, is welcoming the cooler months with limited-time offerings beginning Oct. 1. Guests can dig into the Garlic Parm Tendies, which start with Haven’s signature chicken dipped in mild before being coated with the brand’s garlic parm shake. More than a simple garlic powder and Parmesan combination, the shake features Pecorino Romano, herbs and spices, giving the classic combination a little more character. The new Pesto Ranch, Haven’s house-made ranch blended with fresh basil pesto, offers a creamy option for dipping. The Garlic Parm Tendies are available as a Tendie Duo for $10.99 or a Tendie Trio for $13.99. Guests can also opt for a Tendie Duo Combo for $15.75 or a Tendie Trio Combo for $18.75, with Haven’s traditional Southern sides rounding out each order. “When we develop a new menu item, we want the flavors to complement the chicken rather than compete with it,” said Rob LaTronica, founder and culinary lead for Haven Hot Chicken. “The Garlic Parm Tendies have a richer, more indulgent profile, while the Pesto Ranch cuts through that richness with a bright, fresh flavor. That balance is what makes the combination work.” Haven’s Pumpkin Spice Banana Puddin’ will also be available through Nov. 30, while supplies last. Priced at $5.49 at Connecticut locations and $5.99 at the Franklin, Mass., location, the dessert is whipped with pumpkin spice and pumpkin spice caramel, then topped with cream, more pumpkin spice caramel sauce and a pumpkin spice Nilla wafer brown sugar shake. Whether guests are in the mood for something savory and herby or a sweet finish, Haven’s fall offerings bring together familiar flavors, quality ingredients and generous portions — the kind of food that feels right as the seasons change. articles.title: Molly Baz Joins Sweetgreen as First Chef in Residence
articles.titleKo: Molly Baz Joins Sweetgreen as First Chef in Residence
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Today, sweetgreen announced cookbook author, recipe developer and food personality Molly Baz as its first-ever Chef in Residence. Three new lunch orders, plenty of dill pickles and several executive decisions later, Baz has officially declared that LUNCH MEANS BUSINESS with her new LTO menu. Available at all sweetgreen restaurants from September 29 through November 9, the limited-edition menu features three new craveable orders: Molly’s Big Dill Caesar Wrap, Molly’s Pickle Caesar Sal and Molly’s Double Chick Scoop. “Molly approaches food with curiosity, conviction and a very clear point of view on what makes something delicious. Together, we created a menu that feels distinctly Molly and distinctly sweetgreen, thoughtfully made and anything but basic,” said Zipporah Allen, Chief Commercial Officer at sweetgreen. “Molly is the first of many voices we’ll welcome through our new Chef Residency. Her bold approach to flavor made her a natural choice to kick it off, and these three new delicious lunch orders show what’s possible when we create together.” The menu includes: Molly’s Big Dill Caesar Wrap: Molly’s creamy chicken salad with crisp romaine, fresh dill, Parmesan, pickled red onion, spicy broccoli, garlic breadcrumbs, lemon, Ayoh Dill Pickle Mayo, a pickle spear and Caesar dressing – all wrapped in sweetgreen’s signature olive oil tortilla. Molly’s Pickle Caesar Sal: Molly’s pickle-forward take on a Caesar, featuring her special chicken salad made with Ayoh, fresh dill, Parmesan, pickled red onion, spicy broccoli, garlic breadcrumbs, lemon, Caesar dressing and a pickle spear. Molly’s Double Chick Scoop: A double scoop of Molly’s creamy, dill-forward chicken salad made with Ayoh, with a crisp pickle spear on the side. ”sweetgreen and I go wayyyy back, and I’ve been a fan for years, so returning as its first ever Chef in Residence is a very full-circle moment for me,” said Baz. “I’m on a mission to put an end to boring sandwiches and sad lunches — and that includes wraps! My constant experimentation in the kitchen is how Ayoh was born, and it’s how I landed on this menu of spins on a classic, and highly beloved American food group: the caesar salad. I developed 3 different menu items, all of which feature a big scoop of dilly chicken salad loaded with Dill Pickle Ayoh for maximum flavor. Throw that on my bright, crisp, lemony caesar salad, or pack it into a fresh crunchy cae sal wrap stuffed with a pickle spear and tell me that lunch didn’t just get exponentially more fun and delicious. As a self-proclaimed caesar salad afficionado/expert, I take my caesars extremely seriously, and this one has a LOT to say on the matter.” The collaboration comes to life through Lunch Means Business , a campaign that casts Baz as the ultimate lunchtime boss. Inspired by the larger-than-life executive world of the ‘90s, the creative follows Baz through a workday where every meeting is a tasting, every memo is a menu note and every business decision comes down to one thing: making undeniably delicious food. Because when it comes to taste, Molly is the boss. The campaign will appear across sweetgreen’s social and digital channels, restaurants and out-of-home placements in New York and California. Molly’s limited-edition menu is available from September 29 through November 9 at all sweetgreen restaurants. Customers can order in restaurant, through the sweetgreen app or at sweetgreen.com . With Chili’s gaining new fans like never before and tasting, looking and feeling better than ever, it’s time to give guests a new way to wear their Chili’s love beyond the booth. “Streetwear has dominated mainstream fashion for years, but now we’re starting to see suburban wear have its moment as more consumers are drawn to relaxed, comfort-first fits,” said Jesse Johnson, vice president of marketing at Chili’s. “For decades, Chili’s has shaped suburban culture with our come-as-you-are relaxed atmosphere, so who better to celebrate suburban style with our new merch collection.” Meet the Suburban Collection, where comfort is king and the only real dress code is that you show up dressed. The lineup mixes rugby shirts, hoodies and tees with delightfully specific pieces that could only come from Chili’s, including a crewneck that turns your arms into a Fried Mozz cheese pull and a Baby Backs necklace. articles.title: Chipotle Builds 500 ‘Chipotlanes’ in Less Than 2 Years to Reach 1,500
articles.titleKo: Chipotle Builds 500 ‘Chipotlanes’ in Less Than 2 Years to Reach 1,500
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Chipotle’s pickup lane journey quietly began in late 2018 when it started piloting an earlier generation of what became known as the “Chipotlane.” The following November, at CNBC’s Evolve Summit in Los Angeles, then-CEO Brian Niccol shared a comment hinting fleet-changing potential. He claimed it was taking Chipotle “all of 12 seconds” to deliver food through the format, which was a notable comment for more than the obvious. Chipotle wasn’t a brand that built “drive-thrus.” Fast casual, in general, was historically a category that viewed the channel as a reflection of pre-made food delivered quickly without customization. How could a guest walk the line and see a burrito being crafted while driving outside a restaurant? The same was true of menuboards and the friction of shouting builds through a speaker box. This, too, as digital orders surged inside restaurants. Chipotle, though, viewed the possibility through the lens of customers carrying kiosks in their pockets. Scott Boatwright, the brand’s current chief executive who was COO at the time, was working out of Chipotle’s Denver office when he observed customers heading to a downtown restaurant and ordering through digital channels. But when they showed up, they seemed lost. Should they wait in line? Cut to the front? Boatwright and his team decided to cut a hole in the wall, place a pickup sign over it, and have employees pass bags through the entry point. Sales via the channel popped 50 percent (this store still exists today). In a sense, it’s where the Chipotlane’s true vision began to bubble. First, however, it led to the mobile ordering pickup shelving units so ubiquitous today through the category. Those allowed order-ahead diners to wayfind without disrupting in-store queues. And so, the next question became, could Chipotle solve the same problem for people who didn’t want to get out of their cars? MORE: Chipotle’s Operational Reset is Driving Clear Results The Story of Where Chipotle Got Off Track, and How it Found its Way Back Scott Boatwright Charts the Future of Chipotle as CEO During an office brainstorm, the idea of “a drive-thru, but not a drive-thru,” surfaced. With technology flooding QSR and consumer preference leaving behind the old days of “drive-thru equals food as fuel and nothing but food as fuel,” Chipotle took this kiosk-in-the-pocket notion and developed an approach where guests had to order ahead and pull up for pickup. No ordering at the store. It reconfigured layouts so employees serving the window had to shuffle just a few feet. And as noted, Chipotle tested “Chipotlanes” in five restaurants and saw immediate performance. Early openings hit the market with sales 20 percent higher and 200 basis-points of store-level margin improvement. They also drove 15 percent loftier digital sales mix—a vital lever when you consider the impact third-party delivery burdens on this corner of the business. Come summer 2021, Chipotle had 250 of them. A year later in November, there were 500. Milestone Chipotlane No. 1,000 arrived November 2024, meaning the company took roughly five years to build (or tack on) a fleet of pickup-lane restaurants roughly the size of concepts like Zaxbys, Culver’s, and Carl’s Jr . And, the company announced Tuesday, it needed less than two more years to get another 500 in operation. Chipotle’s 1,500 th Chipotlane arrived in Bradenton, Florida, a Gulf Coast city of about 60,000 that wedges south of Tampa and north of Sarasota along the Manatee River. Chipotle said the restaurant opened amid continued growth across Florida, where it plans to lift the chain’s footprint by about 17 percent this year and create 1,500 jobs. The larger success of “Chipotlane,” though, has quickly brought it deeper into the brand’s development mix. It opened 100 corporate restaurants in Q2 (Chipotle only has licensed stores overseas) and ex

articles.title: Dishoom Borough to Open this October
articles.titleKo: Dishoom Borough to Open this October
articles.originalSummary: Dishoom will open its newest London café this October, bringing its loving homage of Bombay to Borough. Set within the West Wing of the Grade II-listed Hop Exchange the 8,060 sq ft café will span two floors, with spaces for all-day dining and a covered verandah. Ahead of the official opening, Dishoom Borough will welcome its first guests for a soft launch from 12th – 20th October offering 50% off food, sign up here to be the first to hear more. Built in 1867 and designed by R.H. Moore, the Hop Exchange was once a bustling trading floor for London’s hop and brewing industry, and is the last remaining example of the city’s Victorian ‘outcry’ exchanges. Like every Dishoom, Borough will share the team’s deep love for Bombay, its food, history, culture and quirks while paying homage to the Irani cafés that were once part of the fabric of the city. Open from breakfast until late, the new café will bring together Dishoom’s much-loved food, drink and warm hospitality, alongside a new dish and drink created exclusively for Borough. Dishoom Borough’s arrival will be celebrated with a Diwali gathering, with further events to follow. “I’ve wanted to open a restaurant in Borough for well over fifteen years. It’s one of my favourite parts of London, and one of those rare places that still feels completely itself,” said Brian Trollip, Dishoom CEO. “We’ve waited a long time to find a building we really love here, and I’m incredibly excited that we finally have. We think we can create something genuinely special in it, and hopefully add a little more to a part of London that is already unbelievably brilliant.” THE STORYTELLING The opening of every Dishoom café begins with a story: a fictional founding myth set in a particular moment of Bombay’s history, which shapes the character of the café. For Borough, the story harkens back to Bombay’s great Victorian marketplace, Crawford Market. At the cafe’s heart is the democratic spirit of the marketplace: a shared space where people from all walks of life come together. The story also nods to Bombay’s Parsi theatre tradition, known for its lively adaptations of Shakespeare in Gujarati and Urdu.. Hamlet? No, Omelette! Set in Crawford Market during Diwali in 1953, Dishoom Borough’s tale loosely reimagines Romeo and Juliet. Two young people from different corners of the market catch one another’s eye among the stalls and arrange to meet again at a Diwali celebration, only to discover that their families stand on opposite sides of an old divide. Narrated by the owner of an Irani café within the market, the tale leaves the pair asking, ‘What’s in a name?’ It is a story of longing and breaking barriers, set against the colour and commotion of a market where everyone is welcome. THE DESIGN OF DISHOOM BOROUGH The Dishoom team have worked closely with long-time collaborators Macaulay Sinclair on the design of Dishoom Borough. The café draws directly on research carried out across Bombay’s markets, looking particularly to Crawford Market, Fort Market and the much-loved working spice merchant Umrigar Stores. Crawford Market lends the café something of the architecture and grand scale of a civic trading hall, while Fort Market and Umrigar Stores provide the smaller, lived-in details: the particular character of spice-stall shelving, packaging and the daily rhythm of trade. Together, these references ground Borough not in a generic idea of a Bombay market, but in real and particular places. A system of forged metalwork runs throughout the building, with arched screens inspired by Crawford Market framing stairs and entrances, and overhead gantries supporting light fittings. These elements define and connect the different spaces, drawing directly from the ironwork, hanging systems and well-worn architectural language found across Bombay’s markets. articles.title: Introducing Ikona: High-Performance Rest For Everyday Changemakers
articles.titleKo: Introducing Ikona: High-Performance Rest For Everyday Changemakers
articles.originalSummary: Ikano Industry Launches Consumer-Facing Mattress Brand Focused on Restorative Sleep Systems that Support Both Personal Wellbeing and Environmental Responsibility For nearly two decades, Ikano Industry , a core division of Ikano Group, which was founded by Ingvar Kamprad, the founder of IKEA, has quietly powered some of the world’s most trusted sleep brands. Today, the company announced the launch of its first consumer-facing mattress brand: IKONA . Backed by RePoliol®, a pioneering and proprietary technology that delivers high-performance comfort in a more responsible way, IKONA engineers high-performance rest for everyday changemakers with its adaptive mattresses designed to support the body, purpose, and lifestyle of modern consumers. As the largest global mattress supplier for IKEA, Ikano Industry has been producing high-quality sleep solutions since 2007. With IKONA mattresses, Ikano Industry’s decades of expertise are combined with a focus on better materials, circular innovation, and responsible manufacturing across the full value chain. Every IKONA mattress is engineered from the inside out for lasting comfort, support, and performance. “Sleep is increasingly viewed as a performance tool, integral for mental clarity, productivity, emotional resilience, and longevity. Ultimately, better sleep enables people to live and perform fully,” said Silvia Galasso, Chief Sales and Marketing Officer for Ikano Industry. “As we looked at the industry from our supplier perspective, we felt that this promise of better sleep was not being delivered. We recognized we had the expertise to create a mattress platform that would address what consumers both want and deserve: high-performance sleep technology that supports both personal well-being and environmental responsibility and is made accessible through thoughtful pricing.” Sustainability IKONA is engineering a smarter, more circular future for the mattress industry where sustainability is built into the product architecture – not as an afterthought. While sustainability is often defined by materials like organic fabrics and natural fibers, the biggest environmental challenge is the foam inside a mattress. Foam is one of the most difficult materials to recycle. Traditionally it is mechanically downcycled into lower value products or sent to landfills, where it takes hundreds of years to decompose. It is estimated 15 to 18 million mattresses end up in landfills every year. Since 2013, Ikano Industry has been pioneering a technology called RePoliol®, a proprietary innovation that chemically reprocesses foam back into its base ingredient (polyol), allowing it to be used again to produce high-performance comfort. “Real sustainability is about how products are made, how resources are used, and what happens at the end of a product’s life,” said Galasso. “Our RePoliol technology transforms foam waste from both manufacturing and end-of-life mattresses so that we can not only keep materials in use longer but can reduce the amount of waste entering landfills.” IKONA uses other sustainable products in its mattresses including bamboo, a naturally derived fiber chosen for its breathable structure, moisture-wicking performance, and cool-to-the-touch feel; recycled steel coils; sustainable performance yarns from recycled sources that are engineered for durability and reduced resource consumption; and Repes, circular reprocessed fiber technology from internal post-industrial sources. Performance Technology Ikona mattresses combine advanced ergonomic design with personalized support technologies designed to adapt to each body’s unique needs for deeper, more restorative sleep. Developed from decades of award-winning mattress engineering and ergonomic research, IKONA’S IkoMapping technology optimizes weight distribution and supports the body’s natural spinal alignment in any sleep position. It uses five to seven precision support zones, created through IKONA -specific foam contouring or zoned coil constru

articles.title: Sybron Announces B Corp™ Status
articles.titleKo: Sybron Announces B Corp™ Status
articles.originalSummary: Sybron, a leading supplier to some of the largest names in UK hospitality today announces its certification as a B Corporation (B Corp ), making the company the UK’s largest B Corp certified cleaning, hygiene & catering distributor. Certification as a B Corp sees Sybron join a growing movement of companies that are reinventing business for the benefit of all people and our shared planet. The achievement demonstrates that Sybron meets high standards of social and environmental performance, transparency and accountability, alongside a commitment to goals beyond shareholder value. “We are thrilled to announce that Sybron has achieved B Corp certification,” says Sybron’s sales & marketing director, George Mason. “We’re incredibly proud to join the global B Corp community, marking a major milestone in our journey. Achieving B Corp Certification reflects our commitment to building a business that creates a positive impact for our people, our customers, our communities and the planet.” This latest news follows the recent announcement of Sybron’s joint venture with B Corp-certified Lime Sustainable Supplies (LSS), a data-driven supply chain business, to bring unrivalled service, support and sustainability initiatives to the cleaning supplies market. As part of this, Sybron’s group head of ESG, Matt Burtinshaw says: “I very much look forward to leading the business’ sustainability and ESG strategy moving forward, building on the progress already made and helping create even greater measurable impact across the business and wider supply chain.” Sybron is now part of a growing community of over 10,000 businesses globally certified as B Corps. The B Corp community in the UK is the largest and fastest growing in the world, with over 2,600 companies spanning a range of different industries and sizes. “This is about much more than adding a certification to our name,” says George. “It’s about continuing to challenge ourselves, improve the way we do business and make sustainability a bigger part of how we operate every day. This achievement says so much about our loyal and talented team, as well as our clients and the industries we serve.” Verified by B Lab, the not-for-profit behind the B Corp movement, B Corp Certification assesses the entirety of a business’ operations and covers impact areas related to practices around governance, workers, community, the environment and customers. The certification process is rigorous, with companies required to provide evidence on performance while legally embedding their commitment to purpose as well as profit in their company articles. Chris Turner, CEO of B Lab UK, says: “We are delighted to welcome Sybron to the B Corp community. Its commitment to doing business differently will be an inspiration to others and will help spread the notion that success in business is as much about people and planet as it is profit.” Home

articles.titleKo: Mike’s Red Tacos is Taking Birria National

Mike's Red Tacos has sold 350 franchise commitments. Three-unit Mike’s Red Tacos did not begin with a sweeping national plan. It started with a food trend, a friendship, and a suggestion to think bigger. CEO Andrew Feghali had known founder Mike Touma for roughly a decade when Touma approached him with an observation. Birria was gaining traction, and he believed the Mexican specialty could follow a path similar to hot chicken. Feghali brought experience from a franchise portfolio of roughly 100 restaurants across Little Caesars, Jersey Mike’s, and Dave’s Hot Chicken, where he was the first franchisee. The pair spent several weeks visiting birria concepts and sampling the food. Touma initially envisioned selling birria tacos from a trailer stationed outside one of his retail shops. Feghali saw room for a full restaurant. “I said, OK, I think that’s cool. I think you should think a little bit bigger, and open a restaurant. I think you’re onto something interesting here,” Feghali says. Touma later asked Feghali to become his partner. They leased a food truck, and Touma developed the brand, selling tacos on Saturdays in a friend’s parking lot beginning at 11 a.m. and continuing until the food ran out. He eventually opened the first brick-and-mortar restaurant, which landed on Yelp’s list of the top 100 restaurants in the U.S. within a few months. That early recognition offered proof that the concept could attract diners outside its initial following. It also gave the partners a foundation for turning a single restaurant into a franchise opportunity. Feghali then organized the investment group behind the franchise platform, called Four Wall Partners. The idea gained traction faster than its partners anticipated. The company has sold roughly 350 franchise commitments and has several hundred more in its pipeline, Feghali says. That acceleration changed his role. Feghali had been an active board member offering strategic guidance to the corporate team. As the company added employees and awarded large territories, partner and mentor Bill Phelps encouraged him to become CEO. Feghali was initially reluctant. He was content serving as an investor and board member. Conversations with Phelps changed his perspective. He came to see the position as a way to serve the company’s stakeholders and advance Four Wall Partners’ mission of transforming lives across its franchise systems. With close friends joining the corporate team and becoming franchisees, Feghali felt responsible for giving the brand its best chance to succeed and honoring the trust placed in him. The personal stakes were clear. Touma was a longtime family friend who trusted Feghali to assemble the deal, and new hires had left good jobs or declined other opportunities to join the company. “The executive team are folks that have come on board that have left great jobs or passed on other great opportunities because in large part they trusted me,” Feghali says. Operators signed because of the food, category, and business model, he says, but personal trust also influenced their decisions. Taking the CEO job became a way to honor the people committing careers and capital to the venture. “I really feel like it’s more of a service role than something that I had wanted,” Feghali says. “I didn’t have aspirations of becoming CEO of an emerging franchise brand.” Mike’s has its own identity and origin story, though Feghali acknowledges parallels with Dave’s. Each specializes in a segment of a much larger category. Dave’s helped propel Nashville hot chicken into the national conversation. Mike’s sees similar potential for birria within fast-casual Mexican. Feghali says consumer awareness and menu penetration for birria are tracking on a trajectory similar to hot chicken several years ago. articles.title: The Restaurant Industry’s K-Shaped Recovery is Squeezing the Middle
articles.titleKo: The Restaurant Industry’s K-Shaped Recovery is Squeezing the Middle
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . For restaurants in the middle, the answer isn't another gimmick or a sweeping reinvention. The restaurant industry is increasingly splitting in two. At one end, luxury dining continues to command a customer willing to pay for a truly exceptional experience. Michelin-starred restaurants, high-end steakhouses and special-occasion concepts can still thrive because their customers have the means and motivation to spend. At the other end, value wins. McDonald’s and other quick-service brands know exactly what they are selling and to whom. When consumers are watching every dollar, an inexpensive meal with a clear value proposition makes sense. Then there is everyone in the middle. This is where I believe our economy’s K-shaped recovery is becoming particularly painful. Operators face persistently higher labor, food, occupancy and financing costs while serving a customer who is increasingly sensitive to the price of eating out. Many restaurant groups built for a different economic environment are discovering that raising menu prices again isn’t a viable strategy. I’ve spent more than two decades turning around troubled companies across industries, and one lesson holds remarkably consistently no matter what the industry: good businesses rarely collapse because of one catastrophic decision. More often, they suffer death by a thousand cuts. For restaurants in the middle, the answer isn’t another gimmick or a sweeping reinvention. It’s getting relentlessly good at the fundamentals again. Put the Restaurant Back in the Restaurant Business Somewhere along the way, parts of the industry began treating restaurants more like investment theses than operating businesses. I’ve watched sophisticated people approach restaurants with impressive financial models while lacking an appreciation for how extraordinarily difficult these businesses are to operate. You can understand capital structures, growth strategies and unit economics and still not understand what happens inside a restaurant at 7:30 on a Saturday night. Restaurants are operating businesses first. That means understanding food execution, labor, throughput, purchasing, the guest experience and the P&L at the individual restaurant level. It means leaders getting close enough to operations to understand not just what a spreadsheet says is wrong, but why it is wrong. This is especially important for emerging groups with five, 10 or 30 locations. Success can become its own problem. The instincts that allowed a founder to operate two great restaurants don’t automatically become systems capable of supporting 20. Before adding another strategy, platform or layer of management, operators should ask a more basic question: Does this help us sell more meals profitably or operate our restaurants better? If the answer is no, challenge why you’re paying for it. Attack the Slow Killers Restaurant operators understandably focus on their largest expenses. But smaller costs accumulate quietly. Technology is a perfect example. Restaurants have assembled increasingly complicated technology stacks involving POS systems, reservations, delivery, loyalty, scheduling, analytics and countless other services. Individually, each may seem defensible. Collectively, the fees on top of fees can become meaningful. Credit-card fees are another slow killer. Three percent doesn’t sound existential until you consider the amount of revenue passing through cards and the fact that restaurants operate on notoriously thin margins. Then there is SG&A creep. As businesses grow, expenses accumulate because each one can be individually justified. Eventually nobody steps back and asks whether the organization that exists above the restaurants is actually making the restaurants more profitable. Cheese is taking one of its newest concepts nationwide after an initial test in Texas. The family entertainment brand plans to bring Adventure World, its multilevel indoor playground concept, to more than 20 communities across the U.S. in 2026 and 2027. The expansion follows the debut of the first location in Arlington, Texas, in November 2025, which the company says became one of the most successful openings in Chuck E. Cheese history. Adventure World represents a different format for a brand historically built around arcade games, pizza, prizes, and birthday parties. The concept covers active and imaginative play, with locations spanning roughly 12,000 to 18,000 square feet or more. Six U.S. markets are currently scheduled for 2026: West Fargo, North Dakota; Chandler, Arizona; Rochester, New York; Houston; Plano, Texas; and Las Vegas. Another seven have been announced for 2027: Flint, Michigan; MacArthur Park and Hawthorne, California; Crestwood, Illinois; Lakewood, Colorado; Chesterfield, Missouri; and Los Angeles. Additional cities and opening dates will be announced as plans are finalized. Chuck E. Cheese is also taking the concept internationally with three Adventure World locations planned for Jalisco, Mexico. “Families have told us they want a place where kids can move and use their imagination all day, with food and celebrations built right in,” Chuck E. Cheese president Randy Forsythe said in a statement. “That’s exactly what we built. Now we get to share it with kids in a lot more cities.” The expansion builds on an idea Chuck E. Cheese began testing more broadly within its traditional entertainment centers. The company has introduced Trampoline Zones and Superhero Playgrounds as part of its push toward active play. Adventure World takes that strategy and turns it into a standalone destination. The first Adventure World opened November 13 in Arlington as a 12,000-square-foot concept initially geared toward families with children ages 3 to 8. The company said customer feedback following the debut centered on greater interaction with Chuck E. Cheese characters and the freedom for children to create their own adventures. Instead of a traditional arcade-focused experience, Adventure World revolves around themed play areas tied to Chuck E. Cheese characters. Kids can explore Munch’s Cosmic Bounce, a space-themed environment; Bella’s Castle Quest, built around a fairy-tale setting; Jasper’s Bubble Reef, an ocean adventure; and Chuck E.’s Jungle Temple. Locations include climbing structures, slides, ball pits, obstacles, a toddler zone, a large video wall, and a digital live show featuring Chuck E. and friends. Parents can participate in the play areas as well. Food remains part of the model. The Power Up Station, featuring Pasqually and Helen Henny, offers popcorn, nachos, pizza, and wings. Adventure World also retains birthday parties, one of Chuck E. Cheese’s biggest historical business occasions. Packages begin at $99.99 for six children, and the locations can accommodate field trips, playdates, and other group events. Admission is sold at a single price for all-day play instead of a timed format. The Arlington location debuted at $19.99 per child, with two parent admissions included with each child admission. Chuck E. Cheese also brought its Kid Check security system to the concept. Adventure World is part of an effort by parent company CEC Entertainment to expand Chuck E. Cheese beyond its traditional restaurant and arcade model. The company completed a systemwide remodel and brand refresh and has pursued additional extensions across entertainment and licensing. On Tuesday, Sept. 29, Jack’s will bring back its fan-favorite $1 Hamburger Day at all locations, offering its classic hamburger for just $1 from 2 p.m. until close. On Sept. 29, guests can purchase up to five $1 Hamburgers from 2 p.m. until close at all Jack’s locations. The offer is available in-store and through online ordering at order.eatatjacks.com . articles.title: Pizza Hut Reimagines Restaurants as Neighborhood Book Exchanges
articles.titleKo: Pizza Hut Reimagines Restaurants as Neighborhood Book Exchanges
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Each Little Hut Library will come stocked with books and a select quantity of Personal Pan Pizza gift cards while supplies last. The iconic Pizza Hut red roof is popping up somewhere new this fall: your neighborhood . For decades, Pizza Hut’s unmistakable red roofs have been a symbol of pizza nights and good times, and through BOOK IT!, Pizza Hut has spent more than 40 years inspiring a love of reading while rewarding readers with pizza along the way. Now, Pizza Hut is bringing two beloved pieces of its history together with the launch of “Little Hut Libraries,” limited-edition neighborhood book exchanges designed to look like miniature Pizza Hut restaurants and help make books more accessible in communities. Created in collaboration with the Little Free Library non-profit, in celebration of the convergence of National Book Month and National Pizza Month this October, the Little Hut Libraries will bring free books – and a little Pizza Hut nostalgia – directly into neighborhoods across the country. Each Little Hut Library will come stocked with books and a select quantity of Personal Pan Pizza gift cards while supplies last, giving readers the chance to enjoy a free pizza as they participate in the book exchange – a nod to the iconic BOOK IT! experience generations have loved. Little Hut Libraries are available now, and consumers can head to https://littlefreelibrary.org/support/sponsorship-opportunities/pizza-hut-little-free-library/ to apply to receive one for free and bring an iconic red roof and more good reads to their neighborhood. “Pizza Hut has always been about more than pizza; it’s about the memories and moments that happen around it,” said Melissa Friebe, Chief Marketing Officer at Pizza Hut U.S. “Our red roofs and BOOK IT! are two iconic pieces of Pizza Hut history, and we’ve long admired Little Free Library’s mission to bring books to communities across the country. Little Hut Libraries bring our shared passion for reading to life in a uniquely Pizza Hut way, putting more books into communities, all under our beloved red roof.” Pizza Hut and Little Free Library share a longstanding mission to support reading.This partnership builds on Pizza Hut’s more than 40-year commitment through BOOK IT!, which since 1984 has encouraged generations of readers by pairing reading achievements with one of the brand’s most delicious rewards: a Personal Pan Pizza. “We’re grateful to Pizza Hut for bringing its decades-long commitment to young readers to this collaboration,” said Daniel Gumnit, CEO and Executive Director of Little Free Library. “Little Hut Libraries are a fun and nostalgic way to put more books within reach while inviting neighbors to share in the joy of reading. Swig has signed a multi-unit franchise agreement with Summit Management Group to bring the brand to the Pacific Northwest. The 11-unit deal marks Swig’s entry into Washington and extends the brand’s signed franchise agreements across the United States from coast to coast. Swig plans to open its first Washington location by the end of 2026 as the brand continues its nationwide franchise expansion. Franchisees Sean Collins, Jared Collins and Ramey Mills will lead Swig’s development across Washington, bringing extensive experience in multi-unit restaurant and franchise operations across a diverse portfolio of concepts. Through their family-owned franchise group, the team has built a strong track record of developing and operating businesses at scale while maintaining a people-first approach. The group identified Swig as a natural addition to its portfolio because the brand’s strong leadership, community engagement, and values-driven culture closely align with the team’s own approach to business. Swig pioneered the dirty soda category with its premium, customized refreshing beverages. Guests can create a personalized beverage experience by choosing from a variety of bases, including soft drinks from Coke, Pepsi, and Dr Pepper, still and sparkling water, and Swig Energy, then customizing their drinks with flavors, fresh fruits, purees, creams, and other mix-ins. Swig is the Home of the Original Dirty Soda®. “Bringing Swig to Washington represents an important milestone as we continue building our national footprint,” said Alex Dunn, CEO of Swig. “Sean, Jared and Ramey bring an impressive track record as multi-unit operators, and they share our commitment to people, community and creating meaningful experiences for guests. They’re the right team to introduce Swig to Washington and establish a strong foundation for our growth across the state.” Swig designed its franchise model around efficiency and convenience, with a drive-thru-centric footprint that can operate in as little as 800–850 square feet. The concept eliminates the need for complex kitchen infrastructure, helping operators streamline labor, reduce build-out costs and efficiently scale across multiple locations. “Washington opens an important new chapter for Swig as we continue expanding our presence across the country,” said Todd Smith, President of Swig. “This 11-unit commitment allows us to establish meaningful scale from the start while introducing the Original Dirty Soda® experience to communities throughout the region. The Pacific Northwest represents a natural next step for Swig, and we see significant opportunity to build on this momentum throughout the region.” Swig opened its first location in St. George, Utah, in 2010 and has since grown from a single drive-thru concept into a nationally expanding brand with nearly 170 locations across 17 states. Its simple, scalable model, deeply loyal customer base, and highly personalized beverage experience continue to drive the brand’s growth across generations. Swig continues to seek qualified multi-unit operators to support its national expansion. Ideal franchise candidates bring proven experience in restaurant operations and a commitment to delivering exceptional guest experiences at scale. Frederick has been part of Original ChopShop’s leadership team for a decade, most recently serving as Chief Operating Officer. In that role, he helped shape the company’s operations, culture and restaurant teams. As CEO, Frederick will lead the company as it brings its Feel Good Food experience to even more communities. “What started as three Shops in Phoenix is now 30 locations across four markets, and I think ChopShop’s best days are still ahead,” said Jason Morgan, outgoing CEO of Original ChopShop. “I’m proud of everything our team has built over the last 10 years, and I’m excited about where Kyle will take it. I’ll be in his corner as an advisor, and I’m ready to watch this team continue to do big things.” During his tenure as CEO, Morgan guided Original ChopShop through significant growth and established the operational and cultural foundation that continues to support the brand today. Before joining Original ChopShop in 2016, Frederick held leadership roles at Zoës Kitchen. He is a graduate of Louisiana State University and was named a 2022 Top 40 Under 40 honoree by the Dallas Business Journal. “The last 10 years proved what Original ChopShop can be. The next 10 are about showing how far we can take it,” said Frederick. “I’m grateful to Jason for his leadership and for building such a strong foundation. We’ll keep investing in our people, our restaurants and the communities we serve, while bringing Feel Good Food to even more guests. “ The leadership transition comes as Original ChopShop continues to grow under Mac Haik Enterprises, which acquired all outstanding interest in the company. articles.originalSummary: 육우자조금관리위원회(위원장 조재성, 이하 육우자조금)가 ‘제8회 전국 대학생 육우요리대회(이하, 전국대학생 육우요리대회)’를 오는 11월 8일 개최에 맞춰 참가자를 모집한다.전국대학생 육우요리대회는 육우자조금이 주최·주관하고 농림축산식품부가 후원하는 행사로 ‘우리육우를 활용한 건강한 육우 레시피’를 주제로 맛과 영양이 우수한 국내산 소고기 우리육우의 우수성을 널리 알리고 미래 외식 산업을 이끌어갈 대학생들의 참신하고 실용적인 레시피를 발굴하기 위해 기획됐다.참가 대상은 전국 외식 산업 및 식품 관련학과 대학생으로 개인(1인 1팀)

articles.title: Rock N Roll Sushi Appoints Rick Gestring CEO
articles.titleKo: Rock N Roll Sushi Appoints Rick Gestring CEO
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Rock N Roll Sushi has appointed restaurant and franchise executive Rick Gestring as its next Chief Executive Officer. Gestring will lead the 80-unit concept into its next phase of growth, with a focus on strengthening the brand, supporting franchisee success and positioning Rock N Roll Sushi for continued expansion. Gestring brings extensive restaurant and franchise leadership experience to the role. Most recently, he served as Brand Officer for Tasty Restaurant Group, where he led the KFC and Taco Bell restaurant portfolio. Previously, he was Senior Vice President of franchise operations for Honey Baked Ham and Chief Restaurant Officer at Blaze Pizza. His background also includes leadership roles with Dunkin’, Arby’s, Starbucks, Peet’s Coffee and Taco Bell. “Rock N Roll Sushi’s unique American-style sushi brand positioning, coupled with an electrifying restaurant experience and creative menu offerings, have created a tremendously loyal fan following.”, said Gestring. “I look forward to leading the brand, in collaboration with our incredible franchisees and support teams, as together we turn up the volume on growth and expansion.” As Gestring steps into the CEO role, his focus will be on building upon Rock N Roll Sushi’s established foundation while identifying opportunities to strengthen restaurant operational performance, support franchisees, and expand the brand’s reach. Now at 80 locations, Rock N Roll Sushi enters its next chapter with significant momentum and a continued focus on sustainable franchise growth. Gestring succeeds Craig LeMieux, who has served as CEO since 2023 and helped guide Rock N Roll Sushi through a period of significant expansion. The two have been working closely together as part of a planned leadership transition to ensure continuity as the brand enters its next phase of growth. “When I joined Rock N Roll Sushi, I saw an opportunity to lead a truly distinctive brand,” said LeMieux. “I’m proud of what our team and franchise partners have accomplished, and I know Rick understands what makes this brand and its franchise community special. I’m looking forward to seeing where he takes Rock N Roll Sushi next.” “Rick brings a valuable combination of restaurant expertise, franchise knowledge and a fresh perspective to Rock N Roll Sushi,” said Sam Osborne, Chairman of the Board of Rock N Roll Sushi. “The board is confident in his ability to build on the foundation that has been established while identifying new opportunities to strengthen the brand, support our franchise partners and position Rock N Roll Sushi for long-term growth.” The post Rock N Roll Sushi Appoints Rick Gestring CEO appeared first on FSR magazine .

articles.title: SusieCakes Partnering with Susan G. Komen During Breast Cancer Awareness Month
articles.titleKo: SusieCakes Partnering with Susan G. Komen During Breast Cancer Awareness Month
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . SusieCakes is partnering with Susan G. Komen, a leading organization dedicated to fighting breast cancer and advancing a cure, to recognize Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Throughout October, SusieCakes will offer a collection of limited-edition cakes and cupcakes, with a minimum donation of $10,000 to Susan G. Komen. The partnership holds special significance for SusieCakes founder and owner Susan Sarich, a two-time breast cancer survivor. With women making up approximately 80% of the SusieCakes team, the impact of breast cancer is a cause that hits especially close to home for Sarich and the company. “One in eight women in the United States will confront a breast cancer diagnosis in their lifetime, and I am that one,” said Sarich. “But breast cancer isn’t just a statistic; it’s a harsh reality that has touched my life as a two time survivor and has touched the lives of countless women, men, and families nationwide. Its impact extends beyond those diagnosed and affects their friends, families, caregivers, and communities at large. At SusieCakes, where 80% of our team members are female, these stats are significant, and they serve as a stark reminder of the pressing need to double down on our efforts towards finding a cure.” The limited-edition treat collection will run from October 1 through October 31, with SusieCakes offering treats inspired by the iconic pink breast cancer ribbon, giving customers a sweet way to support Komen’s mission. The collaboration will offer four special treats, each benefiting the nonprofit. The SusieCakes x Komen Cupcake will donate $1 from the sale of each cupcake to Komen. Customers can choose between vanilla or chocolate cupcakes topped with natural pink vanilla buttercream and finished with natural pink sugar. The SusieCakes x Komen Ribbon Cupcake 4-Box includes two vanilla and two chocolate cupcakes topped with natural pink buttercream, decorated with a ribbon stencil and bordered with natural pink sugar. SusieCakes will donate $4 from the sale of each four-box. The SusieCakes x Komen Ribbon Flourless Cupcake 4-Box offers a flourless option featuring four chocolate cupcakes topped with natural pink buttercream, decorated with a ribbon stencil and bordered with natural pink sugar. SusieCakes will also donate $4 from the sale of each four-box. Also offered is the SusieCakes x Susan G. Komen Cake, a 6-inch vanilla cake finished with pink buttercream and customizable cake writing. SusieCakes will donate $5 from the sale of every cake to Susan G. Komen throughout the month of October. Each cake also includes a complimentary candle and matchbox. The Komen Cake will be available through October 31 and is offered exclusively through nationwide shipping, making it available to customers across the country. It will not be sold in SusieCakes bakeries and is available while supplies last. Sarich says, “Organizations like Susan G. Komen have been at the forefront of driving progress. Their tireless dedication to funding research, providing support, and advocating for those affected by breast cancer is nothing short of inspiring. For me, supporting Susan G. Komen is more than a charitable endeavor, it’s a personal mission and I know together, we can make days better and together we can make a difference, creating a world where breast cancer is no longer a looming threat.” The SusieCakes x Susan G. Komen collection will be available beginning October 1 through October 31, and each cupcake box will require 24 hours’ notice. The post SusieCakes Partnering with Susan G. Komen During Breast Cancer Awareness Month appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: HTeaO Launching Two New Chai Lattes for Limited Time
articles.titleKo: HTeaO Launching Two New Chai Lattes for Limited Time
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . HTeaO, the nation’s leading iced tea franchise, is giving one of its most beloved flavors a new twist this fall with the launch of two limited-time chai lattes. Beginning October 7, guests can enjoy the new Spiced Cookie Crumble Chai Latte and Toasted Coconut Chai Latte, available hot or iced at participating HTeaO locations for a limited time. Inspired by HTeaO’s popular Texas Chai, the new beverages bring warm, comforting flavors to the menu just in time for fall. The Spiced Cookie Crumble Chai Latte pairs Texas Chai with a dollop of cookie crumble for a sweet, spiced take on the classic, while the Toasted Coconut Chai Latte layers Texas Chai with notes of toasty coconut for a smooth seasonal sip. “Texas Chai has become a favorite among our guests, so we wanted to have a little fun with it and give them two completely new ways to enjoy a flavor they already love,” said Jennifer Montoya, Director of Operations Excellence. “Spiced Cookie Crumble brings that cozy, nostalgic flavor you want this time of year, while Toasted Coconut offers something a little unexpected. Whether you order them hot or iced, both feel like the perfect way to welcome fall at HTeaO.” The new chai lattes can be ordered hot in 12-, 16- and 20-ounce sizes, starting at $4.99, or iced in 24- and 32-ounce sizes, starting at $6.45. Pricing is as follows: 12-ounce hot, $4.99; 16-ounce hot, $5.59; 20-ounce hot, $5.99; 24-ounce iced, $6.45; and 32-ounce iced, $7.25. Known for its wide selection of freshly brewed iced teas, HTeaO offers a beverage experience built around flavor, customization and quality. In addition to its signature sweetened and unsweetened teas, the brand continues to expand its menu with seasonal beverages and limited-time flavors that give guests new ways to enjoy HTeaO throughout the year. The Spiced Cookie Crumble Chai Latte and Toasted Coconut Chai Latte will be available beginning October 7 at participating HTeaO locations for a limited time. The post HTeaO Launching Two New Chai Lattes for Limited Time appeared first on QSR Magazine .

articles.title: MEZŌ Mediterranean and Dedham House of Pizza Name Carlos Vasquez Head Chef and GM
articles.titleKo: MEZŌ Mediterranean and Dedham House of Pizza Name Carlos Vasquez Head Chef and GM
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Carlos Vasquez’s career has taken him through a diverse range of culinary environments. MEZŌ Mediterranean and Dedham House of Pizza have announced the appointment of Carlos Vasquez as Head Chef and General Manager, bringing more than a decade of culinary and restaurant experience spanning Venezuela, Miami, Dallas and Greater Boston to the two Dedham establishments. Vasquez’s career has taken him through a diverse range of culinary environments, from baking and pastry and Japanese-Latin cuisine to Peruvian cuisine, luxury hospitality, large-scale banquets, high-volume restaurant operations and French-inspired hospitality. In his new role, he will oversee culinary operations, kitchen management, menu execution and day-to-day restaurant operations at both MEZŌ Mediterranean and Dedham House of Pizza. Originally from Venezuela, Vasquez began his culinary training at the European Institute of Bread and started baking professionally in 2015 at Panamorarte. His early experience in baking and pastry established a foundation in technique, preparation and discipline while deepening his interest in food and culinary traditions. Vasquez moved to the United States in 2017 at age 28, leaving Venezuela amid the country’s ongoing political and economic crisis and the political persecution he and others were experiencing. He continued his culinary development in South Florida, where he quickly became immersed in a wide range of professional kitchens. From 2017 to 2019, Vasquez worked at Sushi Kong in Miami, a Japanese-fusion restaurant incorporating Latin influences, where he advanced to Chef de Cuisine. He went on to work at La Mar by Gastón Acurio at the Mandarin Oriental Miami under one of South Florida’s leading chefs, Executive Chef Diego Oka, gaining experience in Peruvian cuisine and luxury hospitality. His Miami career also included work at Novecento in Brickell, where he focused on grill and sauté before being selected and trained for the opening team of the restaurant’s larger Doral location. His South Florida experience also included banquet operations at Hilton Miami Downtown and large-scale luxury event catering. In November 2018, he participated in the culinary production of the FIU Torch Awards alongside chefs Dewey LoSasso and Mary Rohan as part of the Bill Hansen Catering & Event Production team. He also participated in culinary programming surrounding Art Basel Miami Beach, working in collaborative environments alongside chefs including James Beard Foundation Award recipient Michelle Bernstein. Vasquez later joined Little Brittany Crêperie as Sous Chef, further expanding his experience in French-inspired hospitality. Vasquez then moved to Dallas, where he joined Pappadeaux Seafood Kitchen, part of the Pappas Restaurants family. He considers the experience a particularly important period of professional training and growth, working within a highly structured, high-volume operation that strengthened his skills in organization, speed, consistency, discipline, workflow and kitchen leadership. In 2024, Vasquez moved to Massachusetts with his wife and family, seeking a community with strong educational opportunities for his three sons. He continued his culinary career in Greater Boston before joining MEZŌ Mediterranean and Dedham House of Pizza. “Carlos brings an incredible breadth of experience to our restaurants,” said George Panagopoulos, owner and executive chef of MEZŌ Mediterranean and Dedham House of Pizza. “His background across so many different cuisines and restaurant environments gives him a unique perspective, but what stood out most was his passion for food, his leadership in the kitchen and his commitment to creating a great experience for guests. articles.title: Multi-Brand Operator Rise Harvest Signs Lease to Open Jeff’s’ Bagel Run in Midvale, Utah
articles.titleKo: Multi-Brand Operator Rise Harvest Signs Lease to Open Jeff’s’ Bagel Run in Midvale, Utah
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Rise Harvest, the Utah-based multi-brand franchise holding company, has signed a lease to open its first Jeff’s Bagel Run at 744 W Blue Vista Ln in the View 72 shopping center in Midvale, Utah. The location is expected to open by the end of 2026 and will be the first Jeff’s Bagel Run operating in the state of Utah. RiseHarvest JBR Midvale PressRe… Jeff’s Bagel Run is known for its scratch-made hot bagels, freshly whipped spreads, and craft beverages, with every bagel made fresh in-shop daily. The Midvale location will bring 20 to 30 new jobs to the community, spanning full-time and part-time positions across all levels of restaurant operations. The opening follows Rise Harvest’s seven-unit area development agreement with Jeff’s Bagel Run, which grants the company exclusive development rights across Salt Lake, Davis, and Weber counties. Rise Harvest intends to develop a minimum of 15 Jeff’s Bagel Run locations across the territory. “Jeff’s Bagel Run fills a real gap in the Utah market,” said Jacob Webb, Founder and CEO of Rise Harvest. “There’s nothing else like it here. Our bagels are made from scratch every single day, right in the shop. We’ve been building toward this opening for some time, and Midvale is the right place to introduce the brand to Utah.” “Opening a first location in a new market is one of the most operationally demanding things a franchise company does,” said April Miller, Chief Operating Officer of Rise Harvest. “Our team has put in the preparation to execute this well and deliver a great guest experience right out of the gate. We are proud to bring something new to this community.” Rise Harvest currently operates 28 locations across Marco’s Pizza, Tropical Smoothie Cafe, and Jeff’s Bagel Run, with 46 franchise agreements signed and additional units in active development across the Mountain West. articles.title: The Flying Biscuit Café Signs Franchise Agreement in Richmond, Virginia
articles.titleKo: The Flying Biscuit Café Signs Franchise Agreement in Richmond, Virginia
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . The Flying Biscuit Café has signed a franchise agreement with Nitant Patel, who will bring the Atlanta-born all-day breakfast and brunch brand to Richmond, Va. The agreement covers one café and marks the brand’s first location in Virginia and its first in the Richmond market. Site selection is underway; the address, opening date and hiring details will be announced once a lease is signed. Nitant Patel is joined by franchise partners Niraj Patel and Nimesh Patel. The three are family and have operated restaurant and retail businesses in Virginia and North Carolina, including convenience stores with delis — a business that put Nitant Patel behind a morning counter running food service, hiring and customer service before he looked at a restaurant of his own. He holds a bachelor’s degree in accounting. He had not eaten at a Flying Biscuit before Niraj Patel brought the brand to him; the group looked at the business model and the brand’s three decades in operation before signing. The Richmond region is one of the fastest-growing markets in Virginia. The Richmond metropolitan statistical area grew from 1,186,501 residents in 2010 to 1,314,434 in the 2020 census, and the U.S. Census Bureau estimated it at 1,349,732 in 2023. Growth has run heaviest in the surrounding counties — Chesterfield, Hanover and Goochland — where new rooftops have outpaced the area’s sit-down breakfast and brunch options. “We’re the first Flying Biscuit in this market, so we get to be a new face here,” said Nitant Patel, franchise partner. “What we want is to leave a lasting impression and make a lot of friends out of it. Richmond has all kinds of people from all kinds of backgrounds, and every one of them should feel looked after when they walk in.” Flying Biscuit serves breakfast, brunch and lunch, with cafés closing in the afternoon. The menu runs to Southern-inspired takes on brunch standards — stuffed French toast, the brand’s famous shrimp and grits, hearty omelets, vegan scrambles, burgers and wraps. The Richmond café will include a full bar, serving the brand’s brunch-forward cocktails alongside the breakfast and lunch menu. “Virginia has been the logical next step north as our Carolina cafés have filled in, and Richmond is where we wanted to start,” said Andrew Scherzer, partner and director of franchise development, Flying Biscuit Franchising. “The Patels have been running restaurant and retail businesses in Virginia and North Carolina for years. They know the market, and they understand a business that opens early and closes in the afternoon — that is a different operation from a dinner house, and they walked in already knowing the difference.” This first café is the extent of the signed agreement. The partners have said they would like to sign for a second café once the first is open, and hope to develop three to five over time. The Richmond agreement follows a run of new-market activity. Flying Biscuit signed its first Missouri lease in the St. Louis metro in August, and added franchise agreements in Nashville, the Tri-Cities in northeast Tennessee and Palm Beach County, Fla. Its newest café opened in downtown Knoxville on Sept. 12. Prospective franchisees can review available markets and development requirements, and start a conversation with the development team, at flyingbiscuitfranchising.com. Pretzelmaker, the beloved pretzel chain owned by FAT Brands Inc. , is giving snack time a spicy upgrade. Now through Dec. 31, the brand is teaming up with Frank’s RedHot to introduce two new Nashville Hot Pretzel Bites, combining the unmistakable, trending flavor of Nashville Hot with Pretzelmaker’s fresh-baked Pretzel Bites for the ultimate snack made for dipping, sharing, and enjoying all season long. The new Frank’s RedHot Nashville Hot Pretzel Bites feature Pretzelmaker’s signature Pretzel Bites tossed in Frank’s RedHot Nashville Hot seasoning for a spicy, zesty kick. For an extra satisfying bite, Frank’s RedHot Nashville Hot Mozzarella Stuffed Pretzel Bites feature warm Pretzel Bites stuffed with mozzarella cheese, baked to perfection and tossed in the same fiery Nashville Hot seasoning. Pretzelmaker is also welcoming the highly anticipated return of its Creamy Jalapeño Ranch , made with Hidden Valley Ranch. The savory dipping sauce helps balance the intense heat of Nashville Hot while adding a flavorful jalapeño kick of its own, making it an ideal pairing for both new Pretzel Bites. “Nashville Hot has quickly become a standout flavor among consumers looking for craveable heat, and we are excited to bring that spice to Pretzelmaker in a way that is uniquely ours,” said Katie Thoms, Vice President of Marketing for Pretzelmaker. “With our newFrank’s RedHot Nashville Hot creations,we are putting a snackable spin on this popular flavor while bringing back our Creamy Jalapeño Ranch to give our guests even more ways to customize every bite.” Since getting its start in 1991 as a single pretzel stand, fans have loved snacking on Pretzelmaker’s fresh-baked, hand-rolled Pretzel Bites and sipping on lemonade. articles.title: Bubbakoo’s Burritos Opening in Bethlehem
articles.titleKo: Bubbakoo’s Burritos Opening in Bethlehem
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . Bubbakoo’s Burritos, the award-winning Mexican-fusion concept, is opening its newest location in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on Tuesday, Sept. 29. Conveniently located at 3926 Nazareth Pike in Bethlehem Square, a key shopping destination on the city’s northside, the new restaurant is locally owned and operated by Deepak and Sarah Patil, who look forward to bringing Bubbakoo’s signature customizable menu and bold flavors to the Lehigh Valley area. To celebrate its arrival in the community, the first 50 guests to make a qualifying purchase on opening day will receive a year’s supply of free burritos, with one free burrito per month for a year. Guests can also take advantage of Bubbakoo’s fall menu additions, including Fried Cauliflower, available as both a starter and protein option, and Apple Pie Egg Rolls. “Bubbakoo’s appealed to us because it puts a unique spin on the customizable fast-casual experience, with a wide variety of flavors and ingredients that give guests the freedom to make every meal their own,” said Deepak Patil. “We were also drawn to how much the brand values being part of the communities it serves. Bethlehem has such a great mix of families, students and local businesses, and we look forward to getting involved with local schools, youth programs and organizations and creating a place where the community feels welcome.” The Patils selected Bethlehem for its diverse population of growing families, local businesses, commuters and students, with Lehigh University, Moravian University and Northampton Community College all nearby. They envision the restaurant as a destination for everything from family dinners and quick lunches to student gatherings and plan to build relationships throughout the community through local sponsorships and partnerships. “Pennsylvania has been an important part of Bubbakoo’s growth, and we’re proud to continue building our presence in the state with Deepak and Sarah,” said Chris Ives, CEO of Bubbakoo’s Burritos. “Bethlehem is the type of community where we believe Bubbakoo’s can really connect with guests, and Deepak and Sarah share our commitment to becoming an active part of the neighborhoods we serve. We look forward to supporting them as they introduce the brand to even more guests across the Lehigh Valley.” Over the past 17 years, Bubbakoo’s Burritos has become a fan favorite for its unique menu, superb customer service, and welcoming dining environment. Living up to its promise to “create something different,” the brand offers more than 12 signature flavors that fuel its ever-evolving lineup, from the Papi Hibachi steak and shrimp Burrito to the Crispy Buffalo Chicken Quesadilla, Nashville Hot Crispy Chicken Burrito, California Steakhouse Burrito, and more. Guests are encouraged to blend creativity with the fresh, high-quality ingredients Bubbakoo’s has to offer. Bubbakoo’s Burritos has established a prominent U.S. presence across the country, creating a dedicated legion of fans. Since its inception in 2008, Bubbakoo’s has grown from its Jersey Shore roots to more than 140 locations across 17 states. The brand has been recognized among Franchise Times’ Top 40 Smartest-Growing Franchises, Entrepreneur’s Franchise 500®, QSR Magazine’s Top 50 Contenders, and the Inc. 5000 list of the fastest-growing private companies in America. articles.title: Popeyes Introduces New Honey Chicken Biscuit
articles.titleKo: Popeyes Introduces New Honey Chicken Biscuit
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on QSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily QSR AM Jolt . As a Real Louisiana Kitchen, Popeyes doesn’t just serve bold flavor, it’s the authority on it. Popeyes’ culinary team is always looking for new ways to bring bold flavors together, and they saw an opportunity to combine some of the menu’s most beloved staples in an entirely new way. It’s no surprise fans have long found their own ways to combine the brand’s signature chicken and biscuits with honey on social media; but now, Popeyes is putting its culinary expertise behind that same craving, transforming it into their newest sandwich innovation, perfect for any meal of the day, available beginning September 28. The Honey Chicken Biscuit is a simple, yet bold innovation: THAT Chicken from Popeyes on a larger version of our iconic buttermilk biscuit, paired with two sachets of sweet honey sauce, all for just $5. A recipe that could only come from a Real Louisiana Kitchen. This sandwich brings Popeyes bold flavor and culinary credentials into a delicious, handheld bite, balancing crunchy and soft, savory and sweet, in a combination true to the brand’s Louisiana roots. This is signature menu innovation at its heart, proof that some of the biggest ideas come from reimagining what’s already cooking in our kitchens. “At Popeyes, quality and bold flavor guide everything we do, and we’re always looking for new ways to bring our most iconic items together,” said Matt Rubin, Popeyes Chief Marketing Officer. “The Honey Chicken Biscuit is exactly that: our craveable chicken, our iconic buttermilk biscuit, and sweet honey sauce, crafted into one new sandwich. It’s simple, it’s unmistakably Popeyes, and it shows the kind of culinary care that turns flavors people already love into something entirely new.” The Honey Chicken Biscuit arrives on the heels of “THAT Chicken from Popeyes,” the brand’s new national campaign celebrating the bold flavor, handcrafted preparation and unmistakable generosity that have made Popeyes chicken iconic for more than 50 years. Popeyes isn’t just celebrating THAT Chicken from Popeyes, they’re finding even more craveable ways to serve it to their loyal guests. The new Honey Chicken Biscuit will be available at participating Popeyes restaurants, the Popeyes app, and Popeyes.com nationwide beginning September 28 for $5. articles.title: Cheesecake Factory and Flower Child Continue to Compete with ‘Everybody and Nobody’
articles.titleKo: Cheesecake Factory and Flower Child Continue to Compete with ‘Everybody and Nobody’
articles.originalSummary: This story was originally published on FSR. To receive daily news and insights, subscribe to our free daily FS Insider . Cheesecake Factory EVP and CFO Matthew Clark is no stranger to questions about Flower Child. “Many, many” have poured in from the investor community, he said, asking about a brand that joined the polished casual giant’s portfolio seven years ago when it purchased North Italia and Fox Restaurant Concepts (where Flower Child resided) for about $308 million. Cheesecake Factory originally bought in three years earlier, in 2016, when it grabbed a minority stake under a deal that allowed it to later acquire full ownership. North Italia touted nine stores. Flower Child—just two years old at the time—had five. Today, there are 50 of the Italian casual concept and 40 of the fast casual (there are 220 or so Cheesecake Factory locations). As is often the case on Wall Street, Clark said, investors understand but probably underappreciate the emerging chain’s path. Flower Child will expand at a pace that makes sense for the brand, he explained, whether it concerns site selection, labor, or just making sure it has the right management unit-by-unit. “And so, I think, we’re continuously reeducating,” Clark said during the Barclays Annual Global Consumer Staples Conference. “Wall Street just loves growth. And we want to make sure that it’s quality growth.” It is understandable, however, why investors would wonder if Cheesecake Factory is going to press the pedal. Flower Child posted same-store sales gains of 13 percent last quarter (17 percent two-year stack). Roughly 8 points flowed from traffic, with 2.5 percent pricing and an added check lift from catering. That spiked annualized average-unit volumes to $5.4 million alongside adjusted mature store-level margins of 20.1 percent. A few older restaurants posted $6.5 million to $7 million. For perspective, if Flower Child was one of the top 50 grossing QSRs in the country ( per the QSR 50 ) by systemwide sales, its AUV would slot fourth, ahead of McDonald’s ($4.088 million) and behind In-N-Out ($6.032 million). Shake Shack follows at $4.048 million. Flower Child’s AUV would also rank second on QSR’s Contenders list , trailing Portillo’s ($8.5 million) and fronting Jollibee ($4.990). The $5.4 million sailed fellow publicly traded fast casual sweetgreen ($2.677 million). Flower Child is a vibe, and one that appeals to families, adults, and everything in between. Still, Flower Child is hardly sitting idle. Clark said the company aims to step into the 20–25 percent growth range. For the full fiscal year, seven are expected to open, as well as five to six Cheesecake Factory boxes, six to seven North Italias, and as many as seven of FRC’s other concepts, like The Henry (a recent opening, in Chicago suburb Wilmette, pushed $10 million Year 1 AUVs at weekly sales of $200,000). Clark said Flower Child boasts the best unit economics of Cheesecake Factory’s suite. It’s about 33 percent cash-on-cash returns. It also has the largest total addressable market given it fits any geography, smaller or larger cities, and more. Additionally, the company knows when it densifies, as it’s done in Dallas and Phoenix, performance increases alongside awareness. It’s a brand uplifting from growth rather than being concerned about sales transfer. And why has Flower Child carved such a defined counter-service niche? Clark said the company internally calls it, “The Cheesecake Factory fast casual.” It’s not assembly line.
